absence_ignore.$comment: Spec 68 §7.5 rule 7a (Spec 69 M-54 note): absence needs no by-law unit for the target. Operator chat 2026-10-20 batch B CHAT-8 (Spec 69a M-237): a unit that carries the target only for a lawfully existing building (its condition or lot_conditions name one of lot_conditions), or only for an ancillary building, a garden or laneway suite (every application.building_types entry in building_types), or only for an accessory structure (accessory_structure_uses: a vocab.accessory_structure_use in application.uses, M-159(2)) does not block absence for a new principal building. Rule 7a v2 (operator approved 2026-10-20, Spec 69a M-240): absence is decided per (zone, building type, target): a DEFINE unit with no statement for the target (define_without_statement) and a unit whose building_types exclude the lot's type and its parent (other_building_types) do not count either. Q-KG3 (HELD): a unit whose lot condition is KNOWN FALSE for the lot (a token in known_false_lot_conditions whose flag is false) does not count either, so a townhouse off a major street, whose only building-length unit is the major-street one, is unregulated by absence; an UNKNOWN condition still blocks (condition_unknown).

article_application.$comment: Spec 69a M-219 (applies M-159): an Article's own application regulation. x.40.1(1) of each residential zone: the Article's regulations "apply to buildings or structures in the <zone> zone, other than ancillary buildings or structures which are subject to Article 10.5.60". A unit of that Article never answers for these building types (a garden or laneway suite is in an ancillary building, 150.7.20.1 / 150.8.20.1); its own chapter (150.7 / 150.8, 10.5.60) does. 10.5.40.1(1) is the same form for Article 10.5.40; 10.5.60.1(1) and R's 10.10.60.1(1) are the converse ("apply to ancillary buildings or structures"), so they list included_building_types instead. A unit of these Articles keyed on a principal type (e.g. 10.5.60.70(1)(C), 10.10.60.70(1)(C): "a lot with a detached houseplex") names the other building on the lot — a cross-structure condition this one-structure evaluation does not model (M-177(1), P2-10).

M-288 (lane B, 2026-10-21-page-4d-b#CHAT-38.F-4D-15, consequence of M-280): the two 150.8.60.60(3) laneway-suite platform-height units name no building type (the platform is the one permitted under (2) for a laneway suite), M-314 (CHAT-49, 2026-10-21-batch-o#CHAT-49): the same pattern for the type-less side-yard units of exceptions 117, 199, 245, 256, 258, 287, 155 (E) and 340 (C); units that name a building type (a garage) are left alone. M-288: with platform_height_m and platform_above_access_floor_m now platform element targets they are set aside for the other suite and ancillary types.

zone_category_chapter.$comment: Spec 69a M-159 (1): a base unit from one of these chapters whose application.zones is empty loads only on a lot whose zone is in its category's zones. A chapter not listed keeps today's behaviour. calculation_handling.description: Scope statement: the regulations of Section 10.10 apply to all lands, uses, buildings and structures in the R zone. It sets no numeric value; it routes R-zone lots to the Section 10.10 regulations.

calculation_handling.description: Lists the uses permitted in the R zone only subject to the numbered conditions in Clause 10.10.20.100; the conditions themselves are keyed under 10.10.20.100.

calculation_handling.description: Permission: in the R zone a dwelling unit is permitted in a detached house. Evaluated from the lot's zone and the chosen building type.
Permission: in the R zone a dwelling unit is permitted in a semi detached house. Evaluated from the lot's zone and the chosen building type.
Permission: in the R zone a dwelling unit is permitted in a townhouse. Evaluated from the lot's zone and the chosen building type.
Permission: in the R zone a dwelling unit is permitted in a detached houseplex. Evaluated from the lot's zone and the chosen building type.
Permission: in the R zone a dwelling unit is permitted in a semi detached houseplex. Evaluated from the lot's zone and the chosen building type.
Clause (F) was deleted by By-law 648-2025; it has no effect.
Permission: in the R zone a dwelling unit is permitted in a apartment building. Evaluated from the lot's zone and the chosen building type.

Permission that applies despite 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A): a detached houseplex, semi-detached houseplex, townhouse or apartment building is permitted in the R zone if it complies with the R zone regulations and all other requirements of the By-law, or is authorized by a Section 45 minor variance. The building type permission is evaluated; compliance with all other regulations is the rest of the evaluation.
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed PERMIT (the clause's effect is to permit the four types). It also sets precedence over the Chapter 900 exception regulations 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A) (a site-specific exception's narrower list of building types does not remove these permissions); ranks_layers is reserved for PROCEDURAL units so it is not keyed here. The minor-variance alternative is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Permits converting a lawfully constructed (pre-December 15, 2023) detached house in the R zone to an apartment building by adding dwelling units entirely within the existing building, which keeps its lawfully existing status.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the construction date and lawful status of the existing building, which we do not hold. The date December 15, 2023 is a date, not a numeric literal.

units.disclosure: Converting an existing detached house into an apartment building is allowed only for a house lawfully built before December 15, 2023, with all new units inside the existing building. We cannot confirm the building's history, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Deeming rule: a detached house converted to an apartment building under (1) may still be treated as a detached house for the listed clauses and regulations (10.5.50.10, 10.5.80.10, 10.5.80.1(2), 10.10.40.10(2) and (11), 10.10.40.40(2), 10.10.80.1(1)(B), 200.5.10.1(1)).
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to an existing converted building; the deemed building type changes which regulations apply, which we cannot determine without the building's history. Cross-referenced regulation numbers are not literals.

units.disclosure: A converted detached house may keep being treated as a detached house for certain height, landscaping, coverage and parking rules. We cannot confirm whether a lot holds such a converted building.

evidence.semi_detached_house: a portion of a semi-detached house

calculation_handling.description: Permits converting one lot's portion of a semi-detached house to more than four dwelling units, still treated as a semi-detached house, if the building was lawfully constructed before December 15, 2023 and the new units are entirely within it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the construction date and lawful status of the existing building. 'more than four' describes the permitted conversion, not a lot condition, so it is listed as an application threshold rather than a condition.if.

units.disclosure: Converting one half of an existing semi-detached house to more than four units is allowed only if it was lawfully built before December 15, 2023 and all units are inside it. We cannot confirm the building's history.

calculation_handling.description: Deeming rule: the unconverted portion of the semi-detached house on the adjacent lot stays in the original building type for applying the by-law's standards.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires knowing that the adjoining half of the semi-detached house was converted under (2); we do not hold that fact.

units.disclosure: If the other half of your semi-detached house was converted to many units, your half is still treated as a semi-detached house. We cannot confirm such a conversion.

evidence.apartment_building: considered to be an apartment building

calculation_handling.description: Deeming rule: for Clause 10.5.40.40 and Regulation 10.10.40.30(1), the converted portion (more than four units) of a semi-detached house may be treated as an apartment building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to an existing converted building; we do not hold conversion history. Cross-referenced regulation numbers are not literals.

units.disclosure: A semi-detached half converted to more than four units may be treated as an apartment building for certain depth and floor-area rules. We cannot confirm such a conversion.

calculation_handling.description: Deeming rule: if both halves of an originally semi-detached house are converted under this regulation, the building is still considered its original building type, subject to 10.10.20.41(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires conversion history of both halves; not held.

units.disclosure: If both halves of a semi-detached house are converted, the building remains a semi-detached house for zoning purposes. We cannot confirm such a conversion.

calculation_handling.description: Any addition or extension to a lawfully existing building converted under (1) or (2) must comply with all other regulations or be authorized by a minor variance under Section 45 of the Planning Act.
calculation_handling.gaps: The unit text does not name a zone (the R zone is named only in (1) and (2)), so zones is left empty for lack of an evidence phrase. 'Section 45' is a statutory section number, not a literal.

units.disclosure: Additions to a converted, lawfully existing building must meet all other zoning rules or get a minor variance. We cannot confirm whether a building is such a converted building.

calculation_handling.description: Extends the meaning of 'lawful', 'lawfully' and 'lawfully existing' for the listed regulations to include buildings, structures or uses authorized or permitted on or before December 15, 2023.
calculation_handling.gaps: A definition of a status we do not hold; the date is not a numeric literal. No zone is named in the unit text.

calculation_handling.description: Extends the meaning of 'lawful', 'lawfully' and 'lawfully existing' for the listed regulations to include buildings for which a building permit was lawfully issued before December 15, 2023.
calculation_handling.gaps: A definition of a status we do not hold; the date is not a numeric literal. No zone is named in the unit text.

calculation_handling.description: Regulations 10.5.1.10(3) and 10.10.40.1(3) (dwelling-unit limits) do not apply to a lawfully existing detached house or semi-detached portion converted under 10.10.20.41(1) or (2).
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.5.1.10(3) and 10.10.40.1(3) (the template has no displaces field; recorded here). Applies only to an existing converted building whose history we do not hold. No zone is named in the unit text.

units.disclosure: The usual limits on the number of dwelling units do not apply to a lawfully existing house converted under these rules. We cannot confirm whether a building qualifies.

evidence.lawfully_existing: has been converted to contain more than four dwelling units

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.10.20.1(1) and (2), a secondary suite is not permitted in the portion of a semi-detached house converted to more than four dwelling units under 10.10.20.41(2).
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a semi-detached portion already converted under (2); conversion history not held. No zone is named in the unit text. 'Despite regulations 150.10.20.1(1) and (2)' displaces the secondary-suite permission for this case only. M-196(1): applied in the interior-conversion answer (a semi-detached portion converted under 10.10.20.41(2) takes no secondary suite); M-214(3): a secondary suite in a semi-detached house is a deferred form, disclosed (forms_deferred).

units.disclosure: A secondary suite is not allowed in a semi-detached half that has been converted to more than four units. We cannot confirm whether a building has been converted.

calculation_handling.description: Up to 5 dwelling units converted from interior floor area of a lawfully existing apartment building on a lot with 100 or more dwelling units are exempt from regulation 10.5.30.1(2) (water main and sewer capacity on major streets).
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.5.30.1(2) for the converted units only; needs the existing building's unit count and lawful status. dwelling_units is read as the lot's existing unit count, an approximation.

units.disclosure: Converting common areas of a large existing apartment building (100+ units) into up to 5 new units is exempt from the water/sewer capacity rule; we do not evaluate existing-building conversions.

calculation_handling.description: Adds an exclusion to the gross floor area of an apartment building: the area converted to additional dwelling units under 10.10.20.60 is deducted, in addition to the areas in 10.5.40.40(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the converted area of an existing building, which we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Floor area converted to new units under this conversion rule is not counted in the building's gross floor area; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from 10.10.40.1(3) and any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on the maximum number of dwelling units on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.10.40.1(3) and article 900.2.10 unit-count provisions for the converted units only.

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building do not count against the maximum number of units; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from 10.10.40.40(1) and any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on maximum floor space index.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the FSI limit for the converted units only; needs existing-building facts.

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building are exempt from the floor space index limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from 10.10.40.50(1) and any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on additional minimum amenity space.
calculation_handling.gaps: Amenity space is not a DSL target; displacement applies to the converted units only.

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building need no additional amenity space; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from 200.5.10.1(1), Table 200.5.10.1 and any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on additional minimum visitor parking spaces.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces visitor parking requirements for the converted units only.

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building need no additional visitor parking; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from 200.15.10.5(1), Table 200.15.10.5 and any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on minimum additional accessible parking spaces.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces accessible parking requirements for the converted units only.

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building need no additional accessible parking; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on additional minimum residential occupant parking spaces.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces only article 900.2.10 provisions; the base parking reduction is governed by 10.10.20.60(2).

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building need no additional resident parking under site-specific provisions; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from 220.5.10.1(1) and (2) and any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on additional minimum loading spaces.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces loading space requirements for the converted units only.

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building need no additional loading spaces; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The converted units are exempt from 230.5.10.1(5) and any 900.2.10 prevailing provision on additional long-term and short-term bicycle parking spaces.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces bicycle parking requirements for the converted units only.

units.disclosure: Up to 5 converted units in a large existing apartment building need no additional bicycle parking; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: For compliance with 10.10.20.60, a lawful existing parking space or drive aisle smaller than the required minimum length, width or vertical clearance is deemed to meet the minimum at its lawful dimension, provided no alteration increases the noncompliance after June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Grandfathers several as-built dimensions (parking space length, width, vertical clearance; drive aisle width) at once; no single DSL target and no as-built input, so keyed UNUSUAL rather than an existing() LIMIT.

units.disclosure: Existing undersized parking spaces and drive aisles in the building are treated as compliant for this conversion if not made worse after June 26, 2025; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 200.5.10.11(1)(C), lawful resident occupant parking spaces of a lawfully existing building may be reduced for a conversion under 10.10.20.60(1), if the converted spaces are within a building and at least 1 residential occupant parking space per lawfully existing dwelling unit is maintained.
calculation_handling.gaps: The zone is not named in this clause; keyed to R from the article context (10.10 is the R zone) with no zone evidence phrase. The rate counts lawfully existing dwelling units, not proposed units. The 'located within a building' proviso is not expressed.

units.disclosure: When converting common areas to units, existing resident parking may be reduced to 1 space per existing unit, using spaces inside the building; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the 10.10.20.60(1)/(2) exemptions: converted dwelling units must comply with 5.10.1.30(3)(A) on dwelling units below grade, unless a Section 45 minor variance authorizes otherwise.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to the existing-building conversion path; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: Converted units below grade must meet the below-grade unit rule in 5.10.1.30(3)(A); not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the exemptions: interior floor area used for lawfully existing dwelling units may not be converted to additional dwelling units, unless a Section 45 minor variance authorizes it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Existing-building conversion path; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: Existing units cannot be split into extra units under this conversion rule; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the exemptions: interior floor area used for lawfully existing amenity space may not be reduced, unless a Section 45 minor variance authorizes it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Amenity space is not modelled; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: Existing indoor amenity space cannot be reduced by the conversion; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the exemptions: the lawful number of visitor and accessible parking spaces of a lawfully existing building may not be reduced, unless a Section 45 minor variance authorizes it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Existing-building conversion path; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: Existing visitor and accessible parking cannot be reduced by the conversion; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the exemptions: the lawful number of long-term and short-term bicycle parking spaces of a lawfully existing building may not be reduced, unless a Section 45 minor variance authorizes it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Existing-building conversion path; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: Existing bicycle parking cannot be reduced by the conversion; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the exemptions: interior floor area used for common facilities secured as an improvement by registered City agreements may not be converted to additional dwelling units, unless a Section 45 minor variance authorizes it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires knowledge of registered City agreements on title, which we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Common facilities secured by a City agreement on title cannot be converted to units; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: For 10.10.20.60(1)-(3), lawful / lawfully existing also includes buildings, structures or uses authorized or permitted on or before June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Definition of a term, no DSL variable; zone keyed from article context.

calculation_handling.description: For 10.10.20.60(1)-(3), lawful / lawfully existing also includes anything for which a building permit was lawfully issued before June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Definition of a term, no DSL variable; zone keyed from article context.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets lot requirements for a detached house, those requirements are applied to a detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Read as INCLUDE (the houseplex takes the exception's detached-house lot requirements); a PROCEDURAL reading is possible because it opens with 'Despite regulations 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A)'. The condition 'the only residential building on a lot' has no vocab.lot_condition token and is not keyed as a condition. Depends on Chapter 900 exception content (backlog).

units.disclosure: If your lot is in a Chapter 900 exception area with lot requirements for a detached house, those requirements also apply to a detached houseplex; we do not yet evaluate exception lot requirements.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets lot requirements for a semi-detached house, those requirements (for the portion that is an individual dwelling unit) are applied to a semi-detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Read as INCLUDE; a PROCEDURAL reading is possible ('Despite regulations 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A)'). The condition 'the only residential building on a lot' has no vocab.lot_condition token. Depends on Chapter 900 exception content (backlog).

units.disclosure: If your lot is in a Chapter 900 exception area with lot requirements for a semi-detached house, those requirements also apply to a semi-detached houseplex; we do not yet evaluate exception lot requirements.

evidence.secondary_suite: a residential building with a secondary suite
evidence.semi_detached_houseplex: semi-detached houseplex or a residential building

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot coverage under 10.10.60.70(1)(C) is more permissive than the coverage that would apply under 10.10.30.1(1) (exception lot requirements), the more permissive one prevails.
calculation_handling.gaps: Precedence is conditional on which value is more permissive, not a fixed layer order; 'base > exception' records that the base-chapter regulation 10.10.60.70(1)(C) may override the exception-derived coverage despite 900.1.10(3)/(4)(A). The secondary-suite arm is an alternative (or), not a conjunction, so it is recorded in application rather than condition.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum lot area in the R zone is the numerical value after the letter "a" in the lot's zone label (square metres), when the label has an "a" value.
calculation_handling.gaps: Condition keyed as a presence test only (labelled(a)); no lot_condition token applies to a presence test.

calculation_handling.description: Where the zone label has no "a" value, the minimum lot area (square metres) is the required minimum lot frontage multiplied by 30 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: required_lot_frontage_m is the required (label f / zone) frontage, not the measured frontage, per the clause wording "required minimum lot frontage". If no required frontage resolves for the lot, the result is not_evaluated.

evidence.label_value: the letter "f"

calculation_handling.description: Where the zone label carries an 'f' value, that value (metres) is the required minimum lot frontage.

evidence.label_value: an "f" value

calculation_handling.description: Where the zone label has no 'f' value, the required minimum lot frontage is 6.0 m.

evidence.townhouse: for a townhouse with every dwelling unit
evidence.all_units_front_street: every dwelling unit fronting directly on a street

calculation_handling.description: Measurement rule for the frontage required by (A) or (B): for a semi-detached house it is required per dwelling unit; for a townhouse with every unit fronting a street it is required per dwelling unit and reduced by 1.0 m for each unit without an individual private driveway leading to its front.
calculation_handling.gaps: Modifies the (A)/(B) value rather than setting its own bound; the per-unit multiplication and the 1.0 m per-unit reduction depend on the unit count and on how many units lack an individual driveway, which has no DSL input, so no expression is written. The 1.0 m reduction is listed as a cross-reference adjustment for lack of a closer reason. The lot conditions are arm-specific (townhouse arm only), so they are recorded in application, not as a conjunctive condition. M-176(1) / M-187 Q4: the townhouse arm is the driveway trade-off (1.0 m less per unit without an individual private driveway; townhouse_driveway_width); M-214(2)/(3): the semi-detached house and townhouse forms are not modelled in R, so the per-unit frontage is disclosed, not bound.

units.disclosure: For a semi-detached house, and for a townhouse whose units all front a street, the minimum frontage applies to each dwelling unit: the f value on the zoning map, or 6.0 m where the zone label has no f value. A townhouse unit without its own private driveway may have 1.0 m less (5.0 m per unit at the 6.0 m default). We do not know the driveway layout, so the 1.0 m reduction is disclosed, not applied; this per-unit frontage is not yet calculated.

evidence.unit_not_fronting_street: not fronting directly on a street

calculation_handling.description: Despite (A)-(C), a lot with a townhouse having one or more dwelling units not fronting directly on a street requires a minimum lot frontage of 30.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The trigger is the negation of the all_units_front_street token, which the condition grammar cannot express (no negated token); condition is left 'none' and the arm applies only to townhouses where some unit does not front a street, which needs the user's layout. 'despite (A), (B) and (C)' is a within-regulation precedence and is not keyed as a displacement.

units.disclosure: A townhouse lot where any unit does not face the street needs at least 30.0 m of frontage. We need your proposed layout to know whether this applies.

calculation_handling.description: Scope statement: Article 10.10.40 applies to buildings or structures in the R zone other than ancillary buildings or structures, which are governed by Articles 10.5.60 and 10.10.60.
calculation_handling.gaps: Scope only; excludes ancillary_building from Article 10.10.40 units.

calculation_handling.description: For 10.10.40.1(9), lawful / lawfully existing also includes buildings, structures or uses authorized or permitted on or before June 26, 2025, and those for which a building permit was lawfully issued before June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Term definition for the bedroom transition rule; zone keyed from article context (no zone phrase in the unit).

calculation_handling.description: Defines a 'request for a zoning certificate' by reference to Municipal Code Chapter 363, Article I.
Defines a 'complete application for a zoning by-law amendment' by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
Defines a 'complete application for a minor variance' by reference to Section 2 of O. Reg. 200/96.
Defines a 'complete application for site plan approval' by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
A maximum of one residential building is permitted on a lot in the R zone.
calculation_handling.gaps: Counts residential buildings only; building_types 'any' because the clause names no specific type. Displaced by (2)(B) on a lot abutting a major street for townhouses and apartment buildings.

calculation_handling.description: Despite (2)(A), more than one townhouse or apartment building, or combination, is permitted on a lot abutting a major street.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the one-building limit of (2)(A) for townhouses and apartment buildings on major-street lots.

calculation_handling.description: If the lot's zone label has the letter u, the number after u is the maximum number of dwelling units on the lot.
Despite (3)(A), an apartment building on a lot abutting a major street may have the greater of 60 dwelling units or the label u value.
calculation_handling.gaps: Apartment buildings are outside the core MaxBLD types (detached/semi/row) but the limit is fully expressible.

evidence.no_individual_private_driveway: does not have an individual private driveway

calculation_handling.description: Minimum width of a townhouse dwelling unit is 5.0 metres if the unit does not have an individual private driveway leading directly to its front.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only under no_individual_private_driveway (design choice). By M-176(1) (build more) no individual private driveway is assumed, so this 5.0 m is answered; (B) 6.0 m is the disclosed trade-off (vocab design_choice_disclosure.default_overrides).

units.disclosure: Townhouse unit width is 5.0 m per unit without an individual private driveway, 6.0 m with one.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum width of a townhouse dwelling unit is 6.0 metres in all other cases, i.e. where the unit has an individual private driveway leading directly to its front.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'In all other cases' read as the unit having an individual private driveway; whether it does is a design input.

calculation_handling.description: A building, or a detached addition, with dwelling units is not permitted in the rear of another building or of the original part of the same building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Site layout of multiple buildings is not modelled; MaxBLD assumes one principal building fronting the street.

units.disclosure: A building with dwelling units cannot be placed behind another building on the lot (except townhouses or apartments on a major street); not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: A building, or a detached addition, is not permitted in front of a building with dwelling units so as to put a building with dwelling units in the rear of another building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Site layout of multiple buildings is not modelled.

units.disclosure: A new building cannot be placed in front of an existing building with units so that the units end up at the rear; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: (5)(A) and (5)(B) do not apply to townhouses or apartment buildings on a lot abutting a major street.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.10.40.1(5)(A) and (5)(B) for those types on major-street lots.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 900.1.10(3) and (4)(A), where a detached houseplex is the only residential building on the lot and the applicable Chapter 900 exception has principal building requirements for a detached house, the houseplex is subject to those detached-house exception requirements.
calculation_handling.gaps: Maps exception requirements written for detached house onto detached houseplex; the 'only residential building on a lot' condition has no vocab token. Zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: On a lot with a site-specific exception, a detached houseplex follows the exception's rules for a detached house; exceptions are not yet evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 900.1.10(3) and (4)(A), where a semi-detached houseplex is the only residential building on the lot and the applicable Chapter 900 exception has principal building requirements for a semi-detached house, the houseplex is subject to those requirements for the portion of a semi-detached house that is an individual dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Maps exception requirements for semi-detached house onto semi-detached houseplex; 'only residential building' condition has no vocab token. Zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: On a lot with a site-specific exception, a semi-detached houseplex follows the exception's rules for a semi-detached house; exceptions are not yet evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.10.40.1(6), 900.1.10(3) and (4)(A), if a regulation in 10.10.40.10, 10.10.40.30 or 10.10.40.40 for a detached or semi-detached houseplex is more permissive than the one that would apply under (6), the more permissive regulation prevails.
calculation_handling.gaps: Base prevails over exception only where more permissive, per regulation (height, depth, FSI); a plain layer ranking cannot express 'more permissive wins'. Zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: For houseplexes, if the regular R-zone height, depth or density rule is more generous than the site exception, the generous rule applies; exceptions are not yet evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: In a detached or semi-detached houseplex with two dwelling units, the maximum number of bedrooms is four times the number of dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: Stem text reads 'semi- detached houseplex' in the heading. A bachelor unit counts as one bedroom per (8)(C).

calculation_handling.description: In a detached or semi-detached houseplex with three or more dwelling units, the maximum number of bedrooms is three times the number of dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: The multiplier 'three' and the threshold 'three or more' are the same word in the text; the first binds the expression, the second the condition.

calculation_handling.description: For counting bedrooms under (8)(A) and (B), a bachelor dwelling unit has one bedroom.
calculation_handling.gaps: Counting rule applied to the bedroom_count user input.

calculation_handling.description: A houseplex may exceed the (8) bedroom maximum if it is a lawfully existing residential building and no bedrooms are added that increase the noncompliance after June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Transition rule for existing buildings; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: An existing houseplex with more bedrooms than now allowed may keep them if none are added after June 26, 2025; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: A houseplex built under a permit issued after June 26, 2025 may exceed the (8) bedroom maximum if its bedrooms per unit do not exceed those identified in a zoning certificate, zoning by-law amendment, minor variance or site plan approval whose request or complete application was filed on or before June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires application-filing history we do not hold; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: Projects with applications filed on or before June 26, 2025 may keep their approved bedroom counts; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: For a building constructed under (9)(B), no bedrooms may be added after the founding building permit if they would increase the noncompliance beyond that permit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires permit history; zone keyed from article context.

units.disclosure: Bedrooms cannot be added beyond what the transitional permit allowed; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum height in the R zone is the HT value on the Height Overlay Map.

evidence.overlay_mapped: no numerical value following the letters

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot has no HT value on the Height Overlay Map, the maximum height is 10.0 m.
For a detached or semi-detached houseplex, maximum height is the greater of the HT overlay value and 10.0 m (an absent HT argument is dropped).

numeric_expression: height_m = by_type(townhouse: max(13.0 m; overlay(HT)); apartment_building: max(19.0 m; overlay(HT))) @(1)(D)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street, a townhouse may reach the greater of 13.0 m or HT, and an apartment building the greater of 19.0 m or HT.
calculation_handling.gaps: The townhouse arm comes from (1)(D)(i) and the apartment arm from (1)(D)(ii); cited at the unit path (1)(D). Requires knowing whether the lot abuts a major street, which may not be held for every lot.

calculation_handling.description: Rooftop equipment on the tower portion of a building may exceed the maximum height by 6.5 m if it covers no more than 450 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 6.5 m projection allowance has no DSL target (rooftop equipment height) and 450 m2 is a roof-equipment area threshold with no DSL input; both recorded as threshold_used_in_application as the closest closed reason. Towers (storeys above 24.0 m) are outside MaxBLD building types.

units.disclosure: On the tower part of a building (storeys more than 24.0 m above the ground), rooftop equipment may rise up to 6.5 m above the height limit if it covers no more than 450 m²; towers are apartment forms and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Chimneys, pipes and vents on a tower roof may exceed the (10)(A) allowance by a further 3.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 3.0 m further projection has no DSL target; recorded as threshold_used_in_application as the closest closed reason.

units.disclosure: On the tower part of a building, chimneys, pipes and vents may rise a further 3.0 m above the 6.5 m rooftop allowance; towers are apartment forms and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a tower for 10.10.40.10(10): portions enclosing storeys above 24.0 m, with average storey GFA above 24.0 m of no more than 750 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: The defined term "tower" is not a DSL variable; target none.

units.disclosure: A tower is the part of a building enclosing storeys more than 24.0 m above the ground, where no storey above 24.0 m averages more than 750 m² of floor area; towers are apartment forms and are not modelled.

evidence.detached_houseplex: residential building, other than an apartment building
evidence.flat_or_shallow_roof: slope of less than 1.0 vertical units for every 10.0 horizontal units

calculation_handling.description: With a flat or shallow roof (slope under 1.0 vertical to 10.0 horizontal over more than 50 percent of the roof area), main walls may rise above the main-wall height limit if the front and rear main walls above it are set back at least 1.4 m from the front and rear main walls below. Only the storey above the limit is set back; the storeys below are unchanged.
calculation_handling.gaps: The roof form is the builder's choice (flat_or_shallow_roof, M-172(3)); Layer 3 computes both roof forms and headlines the larger (M-184).

units.disclosure: The top storey is set back 1.4 m from the front and rear walls.

Only the storey above the limit is set back; the storeys below are unchanged.
calculation_handling.gaps: The roof form is the builder's choice (flat_or_shallow_roof, M-172(3)); Layer 3 computes both roof forms and headlines the larger (M-184).

calculation_handling.description: Main wall height limit is the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m below the permitted maximum height, for all side main walls over at least 70% of their width.
calculation_handling.gaps: Main-wall height is an envelope limit (M-176(2)): the storey above max(7.0 m; H − 2.5 m) is a roof storey in the Spec 78 §Phase-5 max-build pass. Which pair takes the limit (all side walls for 70 % of their width, or the front and rear walls for the frontage-tier share) is a design choice the maximum build makes (P5.12 main_wall_pair). The subject is per zone (M-190): RM names a detached or semi-detached house only, so an RM houseplex or townhouse has no main-wall cap; RT has no main-wall rule (M-186).

units.disclosure: Main walls may be no higher than the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m less than the permitted maximum height, on either all side main walls (for at least 70% of each side main wall's width) or all front and rear main walls (for at least the share of their total width the clause sets by lot frontage); the design chooses which pair.

calculation_handling.description: Where there is no ST value on the map, the number of storeys is not limited by this regulation.
The ST storey limit in (3)(A) does not apply to detached or semi-detached houseplexes.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.10.40.10(3)(A) for houseplexes; displaces[] is not a keyed field here.

numeric_expression: height_storeys = by_type(townhouse: max(4 storeys; overlay(ST)); apartment_building: max(6 storeys; overlay(ST))) @(3)(D)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street, a townhouse may have the greater of 4 storeys or ST, and an apartment building the greater of 6 storeys or ST (excluding a mechanical penthouse).
calculation_handling.gaps: The text writes the numbers as words ("four storeys", "six storeys"); normalized to numerals 4 and 6. Arms come from (3)(D)(i) and (ii). Mechanical penthouse exclusion not expressed. Requires major street status of the lot.

calculation_handling.description: A roof above the second storey on a detached house in the R zone may not be steeper than 5.0 vertical units for every 3.0 horizontal units.
calculation_handling.gaps: Which roof is above the second storey is Layer 3 geometry (Spec 78 P5.2 item 6, form (b)): the pitched roof is capped by this slope only on a detached house of more than two storeys.

units.disclosure: On a detached house in the R zone, a roof above the second storey may be no steeper than 5 vertical to 3 horizontal.

calculation_handling.description: Dormer walls are not main walls if the dormer face is in a roof directly above a main wall within the main wall height limit (and (B) is met).
calculation_handling.gaps: "a residential building with two or more storeys": building_types left any because no specific type is named; "two" recorded as a threshold literal.

units.disclosure: Dormer walls do not count as main walls if each dormer face sits in a roof directly above a part of a main wall within the main wall height limit; the design chooses the dormers.

calculation_handling.description: Dormer walls are not main walls if total dormer face width is no more than 40% of the width of the qualifying main walls.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-185: the maximum build takes the dormers at this 40 % share of the main-wall width (the design chooses the dormers, M-176(3)); the share feeds the Spec 78 §Phase-5 roof-storey area (P5.12 dormers_at_max). Kept DEFINE: the clause decides whether dormer walls count as main walls.

units.disclosure: Dormer walls do not count as main walls if the dormer faces total no more than 40% of the width of the main walls below them that are within the main wall height limit; the design chooses the dormers.

calculation_handling.description: The lowest point of a main pedestrian entrance through the front or a side main wall of a detached or semi-detached house may be no higher than 1.2 m above established grade.
calculation_handling.gaps: The entrance elevation is a design choice (M-172, restrictive): disclosed, never a bound on the build answer (M-174).

units.disclosure: The main front entrance may be no more than 1.2 m above the ground level the City measures from (established grade).

calculation_handling.gaps: Relative to existing building floor levels; no DSL target. "residential building" names no specific type, so building_types any.

units.disclosure: In the R zone a rear addition's floors may not rise above the existing top floor; the renovation answer keeps the back-room storeys at or below the existing storeys.

calculation_handling.description: Roof slope limit for altered roofs of lawfully existing detached houses in the R zone (in addition to 10.5.40.11(3)): the altered roof may not be steeper than 5.0 vertical to 3.0 horizontal.
calculation_handling.gaps: The DSL has no roof-slope target, so the numeric limit cannot be keyed as a LIMIT; keyed UNUSUAL. The 5.0 and 3.0 literals are the slope limit itself; no literal_not_expressed_reason fits exactly, threshold_used_in_application is the closest closed value. Applies only to an altered roof of a lawfully existing building, which needs as-built facts we do not hold.

units.disclosure: For an existing detached house in the R zone, an altered roof may not be steeper than 5 units up for every 3 units across. We do not check roof slope; confirm it with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: In the R zone, on a lot abutting a major street, the maximum building length of a townhouse is 19.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only when the lot abuts a major street; depends on the major-street designation being known for the lot.

calculation_handling.description: In the R zone, on a lot abutting a major street, the maximum building length of an apartment building is 25.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only when the lot abuts a major street; depends on the major-street designation being known for the lot.

calculation_handling.description: In the R zone the maximum building depth is 17.0 metres for a detached house, semi-detached house, detached houseplex, semi-detached houseplex, townhouse or apartment building.

condition.if: (lot_depth_m ≥ 36.0 m and lot_frontage_m < 10.0 m) or (lot_depth_m ≥ 40.0 m and lot_frontage_m ≥ 10.0 m)

calculation_handling.description: Despite (A), a detached or semi-detached houseplex may have a building depth of 19.0 metres if the lot has a depth of 36.0 m or more and frontage under 10.0 m, or a depth of 40.0 m or more and frontage of 10.0 m or more.
calculation_handling.gaps: The condition has no parentheses in the grammar; it is read with 'and' binding tighter than 'or' ((i) or (ii)). Lot frontage here is the measured frontage.

condition.if: (proposed_height_m ≤ 13.0 m and lot_depth_m ≥ 36.0 m and lot_frontage_m < 10.0 m) or (proposed_height_m ≤ 13.0 m and lot_depth_m ≥ 40.0 m and lot_frontage_m ≥ 10.0 m)

calculation_handling.description: Despite (A), an apartment building 13.0 metres or less in height may have a building depth of 19.0 metres on a lot meeting the (i) or (ii) depth/frontage test, if no part of a side main wall with a primary window is set back less than 5.5 metres from a side lot line not abutting a street.
calculation_handling.gaps: The (iii) proviso (side main wall with a primary window at least 5.5 m from a non-street side lot line) is a design condition with no vocab token or DSL variable, so the 5.5 m is not expressed; 'and' binds tighter than 'or' in the condition.

units.disclosure: The 19.0 m depth for low apartment buildings also requires side walls with main windows to be at least 5.5 m from the side lot line; we do not check window placement.

calculation_handling.description: Despite (A) to (C), maximum building depth does not apply to a townhouse or apartment building on a lot abutting a major street.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.10.40.30(1)(A) and (1)(C) for these types on major-street lots.

calculation_handling.description: A pre-October 15, 1953 detached or semi-detached house on a lot with permitted FSI 0.6 may get a rear addition if overall FSI including the addition does not exceed 0.69.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a detached or semi-detached house erected before October 15, 1953 on a lot whose permitted FSI is 0.6; the 0.6 is the permitted FSI used to decide whether the rear-addition allowance applies, not a limit. Depends on the existing building's construction date and prior additions, which we do not hold. The 0.69 is a ceiling on the permission, not a general FSI limit, so it is not keyed as an fsi LIMIT. M-211(3) (with M-192): the pre-15 October 1953 rear-addition relief (overall FSI up to 0.69 on a 0.6 lot) is a renovation reading, disclosed (r_pre1953_fsi_relief), never applied: the build year is a site fact (M-158, M-169), so the new-build answer keeps the 0.6.

units.disclosure: Older houses (built before October 15, 1953) on 0.6 FSI lots may add a rear addition up to an overall FSI of 0.69; we do not evaluate this because it depends on the age of the existing house.

calculation_handling.description: The rear addition may be no closer to a side lot line than the existing side main wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a detached or semi-detached house erected before October 15, 1953 on a lot whose permitted FSI is 0.6; the 0.6 is the permitted FSI used to decide whether the rear-addition allowance applies, not a limit. units.disclosure: The rear-addition allowance for older houses requires the addition to stay within the existing side wall lines; we do not evaluate it.

calculation_handling.description: The rear-addition allowance requires any prior addition to be at least 5 years old.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a detached or semi-detached house erected before October 15, 1953 on a lot whose permitted FSI is 0.6; the 0.6 is the permitted FSI used to decide whether the rear-addition allowance applies, not a limit. Depends on the existing building's construction date and prior additions, which we do not hold. The 5 years is an age test on prior additions; no DSL variable.

units.disclosure: The rear-addition allowance for older houses requires any earlier addition to be at least 5 years old; we do not evaluate it.

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule (in addition to 10.5.40.50(1)): in the R zone, the exterior sides of a lawfully existing platform that was lawfully enclosed under former City of Toronto By-law 438-86 are not main walls.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on as-built facts (a lawfully existing platform, lawfully enclosed under By-law 438-86) that we do not hold. The former by-law is referenced as the source of the enclosure's legality, not as an alternate compliance path, so it is not keyed as a PREVAILING instrument. No DSL variable is defined, so target is none.

units.disclosure: In the R zone, the outside sides of an existing platform that was legally enclosed under the old City of Toronto By-law 438-86 are not counted as main walls. We do not know whether your lot has such a platform.

calculation_handling.description: Despite the encroachment rules 10.5.40.50(2) and 10.5.40.60(1)(A), a lawfully existing porch in the R zone may be reconstructed or replaced within its same outer limits, with no enlargement.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on an existing porch and its lawful status, which we do not hold. A porch has no vocab.uses token. Displaces 10.5.40.50(2) and 10.5.40.60(1)(A) for the existing porch only (no displaces field in the template).

units.disclosure: An existing lawful porch can be rebuilt or replaced in the same footprint even if it doesn't meet today's encroachment rules, as long as it is not enlarged. We don't hold information about existing porches.

A townhouse on a lot abutting a major street has a minimum side yard setback of 0.9 m if all dwelling units front directly onto a street, otherwise 7.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The (ii) 7.5 m arm (units not all fronting a street; token unit_not_fronting_street) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on such a lot the side setback is not_evaluated, never 0.9 m.

evidence.primary_windows: portions of the main wall that have primary windows

calculation_handling.description: An apartment building on a lot abutting a major street has minimum side yard setbacks of 1.8 m for main-wall portions without primary windows, 5.5 m for portions with primary windows, 7.5 m for portions beyond a building length of 25.0 m, and on a corner lot 3.0 m from a side lot line abutting a street.
calculation_handling.gaps: The side setback is 1.8 m for wall portions without primary windows and 5.5 m for portions with them: one statement on the design-choice token primary_windows (M-283; taken as absent, so 1.8 m is answered and the 5.5 m arm is disclosed). The 7.5 m arm for portions beyond a building length of 25.0 m is an additive arm the DSL cannot express (M-130); the base is a necessary minimum on every wall.

units.disclosure: Apartment side setbacks on major streets vary by wall portion (windows, length) and corner-lot status; only partly evaluated.

evidence.primary_windows: portions of the main wall that have primary windows

calculation_handling.gaps: The side setback is 2.4 m for wall portions without primary windows and 5.5 m for portions with them: one statement on the design-choice token primary_windows (M-283; taken as absent, so 2.4 m is answered and the 5.5 m arm is disclosed). The 7.5 m arm for portions beyond a building length of 25.0 m is an additive arm the DSL cannot express (M-130); the base is a necessary minimum on every wall.

units.disclosure: Apartment side setbacks on through lots vary by wall portion; only partly evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Front yard on a major street: lot depth 36.0 m or less: the lesser of the 10.5.40.70(1) setback or 6.0 m where 10.5.40.70(1) applies, else 3.0 m; deeper than 36.0 m: 6.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The through-lot arm (i)(c) (6.0 m) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on a through lot the front setback is not_evaluated, never a guessed value.

calculation_handling.description: The setback regulations 10.5.40.70(1) and 10.10.40.70(1)-(4) do not apply to a transportation use along Eglinton Avenue West and East, provided setbacks are between 0 and 10.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Transportation use (Eglinton transit) has no vocab.uses token and is outside MaxBLD building types. The 0 to 10.5 m setback range is a proviso on the exemption with no DSL target for transit setbacks; recorded as threshold_used_in_application. Area is described by street, so applies_to is map_area. No zone named in the text.

units.disclosure: Transit facilities along Eglinton Avenue are exempt from the normal R-zone setbacks (setbacks between 0 and 10.5 m); this does not affect houses and is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 2.0 m above-ground separation between facing main walls of the same townhouse or apartment building in the R zone when neither wall has openings to dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: The base arm: it applies to every design; the arms that need openings carry the design-choice tokens main_wall_openings (one wall) and main_wall_openings_each (each wall) (M-282), so the smallest separation is answered by default and the larger arms are disclosed. Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 2.0 m between them if neither has openings to dwelling units.

evidence.main_wall_openings: no openings to dwelling units in one of those main walls

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 5.5 m above-ground separation between facing main walls of the same townhouse or apartment building in the R zone when one of the walls has no openings to dwelling units.

Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 5.5 m between them if one of them has no openings to dwelling units.

evidence.main_wall_openings_each: each main wall has an opening to a dwelling unit

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 11.0 m above-ground separation between facing main walls of the same townhouse or apartment building in the R zone when each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: The arm applies when the design has the openings to dwelling units the text names: the design-choice token main_wall_openings_each (M-282; user input main_wall_openings_each, taken as absent, so the smallest separation is answered and this arm is disclosed). Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 11.0 m between them if each has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 5.5 m above-ground separation between main walls of two or more townhouses / apartment buildings on the same R-zone lot abutting a major street, when one or more of the walls has no openings to dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only where two or more townhouses or apartment buildings on the same lot abutting a major street; no token tests that scope (M-149), and the maximum build has one residential building (M-177(3); M-158 new build), so the 5.5 m separation is disclosed, never bound. Suite-to-house separation is 150.7.60.30(1) / 150.8.60.30(1) (M-177(2), M-187 Q12).

units.disclosure: If the lot abutting a major street has two or more townhouses or apartment buildings: their main walls must be at least 5.5 m apart, or 11.0 m where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 11.0 m above-ground separation between main walls of two or more townhouses / apartment buildings on the same R-zone lot abutting a major street, when each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only where two or more townhouses or apartment buildings on the same lot abutting a major street; no token tests that scope (M-149), and the maximum build has one residential building (M-177(3); M-158 new build), so the 11.0 m separation is disclosed, never bound. Suite-to-house separation is 150.7.60.30(1) / 150.8.60.30(1) (M-177(2), M-187 Q12).

units.disclosure: If the lot abutting a major street has two or more townhouses or apartment buildings: their main walls must be at least 5.5 m apart, or 11.0 m where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Where the lawful separation between main walls of lawfully existing buildings on a lot (or within one such building) is less than the by-law requires, that lawful existing separation becomes the minimum for those walls.
calculation_handling.gaps: Sets the minimum to an as-built value. The DSL existing(...) form needs a date or enactment the text does not give, so no expression is written and the unit is keyed as a DEFINE of separation_m rather than a LIMIT. Needs as-built separation data we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Existing buildings whose walls are closer together than today's rules allow may keep that existing distance. We do not hold as-built wall separations.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building covered by (1) must meet the minimum main-wall separation in 10.10.40.80(1) or be authorized by a minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'Section 45' is a statutory section number, not a literal. Applies only to existing buildings relying on (1).

units.disclosure: Additions to such existing buildings must meet the normal wall-separation rule or get a minor variance. We cannot confirm whether a building relies on the existing-separation exemption.

calculation_handling.description: Scope statement: Article 10.10.60 applies to ancillary buildings or structures in the R zone that are ancillary to dwelling units or residential buildings, in addition to Article 10.5.60.
calculation_handling.gaps: Scope only; Article 10.5.60 continues to apply alongside.

calculation_handling.description: In the R zone, an ancillary building containing a parking space (detached garage) must be at least 1.0 m from a rear or side lot line that abuts a street or lane, subject to 10.5.60.20(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: Each arm carries its own abutment test (holds(), M-241): the rear line abutting a street or lane is read as abuts_lane until the ML-1 lot-line classification lands (a rear line abutting a street, a through lot, is not yet told apart); a side line abutting a lane is the lane setback. Subject to 10.5.60.20(4) (not expressed). Whether the ancillary building contains a parking space is a user input (ancillary_contains_parking_space, M-241 (1)).

calculation_handling.description: No minimum setback is required for such a garage from a rear or side lot line that does not abut a street or lane.
calculation_handling.gaps: "no minimum building setback is required" keyed as unregulated (the by-law sets no limit). The "does not abut a street or lane" test is not keyed as a condition token (no negated street/lane token).

calculation_handling.description: In the R zone, ancillary buildings and structures may cover at most 5% of the lot area; the water surface area of an outdoor swimming pool or other water-holding ancillary structure is excluded from that coverage if it complies with 10.5.60.70(2).
calculation_handling.gaps: The 5% limit is the stem of (1), which every unit of this regulation repeats; there is no separate stem unit, so it is keyed as a LIMIT on each exception arm that leaves the limit in force ((A), (B)), with the arm's exclusion described here. It applies 'despite regulation 10.5.60.70(1)', i.e. it replaces the general ancillary coverage limit in the R zone. Arm (A) excludes pool / water-holding structure water surface area when it complies with 10.5.60.70(2); that exclusion needs the pool design and is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: The water surface of an outdoor swimming pool (or other structure holding water) that complies with 10.5.60.70(2) is not counted in the 5% ancillary coverage; the answer does not deduct it.

calculation_handling.description: In the R zone, ancillary buildings and structures may cover at most 5% of the lot area; ancillary buildings or structures containing parking spaces are excluded from that coverage, up to one parking space per dwelling unit on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 5% limit is the stem of (1), which every unit of this regulation repeats; there is no separate stem unit, so it is keyed as a LIMIT on each exception arm that leaves the limit in force ((A), (B)), with the arm's exclusion described here. It applies 'despite regulation 10.5.60.70(1)', i.e. it replaces the general ancillary coverage limit in the R zone. Arm (B) excludes ancillary buildings/structures containing parking spaces, capped at one parking space per dwelling unit (a word, not a numeric literal); the excluded area depends on the parking design and unit count and is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: Ancillary buildings with parking spaces are not counted in the 5% ancillary coverage, up to one parking space per dwelling unit on the lot; the answer does not deduct them.

evidence.secondary_suite: a residential building with a secondary suite

calculation_handling.description: The 5% maximum lot coverage for ancillary buildings and structures (10.10.60.70(1)) does not apply to a lot with a detached houseplex, a semi-detached houseplex or a residential building with a secondary suite, if the overall lot coverage of all buildings and structures on the lot does not exceed 45 percent of the lot area.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the 5% limit of 10.10.60.70(1) (keyed on arms (A) and (B)). The subject is a disjunction (detached houseplex OR semi-detached houseplex OR a residential building with a secondary suite); condition tokens are a conjunction, so has_secondary_suite is not keyed as a condition and the subject is carried in application only. The 45 percent overall-coverage test covers all buildings and structures on the lot and has no threshold token, so it is not keyed as condition.if. Source text is missing 'or' between 'semi-detached houseplex' and 'a residential building'; read as a list.

units.disclosure: If all buildings on the lot together cover no more than 45 % of it, the limit on ancillary building coverage does not apply to a lot with a houseplex or a secondary suite.

evidence.frontage_band: a lot frontage of 7.6 metres or less

calculation_handling.description: A parking space inside a building (not an ancillary building) in the R zone may be converted to habitable space with no replacement parking if the lot frontage is 7.6 m or less, or if it is greater than 7.6 m and the vehicle-entrance floor is below established grade.
calculation_handling.gaps: Only arm (i) (frontage ≤ 7.6 m) is expressed in condition.if; arm (ii) (frontage > 7.6 m with the vehicle-entrance floor below established grade) needs the entrance elevation, which has no DSL input, so the condition is conservatively the frontage arm only. The second 7.6 m occurrence in (ii) is the same threshold. Requires an existing in-building parking space; ancillary buildings are excluded (building_types 'any' as no permitted type is named in this arm).

units.disclosure: Converting an indoor parking space (e.g. a garage) to living space without replacing the parking is allowed on lots 7.6 m wide or less, or on wider lots where the garage floor is below grade. We check the frontage only; we cannot check the garage floor level.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the conversion permission in (1): the parking space must be in a detached house, semi-detached house or townhouse.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires an existing in-building parking space, which we do not hold.

units.disclosure: The garage-to-living-space conversion applies only to detached houses, semi-detached houses and townhouses. We do not hold information about existing garages.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the conversion permission in (1): the vehicle entrance to the parking space must be in the front main wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'in the front main wall' is mapped to garage_entrance_faces_street as the closest token; the front main wall is not strictly the same as facing a street (e.g. corner lots). Requires an existing in-building parking space.

units.disclosure: The conversion applies only where the garage door is in the front wall of the house. We do not hold information about existing garage entrances.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the conversion permission in (1): the driveway to the vehicle entrance must be removed and any front-yard depression filled to established grade.
calculation_handling.gaps: A non-numeric precondition with no requirement token; keyed as part of the PERMIT. Requires an existing driveway and garage.

units.disclosure: To convert the garage, the driveway leading to it must be removed and any dip in the front yard filled to grade. We do not hold existing driveway information.

calculation_handling.description: A parking space inside a building in the R zone may be converted to interior floor area for a use under 10.10.20.100(21) or (22), with no replacement parking, if the space is in a residential building other than an apartment building.
calculation_handling.gaps: The text names residential buildings other than an apartment building (an exclusion, not a list), so building_types is 'any' with apartment_building excluded by the text; ancillary buildings are also excluded. The non-residential use under 10.10.20.100(21)/(22) has no vocab.uses token.

units.disclosure: An indoor parking space in a house (not an apartment building) can be converted to space for certain permitted non-residential uses without replacing the parking. We do not hold information about existing garages.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the conversion permission in (2): the vehicle entrance to the parking space must be in the building's front main wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'in the front main wall' mapped to garage_entrance_faces_street as the closest token. Requires an existing in-building parking space.

units.disclosure: This conversion applies only where the garage door is in the front wall. We do not hold existing garage information.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the conversion permission in (2): the driveway to the vehicle entrance must be removed and any front-yard depression filled to established grade.
calculation_handling.gaps: A non-numeric precondition with no requirement token; keyed as part of the PERMIT.

units.disclosure: The driveway to the converted garage must be removed and the front yard filled to grade. We do not hold existing driveway information.

calculation_handling.description: The removed driveway area in the front yard must be landscaping, but may still be counted as a permitted driveway when calculating required soft landscaping under 10.5.50.10(1)(D).
calculation_handling.gaps: Also contains a deeming rule for the soft-landscaping calculation, recorded here in the description. Requires an existing driveway being removed.

units.disclosure: The area of the removed driveway must become landscaping. We do not hold existing driveway information.

calculation_handling.description: A parking space in the front yard or a side yard abutting a street is subject to 10.5.80.10(3) or must be authorized by a minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'Section 45' is a statutory section number, not a literal. Applies to an existing or proposed front/side-yard parking space, which we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Any parking in the front yard or street-side yard must meet the front-yard parking rule or get a minor variance. We do not hold existing parking pad information.

calculation_handling.description: Regulation 200.5.10.11(1)(C) does not apply to the parking space being converted under (2).
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 200.5.10.11(1)(C) for the converted parking space only (no displaces field in the template).

units.disclosure: A parking rule (200.5.10.11(1)(C)) is waived for the parking space being converted. We do not hold existing garage information.

calculation_handling.description: Despite Chapter 200, no parking space is required in the R zone where access to a side- or rear-yard parking space cannot be provided from a lane or flanking street, the lot frontage is 7.6 m or less, the deed was registered on or before July 2, 1996, and a detached or semi-detached house or houseplex, or one townhouse unit, is erected after July 2, 1996.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the Chapter 200 parking space requirement. The no-lane/no-flanking-street access condition is a negated token test the grammar cannot express, and the deed registration date is data we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Narrow lots (7.6 m or less) with no lane or flanking-street access and a deed registered by July 2, 1996 may need no parking; we cannot confirm the deed date or access.

calculation_handling.description: Despite Chapter 200, no parking space is required where access cannot be provided from a lane or flanking street and a lot not previously severed is severed into at most three lots, each with at most one dwelling unit and a lot frontage of 7.6 m or less.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires severance history and the no-lane/no-flanking-street access test, neither of which we hold or can express.

units.disclosure: Lots created by a first severance into up to three narrow single-unit lots may need no parking; we cannot confirm severance history.

evidence.detached_houseplex: a lot with a detached houseplex
evidence.secondary_suite: a residential building with a secondary suite

calculation_handling.gaps: The ranking is conditional (whichever is more permissive), not a fixed base-over-exception order; keyed as 'base > exception' because the base value only displaces the exception value when it is more permissive. The houseplex and secondary-suite arms are a disjunction, so no condition is keyed (a token list is a conjunction); both arms are recorded in application. Zones left empty: the unit text and stem name no zone (RD applies by chapter, 10.20).

units.disclosure: For a houseplex or a home with a secondary suite in an exception area, the more generous of the base RD lot coverage and the exception's lot coverage applies; we do not yet perform this comparison.

calculation_handling.description: Where the RD zone label carries an "a" value, that value is the required minimum lot area in square metres.
Where the RD zone label has no "a" value, the required minimum lot area is the required minimum lot frontage multiplied by 30 m.
Where the RD zone label carries an "au" value, that value is the required minimum lot area for each dwelling unit in a townhouse.
The required minimum lot frontage is the number after the letter f in the lot's zone label.
Where the zone label has no f value, the required minimum lot frontage is 12.0 m.

evidence.no_individual_private_driveway: does not have an individual private driveway

units.disclosure: The frontage assumes no townhouse unit has its own driveway: 5.0 m per unit (20 m for 4 units). If each unit has its own driveway to the front, it needs 6.0 m per unit (24 m for 4 units).
