calculation_handling.description: Minimum 6.0 m width of a townhouse dwelling unit in all other cases, i.e. where the unit has an individual private driveway leading to its front.
calculation_handling.gaps: "In all other cases" is keyed as the complement of (4)(A): the individual_private_driveway token. Target building_width_m is the nearest vocab target for the width of a townhouse dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Where the RD zone label carries the letter "u", its value is the maximum number of dwelling units on the lot.
For an apartment building on a lot abutting a major street, the maximum number of dwelling units is the greater of 60 or the label "u" value.
calculation_handling.gaps: Zones left empty: the unit text and stem name no zone (RD applies by chapter, 10.20).

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets principal building requirements for a detached house, a detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot takes those requirements (despite 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A)).
calculation_handling.gaps: The "only residential building on a lot" condition has no vocab.lot_condition token; the incorporated requirements live in Chapter 900 exception text. Zones left empty: the unit text and stem name no zone (RD applies by chapter, 10.20).

units.disclosure: If this lot has a Chapter 900 exception with building rules for detached houses, a detached houseplex follows those rules; we do not yet apply that substitution.

calculation_handling.description: For a detached houseplex, a base regulation in 10.20.40.10 to 10.20.40.50 prevails over the exception requirement applied through 10.20.40.1(6) when the base regulation is more permissive.
calculation_handling.gaps: Conditional ranking (only when the base is more permissive), keyed as base > exception. Zones left empty: the unit text and stem name no zone (RD applies by chapter, 10.20).

units.disclosure: For a detached houseplex in an exception area, the more generous of the standard RD building rule and the exception rule applies; we do not yet perform this comparison.

calculation_handling.description: A detached houseplex with two dwelling units may have at most four bedrooms per dwelling unit (four times the number of units).
calculation_handling.gaps: "four" and "two" are written as words; keyed as 4 ratio (a multiplier on a count) and 2 units.

calculation_handling.description: A detached houseplex with three or more dwelling units may have at most three bedrooms per dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: "three" is written as a word; keyed as 3 ratio (multiplier) and 3 units (threshold).

calculation_handling.description: Counting rule: a bachelor dwelling unit counts as one bedroom when applying the bedroom limits in (8)(A) and (8)(B).
Transition: a lawfully existing detached houseplex may exceed the bedroom limit in 10.20.40.1(8), provided no bedrooms added after June 26, 2025 increase the noncompliance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires as-built bedroom counts and lawful-existing status. Zones left empty: the unit text and stem name no zone (RD applies by chapter, 10.20).

units.disclosure: An existing, lawfully built houseplex may keep more bedrooms than the current limit allows; we cannot verify existing bedroom counts.

calculation_handling.description: Transition: a detached houseplex built under a building permit issued after June 26, 2025 may exceed the bedroom limit if it has no more bedrooms per unit than an application (zoning certificate, zoning by-law amendment, minor variance or site plan approval) filed on or before June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Application and permit filing history is not in our data; the condition has no vocab token. Zones left empty: the unit text and stem name no zone (RD applies by chapter, 10.20).

units.disclosure: A houseplex approved through an application filed on or before June 26, 2025 may have more bedrooms than the current limit; we do not have application history.

calculation_handling.description: For a building relying on the (9)(B) transition, no bedrooms may be added after the permit is issued if they would increase the noncompliance beyond that permit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires permit history and as-built bedroom counts. Building type "any": the unit text says "a building" (the stem names a detached houseplex). Zones left empty: the unit text and stem name no zone (RD applies by chapter, 10.20).

units.disclosure: A houseplex using the transition rule cannot later add bedrooms beyond what its permit allowed; we cannot track this.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum height of a building or structure in the RD zone is the HT value on the Height Overlay Map.

evidence.overlay_mapped: no numerical value following the letters

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot has no HT value on the Height Overlay Map, maximum height is 10.0 m.
For a detached houseplex, maximum height is the greater of the HT map value and 10.0 m, despite (A).

numeric_expression: height_m = by_type(townhouse: max(13.0 m; overlay(HT)); apartment_building: max(19.0 m; overlay(HT))) @(1)(D)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street, maximum height is the greater of 13.0 m or HT for a townhouse and the greater of 19.0 m or HT for an apartment building, despite (A) and (B).
Side main walls (for at least 70% of each side wall width) may be no higher than the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m below the permitted maximum height.
calculation_handling.gaps: Main-wall height is an envelope limit (M-176(2)): the storey above max(7.0 m; H − 2.5 m) is a roof storey in the Spec 78 §Phase-5 max-build pass. Which pair takes the limit (all side walls for 70 % of their width, or the front and rear walls for the frontage-tier share) is a design choice the maximum build makes (P5.12 main_wall_pair). The subject is per zone (M-190): RM names a detached or semi-detached house only, so an RM houseplex or townhouse has no main-wall cap; RT has no main-wall rule (M-186).

units.disclosure: Main walls may be no higher than the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m less than the permitted maximum height, on either all side main walls (for at least 70% of each side main wall's width) or all front and rear main walls (for at least the share of their total width the clause sets by lot frontage); the design chooses which pair.

numeric_expression: main_wall_front_rear_share_pct = band(lot_frontage_m; ≥ 12.0 m: 60 pct; > 7.5 m and < 12.0 m: 50 pct; ≤ 7.5 m: 40 pct) @(2)(B)

calculation_handling.description: Alternatively, front and rear main walls (for at least 60%, 50% or 40% of their total width, by lot frontage band) may be no higher than the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m below the permitted maximum height.
calculation_handling.gaps: Main-wall height is an envelope limit (M-176(2)): the storey above max(7.0 m; H − 2.5 m) is a roof storey in the Spec 78 §Phase-5 max-build pass. Which pair takes the limit (all side walls for 70 % of their width, or the front and rear walls for the frontage-tier share) is a design choice the maximum build makes (P5.12 main_wall_pair). The subject is per zone (M-190): RM names a detached or semi-detached house only, so an RM houseplex or townhouse has no main-wall cap; RT has no main-wall rule (M-186).

units.disclosure: Main walls may be no higher than the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m less than the permitted maximum height, on either all side main walls (for at least 70% of each side main wall's width) or all front and rear main walls (for at least the share of their total width the clause sets by lot frontage); the design chooses which pair.

calculation_handling.description: The main wall height limits in (A) and (B) do not apply to townhouses or apartment buildings on lots abutting a major street.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-190: on a lot abutting a major street the x.40.10(2) main-wall cap does not apply to the forms named; those forms are not modelled in the maximum build (M-214(1)) and the lot carries major_street_forms_not_modelled.

units.disclosure: On a major street an apartment building (up to 60 units) or a townhouse may be permitted with larger limits; not modelled here.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum number of storeys in the RD zone is the ST value on the Height Overlay Map.

evidence.overlay_mapped: no numerical value following the letters

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot has no ST value on the Height Overlay Map, the number of storeys is not limited by this regulation.
The storey limit in (A) does not apply to a detached houseplex.

numeric_expression: height_storeys = by_type(townhouse: max(4 storeys; overlay(ST)); apartment_building: max(6 storeys; overlay(ST))) @(3)(D)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street, maximum storeys (excluding a mechanical penthouse) is the greater of four or ST for a townhouse and the greater of six or ST for an apartment building.

evidence.flat_or_shallow_roof: slope of less than 1.0 vertical units for every 10.0 horizontal units

calculation_handling.description: For a residential building with a flat or shallow roof (slope under 1 in 10 over more than 50% of the roof), all main walls may be no higher than the higher of 7.2 m or 2.5 m below the permitted maximum height.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to flat or shallow roofs; the roof type is a user input.

evidence.flat_or_shallow_roof: slope of less than 1.0 vertical units for every 10.0 horizontal units

calculation_handling.description: With a flat or shallow roof (slope under 1.0 vertical to 10.0 horizontal over more than 50 percent of the roof area), main walls may rise above the main-wall height limit if the front and rear main walls above it are set back at least 1.4 m from the front and rear main walls below. Only the storey above the limit is set back; the storeys below are unchanged.
calculation_handling.gaps: The roof form is the builder's choice (flat_or_shallow_roof, M-172(3)); Layer 3 computes both roof forms and headlines the larger (M-184).

units.disclosure: The top storey is set back 1.4 m from the front and rear walls.

calculation_handling.description: The flat-roof main wall rules in (A) and (B) do not apply to townhouses or apartment buildings on a lot abutting a major street.
A parapet on a flat or shallow roof residential building may exceed the main wall height limit in 10.20.40.10(4) by up to 0.3 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed on parapet_projection_m (bound max; Spec 69a M-255): the allowance above the 10.20.40.10(4) main wall height, which answers for a flat or shallow roof.

units.disclosure: On an RD flat or shallow roof, a parapet may rise up to 0.3 m above the main wall height limit.

calculation_handling.description: For a residential building, the lowest point of a main pedestrian entrance through the front wall or a side main wall may be no higher than 1.2 m above established grade.
calculation_handling.gaps: The entrance elevation is a design choice (M-172, restrictive): disclosed, never a bound on the build answer (M-174).

units.disclosure: The main front entrance may be no more than 1.2 m above the ground level the City measures from (established grade).

calculation_handling.description: On a residential building of two or more storeys, dormer walls are not main walls if the dormer face sits in a roof directly above a main wall that does not exceed the main wall height limit (with (B)).
calculation_handling.gaps: Dormer design is a proposal detail with no user input in the vocabulary.

units.disclosure: Dormer walls do not count as main walls if each dormer face sits in a roof directly above a part of a main wall within the main wall height limit; the design chooses the dormers.

calculation_handling.description: Dormer faces in that roof may total no more than 40% of the width of the main walls below that comply with the main wall height limit, measured at the uppermost storey below the roof.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-185: the maximum build takes the dormers at this 40 % share of the main-wall width (the design chooses the dormers, M-176(3)); the share feeds the Spec 78 §Phase-5 roof-storey area (P5.12 dormers_at_max). Kept DEFINE: the clause decides whether dormer walls count as main walls.

units.disclosure: Dormer walls do not count as main walls if the dormer faces total no more than 40% of the width of the main walls below them that are within the main wall height limit; the design chooses the dormers.

calculation_handling.description: Attic floor area meeting 10.5.40.40(1) is not a storey if used only for mechanical equipment and no larger than 20 m2.

units.disclosure: An attic space that meets the City's attic test and holds only mechanical equipment, up to 20 m², does not count as a storey.

calculation_handling.description: When the roof of a lawfully existing residential building in the RD zone is altered, no more than 50 percent of the horizontal roof area may have a slope flatter than 1 vertical to 4 horizontal.
calculation_handling.gaps: No DSL target exists for roof slope or the share of roof area at a given slope, and the rule depends on the as-built status of the building; the numbers are listed as not expressed (closest closed reason).

units.disclosure: If you alter the roof of an existing house in the RD zone, most of the new roof (more than half its area) must keep a slope of at least 1 in 4. We do not check roof slope.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of 18.0 metres or less

calculation_handling.description: Where the required minimum lot frontage is 18.0 m or less, a residential building may be at most 17.0 m long.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of more than 12.0 metres to 18.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: Optional one-storey rear extension of a detached house of up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length (on lots with required frontage over 12.0 m up to 18.0 m): the extended part may be at most 5.0 m high and one storey. The 2.0 m extension length is the stem's permission, recorded under literals_not_expressed as the shared stem value.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit applies only to the optional one-storey extension (up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length); no dsl_target names the extended part (M-102).

units.disclosure: On RD lots needing more than 12.0 m and up to 18.0 m of frontage, a detached house may extend up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length if the extension is no higher than 5.0 m and one storey. We do not model this extension.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of more than 12.0 metres to 18.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: The extended part may be no wider than 50% of the building's width at its widest point.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit applies only to the optional one-storey extension (up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length); no dsl_target names the extended part (M-102).

units.disclosure: On RD lots in the frontage band, the optional one-storey extension may be no wider than 50% of the building's width. We do not model this extension.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of more than 12.0 metres to 18.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: The one-storey extension (up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length) must be at least 3.0 m from each side lot line (RD).
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed on extension_side_setback_m (bound min; Spec 69a M-255): it binds only the extended part, never the whole building. The 2.0 m extension itself and its height, storey and width conditions describe the proposed extension and are not modelled.

units.disclosure: On RD lots in the frontage band, a one-storey extension of up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length must be at least 3.0 m from each side lot line.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of less than 10.0 metres

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of 10.0 metres or greater

On a lot abutting a major street, a townhouse may be up to 19.0 m long.
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires a major-street abutment test for the lot.

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street, an apartment building may be up to 25.0 m long.
calculation_handling.gaps: Apartment buildings are outside MaxBLD building types.

units.disclosure: An apartment building on a major street may be up to 25.0 m long. We do not model apartment buildings, so this limit is not evaluated.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of 18.0 metres or less

calculation_handling.description: Where the required minimum lot frontage is 18.0 m or less, the rear main wall of a detached house or houseplex may be no more than 19.0 m from the required front yard setback (a one-storey extension complying with 10.20.40.20(2) is not counted).
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit is measured from the required front yard setback rather than the front lot line; keyed as building_depth_m. The one-storey extension carve-out is not expressed.

evidence.depth_band: lot depth of 36.0 metres or greater
evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of less than 10.0 metres

evidence.depth_band: lot depth of 40.0 metres or greater
evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of 10.0 metres or greater

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.20.40.20(1), a detached houseplex may have a building depth of up to 19.0 m on a lot at least 40.0 m deep with frontage of 10.0 m or more.

evidence.label_value: in the zone label

evidence.label_value: does not include a "d" value

calculation_handling.description: Where the zone label has no "d" value, floor space index is not limited by this regulation.

evidence.secondary_suite: a residential building with a secondary suite

calculation_handling.description: The FSI limit in (A) and (B) does not apply to a detached houseplex or to a residential building with a secondary suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: The two exempt cases are alternatives (or); condition is left "none" because condition tokens are a conjunction, and the cases are carried in application instead.

calculation_handling.description: The FSI limits do not apply to a townhouse or an apartment building with 60 dwelling units or less on a lot abutting a major street.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 60-unit qualifier is read as applying to the apartment building; the condition grammar cannot scope it to one building type, so it is keyed for both (a townhouse above 60 units is not a realistic case).

calculation_handling.description: A detached house in the RD zone may have at most four platforms (decks or balconies) reached from the second storey or above, and at most one on each of the front, rear and each side.
calculation_handling.gaps: The total (four) is keyed on platform_count (bound max), a platform element target (Spec 69a M-254 / M-255); the one-per-side arm is listed. The platform design itself is a scenario detail.

units.disclosure: Upper-storey decks and balconies on a detached house are limited to four in total and one per side.

calculation_handling.description: Each platform reached from the second storey or above of a detached house in the RD zone may be at most 4.0 square metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to platforms with access from the second storey or above; that is a design fact, not a lot condition.

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot is not subject to lot coverage, the outside sides of a lawfully existing platform that was lawfully enclosed under former City of Toronto By-law 438-86 are not counted as main walls.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the as-built history of a platform enclosure under the former by-law; 'not subject to lot coverage' is read as no Lot Coverage Overlay value (not mapped(LC)).

units.disclosure: An existing platform that was legally enclosed under the old City of Toronto by-law does not count as main walls where no lot coverage applies; we cannot see a building's history, so we do not apply this.

calculation_handling.description: A detached houseplex in the RD zone may have at most 2 platforms reached from the second storey or above for each dwelling unit, with at most one on each of the unit's front and rear sides.
calculation_handling.gaps: No DSL target exists for a count of platforms, so the limits 2 and one are listed as not expressed (closest closed reason; they are count limits); 'second' is the storey ordinal.

units.disclosure: Upper-storey decks and balconies on a houseplex are limited to 2 per unit, one at the front and one at the rear; we do not check the number of platforms.

calculation_handling.description: On a corner lot, a permitted upper-storey platform of a detached houseplex may also be placed on a main wall of a dwelling unit that faces a street.

Minimum rear yard setback is the greater of 7.5 m and 25% of lot depth; this unit carries the 25% of lot depth argument.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage is less than 6.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: Side yard 0.9 m where required frontage is 6.0 m to under 12.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: Side yard 1.2 m where required frontage is 12.0 m to under 15.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: Side yard 1.5 m where required frontage is 15.0 m to under 18.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: Side yard 1.8 m where required frontage is 18.0 m to under 24.0 m.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage is 24.0 metres to less than 30.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: Side yard 2.4 m where required frontage is 24.0 m to under 30.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: Side yard 3.0 m where required frontage is 30.0 m or more.

calculation_handling.description: Optional shift: one side yard may be reduced by up to 0.3 m if the other side yard is increased by the same amount (required frontage 12.0 m to under 18.0 m). The 0.3 m shift is the permitted adjustment to the 10.20.40.70(3) value, not a stand-alone limit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Total side-yard width is unchanged; the split between sides is a design choice we do not evaluate.

units.disclosure: One side yard may be up to 0.3 m narrower if the other side yard is made wider by the same amount (lots needing 12.0 m to under 18.0 m of frontage); the side yard shown is the standard one.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage greater than 18.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: On lots with required frontage over 18.0 m, any part of a building farther back than the lesser of 17.0 m from the front main wall or 19.0 m from the required front yard setback needs a 7.5 m side yard.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to the deep portion of the building; the 17.0 m / 19.0 m depth trigger locates the portion and is not a bound.

units.disclosure: On lots needing more than 18.0 m of frontage, any part of the house more than 17.0 m behind its front wall (or 19.0 m behind the required front setback) needs a 7.5 m side yard.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage greater than 18.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: Same 7.5 m deep-portion side yard as (5)(A); this unit carries the 19.0 m-from-required-front-setback trigger.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to the deep portion of the building.

units.disclosure: On lots needing more than 18.0 m of frontage, any part of the house more than 17.0 m behind its front wall (or 19.0 m behind the required front setback) needs a 7.5 m side yard.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage for the corner lot is 12.0 metres or more

calculation_handling.description: On a corner lot with required frontage of 12.0 m or more and an adjacent lot fronting on the flanking street, the side yard on the street side is at least 3.0 m.

evidence.adjacent_lot_fronts_flanking_street: an adjacent lot fronting on the street

calculation_handling.description: Carries the adjacent-lot condition (B) of the 3.0 m street-side yard; the frontage condition (A) is not in this unit's text.
Townhouse/apartment on a major street: rear yard at least 7.5 m.

evidence.all_units_front_street: all dwelling units front directly onto a street

calculation_handling.description: Townhouse on a major street: side yard 0.9 m if all units front directly onto a street, otherwise 7.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The (ii) 7.5 m arm (units not all fronting a street; token unit_not_fronting_street) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on such a lot the side setback is not_evaluated, never 0.9 m.

calculation_handling.description: Front yard on a major street: lot depth 36.0 m or less: the lesser of the 10.5.40.70(1) setback or 6.0 m where 10.5.40.70(1) applies, else 3.0 m; deeper than 36.0 m: 6.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The through-lot arm (i)(c) (6.0 m) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on a through lot the front setback is not_evaluated, never a guessed value.

calculation_handling.description: Building-length arm modelled over the whole wall; primary-window and corner-lot street-side arms are not expressible.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 5.5 m (wall portions with primary windows) and 7.5 m (wall portions beyond 25.0 m of building length) arms apply to portions of the main wall; they are additive arms the DSL cannot express (M-130). The base is a necessary minimum on every wall.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 2.0 m above-ground separation between facing main walls of the same townhouse or apartment building (major-street lot) where neither wall has openings to dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: The base arm: it applies to every design; the arms that need openings carry the design-choice tokens main_wall_openings (one wall) and main_wall_openings_each (each wall) (M-282), so the smallest separation is answered by default and the larger arms are disclosed. Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 2.0 m between them if neither has openings to dwelling units.

evidence.main_wall_openings: no openings to dwelling units in one of those main walls

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 5.5 m separation between facing main walls of the same building where one of the walls has no openings to dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: The arm applies when the design has the openings to dwelling units the text names: the design-choice token main_wall_openings (M-282; user input main_wall_openings, taken as absent, so the smallest separation is answered and this arm is disclosed). Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 5.5 m between them if one of them has no openings to dwelling units.

evidence.main_wall_openings_each: each main wall has an opening to a dwelling unit

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 11.0 m separation between facing main walls of the same building where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: The arm applies when the design has the openings to dwelling units the text names: the design-choice token main_wall_openings_each (M-282; user input main_wall_openings_each, taken as absent, so the smallest separation is answered and this arm is disclosed). Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 11.0 m between them if each has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 5.5 m separation between main walls of two or more townhouses or apartment buildings on the same major-street lot where one or more of the walls has no openings to dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only where two or more townhouses or apartment buildings on the same lot abutting a major street; no token tests that scope (M-149), and the maximum build has one residential building (M-177(3); M-158 new build), so the 5.5 m separation is disclosed, never bound. Suite-to-house separation is 150.7.60.30(1) / 150.8.60.30(1) (M-177(2), M-187 Q12).

units.disclosure: If the lot abutting a major street has two or more townhouses or apartment buildings: their main walls must be at least 5.5 m apart, or 11.0 m where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum 11.0 m separation between main walls of buildings on the same major-street lot where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: The FSI limits in (A) and (B) do not apply to a detached houseplex, semi-detached houseplex or a residential building with a secondary suite. Displaces 10.40.40.40(1)(A) and (1)(B) for those buildings.
The FSI regulations do not apply to a townhouse or an apartment building with 60 or fewer dwelling units on a lot abutting a major street. Displaces 10.40.40.40(1)(A)-(C).
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires a major-street abutment test; apartment buildings are outside MaxBLD building types.

calculation_handling.description: A detached house in the RS zone may have at most four platforms (decks or balconies) reached from the second storey or above, and at most one on each of the front, rear and each side.
calculation_handling.gaps: The total (four) is keyed on platform_count (bound max), a platform element target (Spec 69a M-254 / M-255); the one-per-side arm is listed. The platform design itself is a scenario detail.

units.disclosure: Upper-storey decks and balconies on a detached house are limited to four in total and one per side.

calculation_handling.description: Each platform with access from the second storey or above of a detached house may be at most 4.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: A semi-detached house may have at most three upper-storey platforms per dwelling unit, and at most one on each of the front, rear and side of the unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: No vocab.dsl_target counts platforms, so this numeric count limit cannot be keyed as a LIMIT; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) and the counts are listed as unexpressed literals. Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: Each upper-storey platform of a semi-detached house may be at most 4.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: A rear upper-storey platform of a semi-detached house must be at least 1.8 m from the common wall dividing the dwelling units (or its projection to a lot line).
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed on separation_m as the nearest target (distance to the common wall between units); no target names a distance from a party wall. Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: A detached or semi-detached houseplex may have at most 2 upper-storey platforms per dwelling unit, and at most one on each of the front and rear of the unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: No vocab.dsl_target counts platforms, so this numeric count limit cannot be keyed as a LIMIT; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) and the counts are listed as unexpressed literals. Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: On a corner lot, a permitted houseplex platform may also be on a main wall of a dwelling unit facing a street.
calculation_handling.gaps: Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum front yard setback of 6.0 m in the RS zone where front-yard averaging (10.5.40.70(1)) does not apply.
Minimum rear yard setback of 7.5 m; one of two minimums, the greater of (A) and (B) governs because both apply independently.
Minimum rear yard setback of 25% of the lot depth; the greater of (A) and (B) governs because both minimums apply independently.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 25 pct literal multiplies a metre-valued variable (lot_depth_m); the grammar has no percentage-of operator, so it is keyed as pct x m.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage

calculation_handling.description: Minimum side yard setback of 0.6 m where the required minimum lot frontage is less than 6.0 m.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage

calculation_handling.description: Minimum side yard setback of 0.9 m where the required minimum lot frontage is 6.0 m to less than 12.0 m.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage

calculation_handling.description: Minimum side yard setback of 1.2 m where the required minimum lot frontage is 12.0 m to less than 15.0 m.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage

calculation_handling.description: Minimum side yard setback of 1.5 m where the required minimum lot frontage is 15.0 m or more.
Minimum side yard setback of 1.8 m for a non-residential building.
Front yard on a major street: lot depth 36.0 m or less: the lesser of the 10.5.40.70(1) setback or 6.0 m where 10.5.40.70(1) applies, else 3.0 m; deeper than 36.0 m: 6.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The through-lot arm (i)(c) (6.0 m) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on a through lot the front setback is not_evaluated, never a guessed value.

calculation_handling.description: Rear yard setback of 7.5 m for a townhouse or apartment building on a lot abutting a major street.
Townhouse side yard setback on a major street: 0.9 m if all dwelling units front directly onto a street, 7.5 m if they do not.
calculation_handling.gaps: The (ii) 7.5 m arm (units not all fronting a street; token unit_not_fronting_street) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on such a lot the side setback is not_evaluated, never 0.9 m.

calculation_handling.description: Apartment building side yard setback on a major street: 2.4 m for main-wall portions without primary windows, 5.5 m for portions with primary windows, 7.5 m for portions exceeding a building length of 25.0 m, and 3.0 m on a corner lot from a side lot line abutting a street.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 5.5 m (wall portions with primary windows) and 7.5 m (wall portions beyond 25.0 m of building length) arms apply to portions of the main wall; they are additive arms the DSL cannot express (M-130). The base is a necessary minimum on every wall.

calculation_handling.description: Where facing main walls of the same townhouse or apartment building have no openings to dwelling units, they must be at least 2.0 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: The base arm: it applies to every design; the arms that need openings carry the design-choice tokens main_wall_openings (one wall) and main_wall_openings_each (each wall) (M-282), so the smallest separation is answered by default and the larger arms are disclosed. Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 2.0 m between them if neither has openings to dwelling units.

evidence.main_wall_openings: no openings to dwelling units in one of those main walls

calculation_handling.description: Where one of the facing main walls of the same townhouse or apartment building has no openings to dwelling units, they must be at least 5.5 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: The arm applies when the design has the openings to dwelling units the text names: the design-choice token main_wall_openings (M-282; user input main_wall_openings, taken as absent, so the smallest separation is answered and this arm is disclosed). Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 5.5 m between them if one of them has no openings to dwelling units.

evidence.main_wall_openings_each: each main wall has an opening to a dwelling unit

calculation_handling.description: Where each facing main wall of the same townhouse or apartment building has an opening to a dwelling unit, they must be at least 11.0 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: The arm applies when the design has the openings to dwelling units the text names: the design-choice token main_wall_openings_each (M-282; user input main_wall_openings_each, taken as absent, so the smallest separation is answered and this arm is disclosed). Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 11.0 m between them if each has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Where two or more townhouses or apartment buildings share a lot on a major street and the main wall of one or more of them has no openings to dwelling units, the buildings must be at least 5.5 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only where two or more townhouses or apartment buildings on the same lot abutting a major street; no token tests that scope (M-149), and the maximum build has one residential building (M-177(3); M-158 new build), so the 5.5 m separation is disclosed, never bound. Suite-to-house separation is 150.7.60.30(1) / 150.8.60.30(1) (M-177(2), M-187 Q12).

units.disclosure: If the lot abutting a major street has two or more townhouses or apartment buildings: their main walls must be at least 5.5 m apart, or 11.0 m where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Where two or more townhouses or apartment buildings share a lot on a major street and each facing main wall has an opening to a dwelling unit, the buildings must be at least 11.0 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only where two or more townhouses or apartment buildings on the same lot abutting a major street; no token tests that scope (M-149), and the maximum build has one residential building (M-177(3); M-158 new build), so the 11.0 m separation is disclosed, never bound. Suite-to-house separation is 150.7.60.30(1) / 150.8.60.30(1) (M-177(2), M-187 Q12).

units.disclosure: If the lot abutting a major street has two or more townhouses or apartment buildings: their main walls must be at least 5.5 m apart, or 11.0 m where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: A parking space inside a building (not an ancillary building) may be converted to interior floor area for a use under 10.40.20.100(19) or (20), with no replacement parking required, if the space is in a residential building other than an apartment building (and (B)-(F) are met).
calculation_handling.gaps: Conversion of existing parking to a non-residential use is outside the MaxBLD build scenario.

units.disclosure: An indoor parking space in a house may be converted to certain non-residential uses without replacement parking, subject to conditions. We do not evaluate this conversion.

evidence.garage_entrance_faces_street: vehicle entrance to the parking space is in the front main wall

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the conversion: the vehicle entrance to the parking space is in the front main wall of the building.

Condition of the conversion: the driveway to the vehicle entrance is removed and any front-yard depression is filled to established grade. Keyed REQUIRE with the nearest requirement token (landscaping_type); the obligation is driveway removal and regrading.
calculation_handling.gaps: No requirement token names driveway removal exactly.

units.disclosure: Converting an indoor parking space to a permitted non-residential use (without replacing the parking) is allowed only if the driveway is removed and the front yard regraded; we do not evaluate this.

calculation_handling.description: The removed driveway area in the front yard must be landscaping, but may still count as a permitted driveway when calculating required soft landscaping under 10.5.50.10(1)(D).

evidence.parking_space: a parking space located in the front yard

calculation_handling.description: A parking space in the front yard or a street-side side yard must be subject to 10.5.80.10(3) or be authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.
Regulation 200.5.10.11(1)(C) does not apply to the parking space being converted. Displaces 200.5.10.11(1)(C) for that space.
States that Section 10.5 applies to every land, use, building and structure in the Residential Zone category; no value is computed.
Explains that the zone symbol letters R, RD, RS, RT or RM indicate the primary land use; interpretive text only.
Defines the zone-label letter f as the required minimum lot frontage in metres; the label value is read by the lot-frontage units of each zone.
Defines the zone-label letter a as the required minimum lot area in square metres; the label value is read by the lot-area units of each zone.
Defines the zone-label letters au as the required minimum lot area for each dwelling unit, in square metres; the label value is read by the townhouse and apartment lot-area units.

evidence.label_value: the letter "u" and a numerical value

calculation_handling.description: Defines the zone-label letter u as the permitted maximum number of dwelling units on a lot; the label value is read by the unit-count units of each zone.
Defines the zone-label letter d as the permitted maximum floor space index for a lot; the label value is the zone FSI read by the FSI units.
Minimum driveway width of 2.0 m in the front yard.
Maximum front-yard driveway width of 2.6 m for lots under 6.0 m frontage or townhouse units under 6.0 m wide.

condition.if: (lot_frontage_m ≥ 6.0 m and lot_frontage_m ≤ 23.0 m) or townhouse_unit_width_m ≥ 6.0 m

calculation_handling.description: Maximum driveway width is the lesser of 6.0 m, the cumulative width of side-by-side spaces, the width of a single space, and 2.6 m if all parking is in the rear yard; modelled as the lesser of 6.0 m and the single parking space width.
calculation_handling.gaps: Cumulative side-by-side parking width and the all-parking-in-rear-yard 2.6 m arm are not modelled; parking width has no Chapter 800 definition.

units.disclosure: The cumulative parking width arm and the 2.6 m arm for lots with all parking in the rear yard are not evaluated; the modelled cap is the lesser of 6.0 m and one parking space width.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum driveway width is the lesser of 9.0 m, the cumulative width of side-by-side spaces behind the front main wall, and 2.6 m if all parking is in the rear yard; modelled as 9.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Cumulative parking width and the all-parking-in-rear-yard 2.6 m arm are not modelled.

units.disclosure: The parking-space-width arm and the 2.6 m arm for lots with all parking in the rear yard are not evaluated; the modelled cap is 9.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum width of 2.0 m for a driveway not in or through the front yard.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a driveway that is not in and does not pass through the front yard (for a townhouse, only a unit with an individual private driveway leading to it). Driveway location is a design choice no token or input carries; as a candidate the bound would reach front-yard driveways (Spec 68 §7.5 rule 4a), so the unit is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A driveway that is not in the front yard (or does not pass through it) must be at least 2.0 m wide. We do not check driveway location, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum width is the lesser of 6.0 m and the width of the parking spaces.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a driveway that is not in and does not pass through the front yard (for a townhouse, only a unit with an individual private driveway leading to it). Driveway location is a design choice no token or input carries; as a candidate the bound would reach front-yard driveways (Spec 68 §7.5 rule 4a), so the unit is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A driveway that is not in the front yard (or does not pass through it) may be no wider than the lesser of 6.0 m or the width of the parking spaces. We do not check driveway location, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Minimum driveway width of 2.0 m for each lane; the lane count is not a model input.
calculation_handling.gaps: Per-lane scaling and the three-or-more-dwelling-units proviso for houseplexes are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum total driveway width of 6.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The three-or-more-dwelling-units proviso for houseplexes is not applied as a condition.

calculation_handling.description: A driveway with two points of vehicle access to the same street is permitted when lot frontage exceeds 18.0 m, and (B) also holds.
calculation_handling.gaps: The front yard landscaping compliance condition in (6)(B) is keyed separately.

calculation_handling.description: The two-access driveway also requires the front yard landscaping to comply with Clause 10.5.50.10.
calculation_handling.gaps: A compliance cross-check on another clause; not a numeric or vocabulary requirement.

units.disclosure: Whether the front yard landscaping complies with Clause 10.5.50.10 is not checked here; it is a condition on the two-access driveway permission.

calculation_handling.description: A hammerhead turnaround driveway is permitted when lot frontage exceeds 18.0 m (alternative to (7)(B)), except for large apartment buildings and subject to front yard landscaping compliance.
calculation_handling.gaps: The apartment building exclusion (more than 60 units on a major street, 25 or more elsewhere) and the landscaping cross-check are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: A hammerhead turnaround driveway is permitted when vehicle access is from a street with a right-of-way at least 27.0 m wide.
calculation_handling.gaps: Street right-of-way width is not a model input.

units.disclosure: Hammerhead turnaround driveways on streets with a right-of-way of at least 27.0 m are not evaluated; right-of-way width is not held.

calculation_handling.description: A hammerhead turnaround has a maximum width of 3.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: No target for the width of a hammerhead turnaround.

units.disclosure: The 3.0 m maximum width of a hammerhead turnaround is not evaluated; there is no model target for it.

calculation_handling.description: A hammerhead turnaround extends no more than 4.5 m from one edge of the driveway.

units.disclosure: The 4.5 m limit on how far a hammerhead turnaround extends from one driveway edge is not evaluated; there is no model target for it.

calculation_handling.description: A hammerhead turnaround extends no more than 3.0 m from each opposite driveway edge.

units.disclosure: The 3.0 m limit on how far a hammerhead turnaround extends from each opposite driveway edge is not evaluated; there is no model target for it.

calculation_handling.description: An expansion of a lawfully existing school must comply with Section 150.48 and the zone requirements; schools are not a modelled building type.
calculation_handling.gaps: School buildings are outside the building types the tool models.

units.disclosure: Expansions or additions to a lawfully existing public or private school must comply with Section 150.48 and the zone requirements. The tool does not evaluate school buildings.

calculation_handling.description: A lawfully existing school may be replaced with a new school building that complies with Section 150.48 and the zone requirements; schools are not a modelled building type.
calculation_handling.gaps: School buildings are outside the building types the tool models.

units.disclosure: A lawfully existing public or private school may be replaced with a new school building that complies with Section 150.48 and the zone requirements. The tool does not evaluate school buildings.

calculation_handling.description: A detached house may be converted to a detached houseplex and stays a lawfully existing building if the additional dwelling units are entirely inside the building as it lawfully existed the day before the building permit.

A portion of a semi-detached house on one lot may be converted to a semi-detached houseplex and stays a lawfully existing building if the additional dwelling units are entirely inside the building as it lawfully existed.
The converted portion of the semi-detached house on one lot is treated as a semi-detached houseplex when applying the by-law standards.
The remaining, unconverted portion of the semi-detached house on the abutting lot is treated as its original building type when applying the by-law standards.

If both dwelling units of a semi-detached house are converted, the building stays a lawfully existing building if the additional dwelling units are entirely inside the building as it lawfully existed.

A portion of a townhouse on one lot may be converted to contain up to four dwelling units and stays a lawfully existing building if the additional dwelling units are entirely inside the building as it lawfully existed.
For the listed envelope regulations, the converted portion of a townhouse may be treated as a duplex, triplex or fourplex despite the Chapter 800 building type definitions.
The unconverted portions of the townhouse on adjacent lots are treated as their original building type when applying the by-law standards.
If more than one dwelling unit of a townhouse is converted, the building as a whole is treated as its lawfully existing original building type.
An addition or extension to a converted lawfully existing building must comply with all other regulations or be authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.
Widens the meaning of lawful and lawfully existing to include buildings, structures or uses authorized or permitted on or before June 26, 2025.
Widens the meaning of lawful and lawfully existing to include buildings for which a building permit was lawfully issued before June 26, 2025.

evidence.lawfully_existing: converted to contain up to four dwelling units

calculation_handling.description: A secondary suite is not permitted in the portion of a semi-detached house or townhouse converted to contain up to four dwelling units.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs to know whether the building was converted under 10.5.20.40(2) or (3). M-196(1): applied in the interior-conversion answer (a converted semi-detached house or townhouse portion takes no secondary suite); M-214(3): a secondary suite in a semi or townhouse is a deferred form, disclosed (forms_deferred).

units.disclosure: A secondary suite is not allowed in a semi-detached house or townhouse converted to hold up to four dwelling units; a secondary suite in a semi or townhouse is not modelled in this release.

calculation_handling.description: Lawful parking spaces may be reduced to add dwelling units if the front or side street yard driveway leading to the space is removed and landscaping is provided.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built driveway and parking facts.

calculation_handling.description: Lawful parking spaces may be reduced to add dwelling units if a front or side street yard parking space is permitted under 10.5.80.10(3) or authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built driveway and parking facts.

calculation_handling.description: Points to the additional lot requirements found in each zone of the Residential Zone category; no value is computed.

No townhouse or apartment building may be erected or used on a lot abutting a major street unless the municipal water mains and sewers have adequate capacity, to the satisfaction of the General Manager, Toronto Water.
calculation_handling.gaps: Water and sewer capacity is a municipal determination, not held in the lot data.

calculation_handling.description: The water main and sewer capacity requirement does not apply to a townhouse or apartment building if the lot will contain 10 or fewer dwelling units, dwelling rooms or bed-sitting rooms.
calculation_handling.gaps: The capacity requirement it exempts from is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The water main and sewer capacity requirement does not apply to an addition of less than 50 square metres of gross floor area to a lawfully existing building on a lot with no more than 10 dwelling units, dwelling rooms and bed-sitting rooms.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the addition size and as-built building facts.

calculation_handling.description: The water main and sewer capacity requirement does not apply to replacing or reconstructing a building damaged by fire, explosion, flood or similar cause, or due to a City order, if gross floor area and height are not increased, no setback is reduced and the use is unchanged.
If the lawful lot area of a lawfully existing lot is below the required minimum lot area, that lawful lot area becomes the minimum for the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the lot area as it lawfully existed, an as-built input.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building on such a lot must comply with all other regulations or be authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.

units.disclosure: An addition to a lawfully existing building on a lot smaller than today's minimum must meet every other rule of the by-law or have a minor variance; the maximum build meets them.

calculation_handling.description: A detached house or detached houseplex may be built on a vacant lot that relies on the lawful lot area, and must comply with all other regulations or get a Section 45 minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the lawful lot area and whether the lot is vacant.

units.disclosure: If this is a vacant lot that lawfully existed with less than today's minimum lot area, a detached house or detached houseplex may be built on it if it meets the rest of the by-law or has a minor variance.

calculation_handling.description: On a through lot, any lot line separating the lot from a street may be selected as the front lot line if it is not separated from the street by a 0.3 metre reserve.
calculation_handling.gaps: The tool does not hold street reserve data. M-228 (operator 2026-10-20): the 0.3 m reserve is a site fact not held, taken as not separating (M-169(1)), so either street line qualifies under (A); the designation itself follows (B).

units.disclosure: On a through lot, a street line separated from the street by a 0.3 m reserve cannot be chosen as the front lot line; no reserve is known for this lot, so none is taken.

calculation_handling.description: On a through lot, any lot line separating the lot from a street may be selected as the front lot line if it abuts a street where an adjacent lot has its front lot line on the same street.
calculation_handling.gaps: The tool does not hold which street each adjacent lot fronts. M-228 (operator 2026-10-20): the front lot line is the street line on which the adjacent lots front, read as the lot's address street (parcels.primary_frontage_street_name); the opposite street line is the rear lot line; applied in the Layer 3 lot-line classification (Spec 78 P5.5), disclosed through_lot_front_line.

units.disclosure: This is a through lot; the front lot line is taken on the street the neighbouring lots face (the lot's address street). If the City sets the other street line as the front, the front and rear setbacks swap.

calculation_handling.description: For a lot with a townhouse or apartment building that abuts a major street, the front lot line is the lot line abutting the major street, overriding the choice in (A) and (B).
calculation_handling.gaps: The tool does not hold which lot lines abut a major street.

calculation_handling.description: A residential building may not be erected on a lot without a front lot line of at least 3.5 metres, unless the lot abuts a lane with a minimum width of 6.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: No modelled target for the length of the front lot line or the width of a lane.

units.disclosure: A residential building cannot be built on a lot whose front lot line is under 3.5 metres, unless the lot abuts a lane at least 6.0 metres wide and meets the rear lot line condition. The tool does not evaluate this test.

calculation_handling.description: The exception to the 3.5 metre front lot line minimum also requires at least 3.5 metres of the rear lot line to abut the lane.
calculation_handling.gaps: No modelled target for the length of lot line abutting a lane.

units.disclosure: The exception for a lot with a short front lot line also requires at least 3.5 metres of the rear lot line to abut the lane. The tool does not evaluate this test.

calculation_handling.description: If the lawful lot frontage of a lawfully existing lot is below the required minimum lot frontage, that lawful lot frontage becomes the minimum for the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the lot frontage as it lawfully existed, an as-built input.

units.disclosure: If this lot lawfully existed with less frontage than today's minimum, that lawful frontage is its minimum lot frontage instead.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building on such a lot must comply with all other regulations or be authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.

units.disclosure: An addition to a lawfully existing building on a lot with less than today's minimum frontage must meet every other rule of the by-law or have a minor variance; the maximum build meets them.

calculation_handling.description: On a vacant lawfully existing lot with a reduced lot frontage, a detached house or detached houseplex is allowed only if the lot frontage is at least 6.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to lots relying on the lawful lot frontage and vacant; needs as-built lot facts.

units.disclosure: If this is a vacant lot that existed before the current rules, a house or detached houseplex may be built on it only if the lot frontage is at least 6.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: The detached house or detached houseplex on such a vacant lot must comply with all other requirements or be authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.

units.disclosure: If this is a vacant lot that existed before the current rules, the house or detached houseplex must also meet the rest of the by-law or have a minor variance.

calculation_handling.description: Any part of a building or structure that is permitted to encroach into a required minimum building setback under Clause 10.5.40.60 is not counted in lot coverage.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the footprint of the permitted encroaching parts.

calculation_handling.description: A platform without main walls, and any roof or canopy above it, is not counted in lot coverage if it is attached to, or less than 0.3 metres from, a building and does not encroach into a required setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the platform footprint and its distance from the building.

calculation_handling.description: The platform exclusion from lot coverage applies only if the lot area covered by these structures is no more than 5% of the lot area.
If lawfully existing buildings cover more of the lot than the permitted maximum lot coverage, the lawful covered portion becomes the maximum lot coverage for those buildings.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the lot coverage as it lawfully existed, an as-built input.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to such lawfully existing buildings must comply with all other regulations or be authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.

units.disclosure: An addition to a lawfully existing building that covers more of the lot than allowed must meet every other rule of the by-law or have a minor variance; the maximum build meets them.

calculation_handling.description: The front yard setback of a townhouse or apartment building on a major street is measured from the lot line abutting the major street if the street has been built to the right-of-way width planned on Map 3 of the Official Plan.
calculation_handling.gaps: The tool does not hold whether the street is built to its planned right-of-way width.

calculation_handling.description: If the major street has not been built to its planned right-of-way width on Map 3, the front yard setback is measured from the lot line as it would be after the right-of-way widening is conveyed.
calculation_handling.gaps: The tool does not hold the planned right-of-way widening.

calculation_handling.description: Scopes Article 10.5.40 to buildings and structures in all residential zones, excluding ancillary buildings or structures, which are governed by Article 10.5.60.
Signpost: each residential zone has additional building requirements of its own.
In the Residential Zone category, building height is the distance from established grade to the highest point of the building.
Antennae on the roof of a building may exceed the permitted maximum height by 1.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop-feature allowance above the height limit; it does not change the building envelope and the 1.5 m is not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: Antennae on the roof may rise up to 1.5 m above the height limit; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Flagpoles on the roof of a building may exceed the permitted maximum height by 1.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop-feature allowance above the height limit; it does not change the building envelope and the 1.5 m is not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: Flagpoles on the roof may rise up to 1.5 m above the height limit; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Parapets for a green roof on the roof of a building may exceed the permitted maximum height by 1.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop-feature allowance above the height limit; it does not change the building envelope and the 1.5 m is not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: Parapets for a green roof may rise up to 1.5 m above the height limit; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Satellite dishes on the roof of a building may exceed the permitted maximum height by 1.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop-feature allowance above the height limit; it does not change the building envelope and the 1.5 m is not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: Satellite dishes on the roof may rise up to 1.5 m above the height limit; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Weather vanes on the roof of a building may exceed the permitted maximum height by 1.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop-feature allowance above the height limit; it does not change the building envelope and the 1.5 m is not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: Weather vanes on the roof may rise up to 1.5 m above the height limit; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Functional rooftop equipment (electrical, utility, mechanical, ventilation) may exceed the permitted maximum height by 5.0 m, skylights by only 1.0 m, subject to 10.5.40.10(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop-equipment allowance above the height limit; not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: Rooftop equipment such as mechanical and ventilation units may rise up to 5.0 m above the height limit (skylights 1.0 m) and cover at most 30% of the roof; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Functional rooftop structures (stairwells, roof access, elevator shafts, chimneys, vents, water supply) may exceed the permitted maximum height by 5.0 m, subject to 10.5.40.10(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop-structure allowance above the height limit; not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: Rooftop stairwells, roof access, elevator shafts, chimneys and vents may rise up to 5.0 m above the height limit and cover at most 30% of the roof; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Structures enclosing or screening the (A) and (B) elements may exceed the permitted maximum height by 5.0 m if the building is taller than 15.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop allowance above the height limit; not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: On a building taller than 15.0 m, screens or enclosures around rooftop equipment may rise up to 5.0 m above the height limit; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Rooftop elements that exceed the height limit under 10.5.40.10(3) may cover no more than 30% of the roof area, measured horizontally.
calculation_handling.gaps: A cap on rooftop equipment area as a share of roof area; no DSL target exists for it and the proposed rooftop layout is not an input.

units.disclosure: Rooftop equipment above the height limit may cover at most 30% of the roof; this is not checked.

calculation_handling.description: Rooftop equipment, structures or parts of a building that exceed the height limit of 10.5.40.10(3) and sit within 6.0 m of a street lot line may total no more than 20% of the width of the main walls facing that street, measured parallel to the street.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to rooftop elements above the height limit within 6.0 m of a street lot line (scope not testable, M-149); no dsl_target names a rooftop element's width share (P4), so the 20% is limit_not_modelled (M-102).

units.disclosure: If you place rooftop equipment or structures above the height limit within 6.0 m of a street lot line, their total width may not exceed 20% of the width of the main walls facing that street. We do not calculate this.

calculation_handling.description: Unenclosed safety or wind-protection structures for rooftop amenity space may exceed the permitted maximum height by 3.0 m if on a building taller than 15.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rooftop allowance above the height limit; not an evaluated bound.

units.disclosure: On a building taller than 15.0 m, open railings or wind screens for a rooftop amenity space may rise up to 3.0 m above the height limit; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Those rooftop amenity safety or wind structures must be no closer than 2.0 m to the interior face of any main wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: A placement condition on a rooftop allowance; the 2.0 m is a wall-to-structure distance with no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Open railings or wind screens for a rooftop amenity space must stay at least 2.0 m inside the main walls; rooftop elements are design details and are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building or structure is taller than the permitted maximum height, its lawful height becomes its maximum height.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built lawful height. The clause states no date for 'lawfully existing'; the existing() date argument is keyed as enacted(569-2013) (conservative reading), and the 'greater than the permitted maximum' test is carried by the lawfully_existing condition because the DSL has no atom comparing an existing value with another unit's limit.

units.disclosure: A building that legally exists and is already taller than today's limit keeps its existing height as its limit. We do not know as-built heights, so this is not applied.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building covered by 10.5.40.11(1) must meet the permitted maximum height, or be authorized by a minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: The unit text names no zone; its scope follows 10.5.40.11(1) (Residential Zone category). The minor-variance arm is outside our evaluation. M-192: an addition meets the permitted maximum height; the renovation answer holds every addition to the base height limit (evaluated), so the clause is met by construction; the minor-variance arm is outside our evaluation.

units.disclosure: Additions to an over-height existing building must meet the normal height limit unless a minor variance is granted.

calculation_handling.description: A roof alteration on a lawfully existing building covered by 10.5.40.11(1) may be built up to that building's lawful (existing) maximum height.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on as-built height and roof facts. The unit text names no zone; its scope follows 10.5.40.11(1).

units.disclosure: A new roof on an over-height existing building may go up to the building's existing lawful height. We do not apply this because we lack as-built heights.

calculation_handling.description: If the lawful height of the front and rear main walls of a lawfully existing building exceeds the permitted maximum main wall height, that lawful height becomes their maximum.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built wall heights. The existing() date argument is keyed as enacted(569-2013) because the clause states no date (conservative reading).

units.disclosure: Existing front and rear walls that are legally taller than today's limit keep their existing height as the limit. We do not know as-built wall heights.

calculation_handling.description: If the lawful height of the side main walls of a lawfully existing building exceeds the permitted maximum main wall height, that lawful height becomes their maximum.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built wall heights. The existing() date argument is keyed as enacted(569-2013) because the clause states no date (conservative reading).

units.disclosure: Existing side walls that are legally taller than today's limit keep their existing height as the limit. We do not know as-built wall heights.

calculation_handling.description: New main walls of an addition to a lawfully existing building covered by 10.5.40.11(4) are subject to the main wall heights in 10.5.40.11(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: Includes 10.5.40.11(4), which depends on as-built wall heights. The unit text names no zone; its scope follows 10.5.40.11(4).

units.disclosure: New walls of an addition may match the existing building's lawful wall heights. We cannot check this without as-built data.

calculation_handling.description: If the lawful height of the first floor above established grade in a lawfully existing building exceeds the permitted maximum, that lawful first floor height becomes its maximum.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built first floor height. The existing() date argument is keyed as enacted(569-2013) because the clause states no date (conservative reading).

units.disclosure: An existing first floor that is legally higher above grade than today's limit keeps that height as its limit. We do not know as-built floor heights.

calculation_handling.description: An addition to a lawfully existing building covered by 10.5.40.11(6) may have a first floor above established grade up to the maximum height in 10.5.40.11(6).
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the as-built first floor height. The unit text names no zone; its scope follows 10.5.40.11(6).

units.disclosure: An addition may match the existing building's lawful first floor height. We cannot check this without as-built data.

calculation_handling.description: Measurement rule: building length regulations apply to all main walls of a building, above and below ground, excluding footings.
Excludes from the building-length measure any part of a building or structure permitted to encroach into a required setback under 10.5.40.60; it sets no length of its own.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-171: a measure exclusion that needs design facts (which encroaching parts exist) is disclosed; the permitted maximum building length is answered unchanged.

units.disclosure: Parts of the building allowed to project into a setback, such as eaves, steps or a porch, are not counted in its length.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building is longer than the permitted maximum building length, its lawful length becomes its maximum building length.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the limit to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT.

units.disclosure: An existing building that is lawfully longer than today's limit may keep its length; we cannot check existing building lengths.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building relying on 10.5.40.21(1) must comply with all other regulations or be authorized by a minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Zones left empty: the unit text names no zone (10.5 = Residential Zone category).

units.disclosure: Additions to a building that relies on its existing length must meet all other rules or get a minor variance.

calculation_handling.description: Measurement rule (procedural, sets no limit): building depth is measured to all main walls of a building, above and below ground, excluding the footings.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-31: an informational measurement rule; it sets no number and changes no answer (as 10.5.40.20(1) for length).

calculation_handling.description: Excludes from the building-depth measure any part of a building or structure permitted to encroach into a required setback under 10.5.40.60; it sets no depth of its own.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-171: a measure exclusion that needs design facts (which encroaching parts exist) is disclosed; the permitted maximum building depth is answered unchanged.

units.disclosure: Parts of the building allowed to project into a setback, such as eaves, steps or a porch, are not counted in its depth.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building is deeper than the permitted maximum building depth, its lawful building depth becomes its maximum.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the as-built building depth. The clause states no date for 'lawfully existing'; the existing() date argument is keyed as enacted(569-2013) (conservative reading).

units.disclosure: A legally existing building that is already deeper than today's limit keeps its existing depth as its limit. We do not know as-built depths.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building covered by 10.5.40.31(1) must comply with all other regulations of the By-law, or be authorized by a minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: The unit text names no zone; its scope follows 10.5.40.31(1) (Residential Zone category). The minor-variance arm is outside our evaluation.

units.disclosure: Additions to an over-deep existing building must meet all the other zoning rules unless a minor variance is granted.

calculation_handling.description: Attic test for a residential building other than an apartment building: attic floor area with more than 1.4 m clearance between the ceiling joists and the roof rafters counts toward GFA if at least 80% of that area has more than 2.0 m clearance (and is at least 10.0 m2, see (B)).
calculation_handling.gaps: Layer 2 answers the attic-test thresholds; whether an attic passes, and its floor area, is Layer 3 geometry from the roof form (Spec 78 P5.2 item 6: gfa_pitched_sqm counts a passing attic, attic_outside_gfa_sqm reports a failing one, M-203).

units.disclosure: An attic that does not meet the headroom and size test is livable but not counted in the City's floor-area total (GFA).

calculation_handling.description: Attic test threshold (B): the qualifying attic area must be at least 10.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: Layer 2 answers the attic-test thresholds; whether an attic passes, and its floor area, is Layer 3 geometry from the roof form (Spec 78 P5.2 item 6: gfa_pitched_sqm counts a passing attic, attic_outside_gfa_sqm reports a failing one, M-203).

units.disclosure: An attic that does not meet the headroom and size test is livable but not counted in the City's floor-area total (GFA).

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: attic area meeting 10.5.40.40(1) that is used for mechanical equipment is excluded from GFA if it is no more than 5% of the permitted maximum GFA, up to 20 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on attic use and geometry. M-229 (operator 2026-10-20, amends M-171): applied by default in the maximum design where the counted attic passes 10.5.40.40(1): min(5 % × permitted maximum GFA, 20 m²) is left out of GFA as mechanical-equipment space (a design choice taken as met, M-172(3); as M-210 for suites), disclosed achieved-if mechanical_attic_excluded; the scenario step applies it (Spec 78 P5.13, owed) and the 5 % / 20 m² are clause literals (keying owed).

units.disclosure: Up to the lesser of 5% of the permitted floor-area total (GFA) or 20 m² of a counted attic is taken as mechanical-equipment space and left out of the GFA; this is achieved if that attic space holds the building's mechanical equipment.

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: GFA of a residential building other than an apartment building may be reduced by the basement floor area.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-171 dated note 2026-10-18: the max build excludes the basement from GFA; Spec 78 P5.4 reports it as livable area with in_gfa: false (P5.12 basement_excluded). The permitted maximum GFA itself is unchanged.

units.disclosure: Your counted floor area may exclude the basement floor area.

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: the area of a floor void with more than 4.5 m clearance may be deducted from GFA, up to 10% of the permitted maximum GFA.

units.disclosure: Your counted floor area may exclude the area of a floor void with more than 4.5 m of clearance, up to 10% of the permitted maximum floor area.

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: the area of up to one parking space per dwelling unit may be deducted from GFA.

units.disclosure: Your counted floor area may exclude the area of up to one parking space per dwelling unit inside the building.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of more than 12.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: a detached house on a lot with frontage over 12.0 m may also deduct the area of one additional parking space.

units.disclosure: Your counted floor area may exclude one more parking space, for a detached house on a lot with more than 12.0 m of frontage.

calculation_handling.description: For a non-residential building, FSI = GFA ÷ lot area.
calculation_handling.gaps: Non-residential buildings are outside MaxBLD building types.
