calculation_handling.description: For a residential building other than an apartment building, FSI = (GFA + qualifying attic area per 10.5.40.40(1), subject to (2), − the deductions in 10.5.40.40(3)) ÷ lot area.
calculation_handling.gaps: The attic additions and the basement/void/parking deductions depend on design details.

units.disclosure: Floor space index counts the gross floor area plus an attic that meets the headroom and size test (less up to 20 m² of mechanical attic space), minus the basement, floor voids and inside parking the by-law lets you leave out; the maximum build leaves out the basement, and the voids and parking depend on the design.

calculation_handling.description: For an apartment building, FSI = (GFA − the areas listed in 10.5.40.40(4)) ÷ lot area.
calculation_handling.gaps: Apartment buildings are outside MaxBLD building types.

calculation_handling.description: If lawfully existing buildings on a lot exceed the permitted maximum floor space index, their lawful FSI becomes the maximum FSI for those buildings.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the limit to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT.

units.disclosure: Existing buildings lawfully built above today's floor space index may keep that floor area; we cannot check existing floor area.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck

calculation_handling.description: The exterior sides of a deck, porch, balcony or similar platform attached to or within 0.3 m of a building are not main walls if at least 50% of the sides above the floor are open.

units.disclosure: The sides of a deck, porch or balcony that are at least 50% open above its floor are not main walls; decks and platforms are not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: A platform without main walls (deck, porch, balcony) attached to or within 0.3 m of a building must meet the zone's required minimum building setbacks: its side, rear and front setbacks are the zone's.
calculation_handling.gaps: An element-scoped reference (Spec 69a M-254): each platform setback target takes the zone's setback for that yard, evaluated on the lot. A platform that uses a permitted encroachment (10.5.40.60(1), "Despite regulation 10.5.40.50(2)") is answered by the encroachment and clearance targets instead. Interim before the structure dimension (S.3): the platform's own floor height and area are not modelled.

units.disclosure: A deck, porch or balcony without main walls must meet the required setbacks.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck or balcony

calculation_handling.description: For a residential building other than an apartment building, a deck or balcony at or above the second storey may be no higher than 0.2 m above the floor of the storey it is accessed from.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.2 m is measured from the accessing floor, not from established grade; the proposed platform is a design detail. Apartment buildings are excluded but the text names no positive building type, so building types are keyed as any.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck or balcony

calculation_handling.description: A deck or balcony at or below the first storey of a residential building other than an apartment building may be no higher than 1.2 m above the ground below it; where attached to or within 0.3 m of a front wall, no higher than 1.2 m above established grade.
calculation_handling.gaps: The proposed platform is a design detail, not a lot input.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck or balcony

calculation_handling.description: A low platform attached to or within 0.3 m of a side main wall may be no higher than the floor level it is accessed from.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit is relative to an interior floor level, which no DSL input carries.

units.disclosure: A deck beside a side wall may be no higher than the floor it is reached from; this is not checked.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck or balcony

calculation_handling.description: For a low platform attached to or within 0.3 m of a rear main wall, any part of its floor within 2.5 m of that wall may be no higher than the floor level it is accessed from.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit is relative to an interior floor level, which no DSL input carries.

units.disclosure: A rear deck within 2.5 m of the house may be no higher than the floor it is reached from; this is not checked.

calculation_handling.description: In a front yard, a platform (deck, porch, balcony) with its floor no higher than the first storey may extend into the required front yard setback by the lesser of 2.5 m or 50% of that setback, if it stays at least the required side yard setback from a side lot line; enclosed space is allowed below it.
calculation_handling.gaps: Front-yard platform with a floor no higher than the first storey: the lesser of 2.5 m or 50 % of the required front yard setback, no closer to a side lot line than the required side yard setback; (ii) enclosed space below needs no number. The element's targets are shared by its front-, rear- and side-yard arms (rule 4a takes the most restrictive across them; a per-yard split is not part of the ruling).

units.disclosure: A front-yard deck or porch no higher than the first storey may extend into the front setback by the lesser of 2.5 m or half the setback, if it keeps the side yard setback from the side lot line.

calculation_handling.description: In a front yard, a platform with its floor higher than the first storey may extend into the required front yard setback by the lesser of 1.5 m or 50% of that setback, if it stays at least the required side yard setback from a side lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: Front-yard platform with a floor above the first storey. The element's targets are shared by its front-, rear- and side-yard arms (rule 4a takes the most restrictive across them; a per-yard split is not part of the ruling).

units.disclosure: A front-yard deck, porch or balcony above the first storey may extend into the front setback by the lesser of 1.5 m or half the setback, if it keeps the side yard setback from the side lot line.

calculation_handling.description: In a rear yard, a platform with its floor no higher than the first storey may extend into the required rear yard setback by the lesser of 2.5 m or 50% of that setback, if it stays from a side lot line at least the greater of 0.3 m or the height of the platform floor above the average ground at its side.
calculation_handling.gaps: Rear-yard platform with a floor no higher than the first storey. The clearance is the greater of (i) 0.3 m or (ii) the platform floor's height above the ground beside it; (ii) has no input, so the clearance answered is 0.3 m, which (ii) may exceed. The element's targets are shared by its front-, rear- and side-yard arms (rule 4a takes the most restrictive across them; a per-yard split is not part of the ruling).

units.disclosure: A rear-yard deck no higher than the first storey may extend into the rear setback by the lesser of 2.5 m or half the setback, if it stays from the side lot line at least the greater of 0.3 m or its floor height above the ground.

calculation_handling.description: In a rear yard, a platform with its floor higher than the first storey may extend into the required rear yard setback by the lesser of 1.5 m or 50% of that setback, if it stays from a side lot line at least the required side yard setback plus the height of the first floor above the average ground along the rear main wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a platform whose floor is at / above the first storey as stated; platform floor height is a design fact with no token or DSL input. The vertical distance between the first floor and the average ground along the rear main wall is approximated by entrance_height_m (first floor above established grade). The 0.3 m in the stem is the applicability test.

calculation_handling.description: In a side yard, a platform with its floor no higher than the first storey may extend up to 1.5 m into the required side yard setback, if it stays at least 0.3 m from the side lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: Side-yard platform with a floor no higher than the first storey. The element's targets are shared by its front-, rear- and side-yard arms (rule 4a takes the most restrictive across them; a per-yard split is not part of the ruling).

units.disclosure: A side-yard deck no higher than the first storey may extend up to 1.5 m into the side setback if it stays at least 0.3 m from the side lot line.

calculation_handling.description: In a side yard, a platform with its floor higher than the first storey may extend up to 1.5 m into the required side yard setback only where the side yard abuts a street; otherwise it may not encroach at all.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only to a platform whose floor is at / above the first storey; platform floor height is a design fact with no token or DSL input. The 1.5 m applies under condition side_yard_abuts_street (M-128); (1)(F)(ii) states no literal: where the side yard does not abut a street the unit does not apply and the required side yard setback stands unreduced. The 0.3 m in the stem is the applicability test.

calculation_handling.description: A roof, canopy, awning or similar structure over a platform that meets 10.5.40.60(1) may encroach into a required setback as far as the platform it covers.
calculation_handling.gaps: The extent follows the covered platform's allowance under 10.5.40.60(1).

calculation_handling.description: A canopy or awning not covering a platform may extend into a required setback: in a front or rear yard by the lesser of 2.5 m or 50% of the setback (keeping the required side yard setback from a side lot line); in a side yard by up to 1.5 m (keeping 0.3 m from the side lot line).
calculation_handling.gaps: A canopy or awning not covering a platform: (i) in a front or rear yard the lesser of 2.5 m or 50 % of that yard's required setback (front and rear arms keyed), no closer to a side lot line than the required side yard setback; (ii) in a side yard 1.5 m, 0.3 m from the side lot line. The element's targets are shared by its front-, rear- and side-yard arms (rule 4a takes the most restrictive across them; a per-yard split is not part of the ruling).

units.disclosure: A canopy or awning not over a deck may extend into a front or rear setback by the lesser of 2.5 m or half the setback (keeping the side yard setback from the side lot line), or up to 1.5 m into a side setback (keeping 0.3 m from the side lot line).

calculation_handling.description: Exterior stairs may encroach into a required setback if they run no more than 1.5 horizontal for each 1.0 vertical, are no wider than 2.0 m, and stay at least 0.6 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.6 m lot-line clearance is keyed on stairs_clearance_m (bound min; Spec 69a M-254, the M-243 declared-bound form). The other conditions of the encroachment (proportion, width, height or area) describe the proposed exterior stairs, a design detail with no target; they are listed as not expressed.

units.disclosure: Exterior stairs may project into a setback if they run no more than 1.5 m for each 1.0 m of rise, are no wider than 2.0 m and stay at least 0.6 m from the lot line.

calculation_handling.description: An uncovered ramp may encroach into a required setback if it runs no more than 15 horizontal for each 1.0 vertical, each sloped segment is no wider than 1.5 m, and it stays at least 0.6 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.6 m lot-line clearance is keyed on ramp_clearance_m (bound min; Spec 69a M-254, the M-243 declared-bound form). The other conditions of the encroachment (proportion, width, height or area) describe the proposed an uncovered ramp, a design detail with no target; they are listed as not expressed.

units.disclosure: An uncovered ramp may project into a setback if it is no steeper than 1 in 15, each sloped part is no wider than 1.5 m and it stays at least 0.6 m from the lot line.

calculation_handling.description: An elevating device may encroach into a required setback if it rises no higher than the first floor, has an area of 3.0 m² or less, and stays at least 0.6 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.6 m lot-line clearance is keyed on elevating_device_clearance_m (bound min; Spec 69a M-254, the M-243 declared-bound form). The other conditions of the encroachment (proportion, width, height or area) describe the proposed an elevating device, a design detail with no target; they are listed as not expressed.

units.disclosure: A lift of up to 3.0 m² that rises no higher than the first floor may project into a setback if it stays at least 0.6 m from the lot line.

calculation_handling.description: Cladding added to the original outside surface of a main wall may extend up to 0.15 m into a required setback, if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: Added cladding on a main wall.

units.disclosure: Added cladding may extend up to 0.15 m into a required setback if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with 100 or more dwelling units, added cladding (including vents, pipes or utility equipment beneath it) may extend up to 0.9 m into a required setback, replacing (A).
calculation_handling.gaps: Lots with 100 or more units are outside the MaxBLD building-type scope; recorded for completeness.

calculation_handling.description: A pilaster, decorative column, cornice, sill, belt course or similar architectural feature may extend up to 0.6 m into a required setback, if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: A pilaster, decorative column, cornice, sill, belt course or similar feature.

units.disclosure: Pilasters, cornices, sills and similar features may extend up to 0.6 m into a required setback if they stay at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: A chimney breast may extend up to 0.6 m into a required setback, if it is no wider than 2.0 m and stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: A chimney breast; its width test (no wider than 2.0 m) is a design detail, not a setback (listed).

units.disclosure: A chimney breast up to 2.0 m wide may extend up to 0.6 m into a required setback if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: A bay window, box window or similar window projection may extend up to 0.75 m into the required front or rear yard setback, if the projections take up no more than 65% of the width of that wall at each storey.
calculation_handling.gaps: The DSL has no yard dimension: each statement applies to the yard named in its cited clause.

units.disclosure: A bay or box window may project up to 0.75 m into the front or rear yard setback if the projections take up no more than 65% of that wall's width at each storey; this is a design detail and is not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: A window projection may extend up to 0.6 m into the required side yard setback, if the projections take up no more than 30% of the width of the side main wall at each storey and stay at least 0.6 m from the side lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: Side-yard window projections: 0.6 m, at most 30 % of the side main wall width per storey, 0.6 m from the side lot line.

units.disclosure: Bay or box windows may extend up to 0.6 m into the side setback if they take up no more than 30% of the side wall at each storey and stay at least 0.6 m from the side lot line.

calculation_handling.description: A dormer may not have any of its walls closer to a lot line than the required minimum building setback (dormers do not encroach).

units.disclosure: No wall of a roof dormer may be closer to a lot line than the required setback; the maximum design keeps dormers inside the setbacks.

calculation_handling.description: Roof eaves may extend up to 0.9 m into a required setback, if they stay at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: Roof eaves: a maximum projection and a lot-line clearance minimum in one LIMIT; each target declares its bound (M-243 amends M-106, the M-239 mechanism).

units.disclosure: Roof eaves may extend up to 0.9 m into a required setback if they stay at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: Wall-mounted vents, pipes or utility equipment may extend up to 0.6 m into the required rear or side yard setback, if they stay at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: Vents, pipes or utility equipment into a rear or side yard setback; the 0.3 m clearance is the (8) lead-in's.

units.disclosure: Wall-mounted vents, pipes or utility equipment may extend up to 0.6 m into a rear or side setback if they stay at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: A wall-mounted satellite dish may extend up to 0.9 m into any required setback, if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: A satellite dish; the 0.3 m clearance is the (8) lead-in's.

units.disclosure: A wall-mounted satellite dish may extend up to 0.9 m into any required setback if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: A wall-mounted antenna or antenna pole may extend up to 0.9 m into the required rear or side yard setback, if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: An antenna or its pole into a rear or side yard setback; the 0.3 m clearance is the (8) lead-in's.

units.disclosure: A wall-mounted antenna may extend up to 0.9 m into a rear or side setback if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: A wall-mounted air conditioner may extend up to 0.9 m into the required rear yard setback, and into the required side yard setback only if it is not above the first storey; it must stay at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: An air conditioner: into a rear yard setback, and into a side yard setback only if not above the first storey (that storey test is a design detail, not keyed); the 0.3 m clearance is the (8) lead-in's.

units.disclosure: A wall-mounted air conditioner may extend up to 0.9 m into the rear setback, or the side setback if not above the first storey, if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.

calculation_handling.description: Public utility metering equipment (such as electric or gas meters) mounted on a wall may extend into any required setback, with no stated maximum, if it stays at least 0.3 m from a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: No maximum encroachment is stated for meters; only the 0.3 m lot-line clearance from the stem is a limit.

units.disclosure: Wall-mounted utility meters may project into any setback if they stay at least 0.3 m from the lot line; this is a design detail and is not modelled.

evidence.one_abutting_building_within_15_m: 15.0 metres or less from the subject lot

calculation_handling.description: Front-yard averaging, one neighbour: where one abutting Residential-zone lot has a building fronting the same street within 15.0 m of the subject lot, the minimum front yard setback equals that building's front yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the neighbouring building's front yard setback and its distance from the lot.

units.disclosure: The front setback averages the neighbouring houses' setbacks, which are estimated; a survey may differ.

calculation_handling.description: Front-yard averaging, two neighbours: where the lot is between two abutting Residential-zone lots, each with a building fronting the same street within 15.0 m, the minimum front yard setback is the average of those two buildings' front yard setbacks (abutting_front_setback_m read as the average of the abutting buildings).
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs both neighbouring buildings' front yard setbacks and distances.

units.disclosure: The front setback averages the neighbouring houses' setbacks, which are estimated; a survey may differ.

calculation_handling.description: A building or structure must be at least 2.5 m from the original centreline of a lane.
calculation_handling.gaps: Measured from the original lane centreline, not the lot line; needs lane centreline geometry.

units.disclosure: A building must stay at least 2.5 metres from the original centreline of a lane. We do not hold lane centreline geometry, so we do not evaluate this.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building or structure is closer to the front lot line than the required minimum, its lawful setback is its minimum front yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT. M-192: a lawfully-existing setback relief; it needs the existing building position, so it is disclosed, never applied (as (1)(B), (1)(C)).

units.disclosure: A lawfully existing building that sits closer to the front lot line than today's minimum keeps that front setback; this needs the existing building's position, so it is disclosed, not calculated.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building or structure is closer to the rear lot line than the required minimum, its lawful setback is its minimum rear yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT.

units.disclosure: Existing buildings that lawfully sit closer to a lot line than today's rules allow keep that setback; we cannot check existing building positions.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building or structure is closer to a side lot line than the required minimum, its lawful setback is its minimum side yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT.

units.disclosure: Existing buildings that lawfully sit closer to a lot line than today's rules allow keep that setback; we cannot check existing building positions.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building relying on 10.5.40.71(1) must meet the required minimum setbacks or be authorized by a minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Zones left empty: the unit text names no zone (10.5 = Residential Zone category).

units.disclosure: Additions to a building that relies on its existing setbacks must meet the current setbacks or get a minor variance.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of 12.2 metres or less

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with frontage of 12.2 m or less, an addition above a lawfully existing building may use the lawful existing setbacks permitted by 10.5.40.71(1).
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT. Zones left empty: the unit text names no zone. M-192 / M-211(1): the one lawfully-existing relief applied in the renovation answer — on a lot of 12.2 m or less the up-addition keeps the existing footprint setbacks (setbacks only; the depth and length caps still bind), achieved if the house is lawfully existing (disclosed addition_above_existing).

units.disclosure: On a lot of 12.2 m or less, an addition above the house keeps its setbacks (achieved if the house is lawfully existing).

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with frontage under 9.0 m, a rear or side addition to a lawfully existing building may use the existing lawful side yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT. Zones left empty: the unit text names no zone. M-211(5) / M-192: a renovation rule for side or rear additions to a lawfully existing building; it needs the existing side-wall position, so it is disclosed, never applied.

units.disclosure: For a side or rear addition to a lawfully existing building on a lot under 9.0 m wide, the side yard may stay at the existing building's; this is a renovation rule and is not calculated.

numeric_expression: side_setback_m = max(50 pct × side_setback_m; existing(side_setback_m; enacted(569-2013))) @(4)(B)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with frontage of 9.0 m to 12.2 m, the side setback for a rear or side addition to a lawfully existing building is the greater of 50% of the required minimum side yard setback or the existing lawful side setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT. The 50% applies to the zone's required side yard setback (a cross-referenced value). Zones left empty: the unit text names no zone. M-211(5) / M-192: a renovation rule for side or rear additions to a lawfully existing building; it needs the existing side-wall position, so it is disclosed, never applied.

units.disclosure: For a side or rear addition to a lawfully existing building on a lot 9.0 m to 12.2 m wide, the side yard is the larger of half the normal side yard or the existing one; this is a renovation rule and is not calculated.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building or structure is closer to the original centreline of a lane than required, that lawful distance is its minimum distance from the lane centreline.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT.

units.disclosure: Existing buildings that lawfully sit closer to a lot line than today's rules allow keep that setback; we cannot check existing building positions.

calculation_handling.description: An addition above a lawfully existing building may keep the lawful existing distance from the original lane centreline permitted by 10.5.40.71(5).
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the minimum to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT. Zones left empty: the unit text names no zone.

units.disclosure: Building up over an existing building near a lane may keep its existing distance from the lane; we cannot check this.

calculation_handling.description: On narrow lots (frontage under 6.0 metres) or townhouse dwelling units under 6.0 metres wide, the whole front yard except a permitted driveway or parking pad must be landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: No percentage is stated, so no landscaping share is computed.

condition.if: (lot_frontage_m ≥ 6.0 m and lot_frontage_m < 15.0 m) or townhouse_unit_width_m ≥ 6.0 m

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of 6.0 metres to less than 15.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: For lots with 6.0 to under 15.0 metres of frontage, or townhouse dwelling units at least 6.0 metres wide, at least 50 percent of the front yard must be landscaping.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of 15.0 metres or greater

calculation_handling.description: For lots with 15.0 metres or more of frontage, at least 60 percent of the front yard must be landscaping.

At least 75 percent of the required front yard landscaping must be soft landscaping; if the lot has no permitted front yard driveway, at least 75 percent of the whole front yard must be soft landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 75 percent is applied to the required landscaping share (or to the whole front yard when there is no driveway); the base is not separated in the expression.

calculation_handling.description: On a corner lot, at least 60 percent of the side yard abutting a street must be landscaping.
At least 75 percent of the side yard landscaping required in (A) must be soft landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: No modelled target for the soft landscaping share of a side yard abutting a street.

units.disclosure: On a corner lot, at least 75 percent of the required side yard landscaping must be soft landscaping. The tool does not evaluate this share.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage is greater than 6.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with a residential building other than an apartment building, at least 50% of the rear yard must be soft landscaping if the lot frontage is greater than 6.0 metres.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage is 6.0 metres or less

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with a residential building other than an apartment building, at least 25% of the rear yard must be soft landscaping if the lot frontage is 6.0 metres or less.
The landscaping and soft landscaping calculations exclude the setback area covered by permitted encroachments and the area covered by public utility equipment.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the footprint of permitted encroachments and utility equipment.

calculation_handling.description: For the soft landscaping required by 10.5.50.10(3) and (4), the water surface area of outdoor swimming pools and similar water features counts as soft landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the water surface area of pools and similar features.

calculation_handling.description: Scope: Article 10.5.60 applies to ancillary buildings or structures in the Residential Zone category that are ancillary to dwelling units or residential buildings.
An ancillary building in the Residential Zone category may not be used for living accommodation.
calculation_handling.gaps: Living accommodation is not a vocab.uses token, so the prohibited use is described here rather than keyed. Whether an ancillary building is used for living accommodation is a design/use fact we do not evaluate.

units.disclosure: An accessory building (such as a garage or shed) in a residential zone cannot be used as living space. We do not check how an accessory building will be used.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building in the Residential Zone category may have both food preparation facilities and sanitary facilities if it is for indoor amenity space required by the By-law.
calculation_handling.gaps: Facilities and amenity-space purpose are design facts with no vocab token; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: An accessory building used as required indoor amenity space may have both a kitchen and washroom facilities. We do not check accessory building fit-out.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building in the Residential Zone category used for any purpose other than required indoor amenity space may have either food preparation facilities or sanitary facilities, but not both.
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed PERMIT (the clause grants either facility); its 'but not both' limb is a restriction on the same permission and is described here, not keyed as a separate PROHIBIT. Design facts with no vocab token; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: Any other accessory building may have a kitchen or washroom facilities, but not both. We do not check accessory building fit-out.

calculation_handling.description: In the Residential Zone category, no above-ground part of an ancillary building or structure may be erected before the main walls and roof of a residential building on the same lot are erected and completed.
calculation_handling.gaps: A construction-sequencing rule; it constrains timing, not the built envelope, and is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: An accessory building cannot be built above ground before the house on the same lot has its main walls up and roof completed. This is a construction-timing rule we do not evaluate.

calculation_handling.description: In the Residential Zone category, an ancillary building or structure may not be located in a front yard.
calculation_handling.gaps: A siting rule for a proposed ancillary building; we do not place ancillary buildings, so it is shown as information.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.10(1), public utility equipment essential to the building's operation (such as an electrical transformer or equipment to connect to public utilities) may be located in the front yard.
calculation_handling.gaps: Public utility equipment has no vocab.uses or building_type token. The unit text names no zone (the Residential Zone category is named only in (1)), so zones is left empty for lack of an evidence phrase. Displaces 10.5.60.10(1) for this equipment only.

calculation_handling.description: Measurement rule: required minimum ancillary building setbacks apply to all parts of an ancillary building or structure above and below ground, excluding footings.
calculation_handling.gaps: Inclusion rule for setback measurement; no DSL variable defined.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.10(1), a ground-mounted heating or air-conditioning device may be located in a front yard if it is at least 6.0 metres from the front lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: The device's own target (energy_device_front_setback_m, M-281) answers for the device; it never limits the house's front setback. Whether a device is placed in the front yard is a design fact.

units.disclosure: A ground-mounted heating or air-conditioning unit may sit in the front yard if it is at least 6.0 m from the front lot line.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(3)(A), a ground-mounted heating or air-conditioning device may be in a side yard if it is no closer to the side lot line than the lesser of 0.9 m or the required minimum side yard setback for the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The device's own target (energy_device_side_clearance_m, M-281) answers for the device; side_setback_m is the residential building's required side yard (the blank_side_wall design choice, M-259, applies to it). Whether a device is placed in a side yard is a design fact.

units.disclosure: A ground-mounted heating or air-conditioning unit in a side yard must be at least 0.9 m (or the house's side setback, if less) from the side lot line.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(2) and (3), an open platform (at least 50% of its exterior sides above the floor open, and no closer than 0.3 m to the residential building) has a minimum rear and side yard setback equal to the greater of (A) 0.3 m or (B) its floor height above the ground; this unit carries the 0.3 m argument.
calculation_handling.gaps: The other greater-of argument is unit (11)(B). Mixed targets (rear and side) in one unit. The 50% openness and the stem's 0.3 m separation-from-building qualifier are not expressible conditions.

units.disclosure: Open decks must be set back from the rear and side lot lines by at least 0.3 m or their floor height, whichever is greater; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: The second greater-of argument for an open platform's minimum rear and side yard setback: a distance equal to the highest vertical distance between any part of the platform floor and the ground below it.
calculation_handling.gaps: The platform floor height above the ground below it has no licensed DSL variable (proposed_height_m / platform_height_m are not licensed by this text), so no expression is written. Applies to both rear and side setbacks.

units.disclosure: Open decks must be set back from the rear and side lot lines by at least their floor height above the ground, if more than 0.3 m; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: On a through lot where a residential building on an adjacent lot fronts on the street abutting the rear lot line, an ancillary building's minimum rear yard setback equals the required minimum front yard setback for the residential building on the adjacent lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The value is the adjacent lot's required front yard setback, which has no DSL variable (abutting_front_setback_m is the actual setback and is not licensed by this text), so no numeric expression could be written. The adjacent-lot-fronts-rear-street condition has no vocab token.

units.disclosure: On a through lot, a shed or garage must be set back from the rear street as far as the neighbour's required front setback; not evaluated.

condition.if: (lot_depth_m > 45 m and proposed_height_m > 2.5 m) or (lot_depth_m > 45 m and ancillary_floor_area_m2 > 10 m2)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot deeper than 45 m, an ancillary building taller than 2.5 m or with floor area over 10 square metres has a minimum rear yard setback equal to half its height.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'half' is written as 0.5 ratio (word numeral). The floor-area test uses interior_floor_area_m2 (a target used as a variable) for 'floor area'; no floor-area band token exists. Ancillary building height and floor area are scenario values. Subject to 10.5.60.20(5).

units.disclosure: Larger sheds or garages on deep lots must be set back from the rear lot line by half their height; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: In cases other than (2)(A) and (2)(B), the minimum rear yard setback for ancillary buildings or structures is 0.3 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'Other cases' is the residual of (A) and (B); the residual cannot be written as a condition, so condition is none. Subject to 10.5.60.20(5).

units.disclosure: Sheds and other ancillary buildings generally need a 0.3 m rear setback; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building or structure in a side yard has the same minimum side yard setback as the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The value is the residential building's own side_setback_m; writing side_setback_m = side_setback_m on the same target is circular, so no expression is written. Subject to 10.5.60.20(6) and (7).

units.disclosure: A shed or garage in a side yard needs the same side setback as the house; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building in a rear yard and less than 1.8 m from the residential building has the same minimum side yard setback as the residential building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Value equals the residential building's side_setback_m (same target, circular), so no expression; the rear-yard location is a placement input.

units.disclosure: A shed close to the house (under 1.8 m) in the rear yard needs the house's side setback; not evaluated.

numeric_expression: side_setback_m = if(required_lot_frontage_m ≥ 21.0 m and (proposed_height_m > 2.5 m or ancillary_floor_area_m2 > 10 m2); 0.5 ratio × proposed_height_m; 0.3 m) @(3)(C)

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building in a rear yard and 1.8 m or more from the residential building: (i) on a corner lot where an adjacent residential building fronts the flanking street, set back from that street side lot line by the adjacent building's required front yard setback; (ii) on a lot with required minimum lot frontage of 21.0 m or more, if taller than 2.5 m or over 10 square metres floor area, a side setback of half its height; (iii) otherwise 0.3 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Arm (i) (corner lot, adjacent lot fronting the flanking street; value is the adjacent building's required front setback) has no DSL variable and is not expressed. 'half' written as 0.5 ratio; floor area read as interior_floor_area_m2.

units.disclosure: Sheds farther than 1.8 m from the house generally need a 0.3 m side setback, or half their height for larger ones on wide lots; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(2), (3) and (5) to (11), an ancillary building or structure may be no closer than 2.5 metres from the original centreline of a lane.
calculation_handling.gaps: Measured from the original lane centreline, not the lot line; lane_setback_m is measured from the lot line, so evaluation needs the lane's original width, which we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Sheds and garages must stay at least 2.5 m from the original centreline of a lane; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building containing a parking space, where the rear lot line abuts a lane and vehicle access is from the lane, has a minimum rear yard setback of 1.0 metres, subject to 10.5.60.20(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: Vehicle access from the lane is a design input with no separate token.

units.disclosure: A rear garage entered from a lane needs a 1.0 m rear setback (and 2.5 m from the lane centreline); not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building containing a parking space on a through lot with vehicle access from the street abutting the rear lot line has a minimum rear yard setback of the greater of the adjacent lot's required front yard setback or 6.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Arm (i), the adjacent lot's required front yard setback, has no DSL variable, so only the 6.0 m arm is expressed (a lower bound of the true max).

units.disclosure: A garage on a through lot entered from the rear street needs at least 6.0 m rear setback, or the neighbour's front setback if larger; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building containing a parking space, where a side lot line abuts a lane and vehicle access is from the lane, has a minimum building setback of 1.0 metres from that side lot line, subject to 10.5.60.20(4).
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed to lane_setback_m (setback from a lot line abutting a lane). Vehicle access from the lane is a design input.

units.disclosure: A garage entered from a lane along the side needs a 1.0 m setback from that side lot line; not evaluated.

evidence.garage_entrance_faces_street: vehicle access is from the street

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building containing a parking space on a corner lot with vehicle access from the street abutting the side lot line has a minimum side yard setback of 6.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Read as the setback from the side lot line abutting the street (side_setback_street_m). Vehicle access from the flanking street is a design input (garage_entrance_faces_street, kept out of the condition because it is a design choice).

units.disclosure: A garage on a corner lot entered from the side street needs a 6.0 m setback; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(3) and (6), an ancillary building containing parking spaces for dwelling units on abutting lots may be located on the common side lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: A shared garage straddling two lots is a design choice we do not model.

units.disclosure: A garage shared with the neighbouring lot may sit on the common side lot line; not evaluated.

evidence.detached_house: residential building other than an apartment building
evidence.semi_detached_house: residential building other than an apartment building
evidence.detached_houseplex: residential building other than an apartment building
evidence.semi_detached_houseplex: residential building other than an apartment building
evidence.townhouse: residential building other than an apartment building

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(2), on a lot with a residential building other than an apartment building, an outdoor pool or other water structure has a minimum rear yard setback of 25.0 m on a through lot where an adjacent lot fronts the rear street, 3.0 m on a corner lot where an adjacent lot fronts the flanking street, 1.2 m otherwise, and none if the water surface area is 1.0 square metres or less.
calculation_handling.gaps: The arms are selected by through_lot / corner_lot plus adjacent-lot frontage, which an expression cannot test, so the three values are listed per arm and must not be applied together. The 1.0 m2 water-area exemption has no DSL variable. 'Other than an apartment building' is keyed as the non-apartment residential types.

units.disclosure: Pools need a rear setback of 1.2 m, or more on through and corner lots; tiny water features (1 m2 or less) are exempt; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(2), on a lot with an apartment building an outdoor pool or water structure has a minimum rear yard setback of 7.5 m on a through lot, 4.5 m otherwise, and none if the water surface area is 3.0 square metres or less.
calculation_handling.gaps: Arms selected by through_lot are listed per arm (not to be applied together); the water-area exemption has no DSL variable.

units.disclosure: Pools on apartment lots need a 4.5 m rear setback (7.5 m on through lots); not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(3), on a lot with a residential building other than an apartment building, a pool or water structure has a minimum side yard setback of the greater of 1.2 m or the side setback required by 10.5.60.20(3); on a corner lot, the residential building's required side yard setback plus 1.5 m from the side lot line abutting a street; none if the water surface area is 1.0 square metres or less.
calculation_handling.gaps: Arm (i) is max(1.2 m; the 10.5.60.20(3) ancillary side setback), whose second argument has no DSL variable, so only 1.2 m is expressed. Arm (ii) applies only on a corner_lot, which a unit-wide condition cannot scope to that statement. Water-area exemption has no DSL variable.

units.disclosure: Pools need at least 1.2 m side setback, more on the street side of a corner lot; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(3), on a lot with an apartment building a pool or water structure has a minimum side yard setback of 4.5 m, 7.5 m from a side lot line abutting a street on a corner lot, and none if the water surface area is 3.0 square metres or less.
calculation_handling.gaps: The corner-lot arm is a different target and applies only on a corner_lot; the water-area exemption has no DSL variable.

units.disclosure: Pools on apartment lots need a 4.5 m side setback (7.5 m on the street side of a corner lot); not evaluated.

evidence.building_height_band: with a height greater than 2.5 metres

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building or structure taller than 2.5 m or larger than 10 m2 GFA must be at least 1.8 m from a residential building on the same lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The condition is a disjunction of a height test (proposed_height_m of the ancillary building) and a GFA test (gfa_m2 of the ancillary building); there is no GFA band token, so only building_height_band is listed. The heights and GFAs of proposed ancillary structures are scenario values.

calculation_handling.description: A ground-mounted heating or air-conditioning device in the rear yard may be no more than 2.0 m from the rear main wall of the residential building.
calculation_handling.gaps: separation_m is normally a minimum between buildings; here it is a maximum distance between a device and the rear main wall, the nearest vocab target. building_types any: "the residential building" names no type. Equipment placement is not part of the envelope calculation.

calculation_handling.description: Measurement rule: in the Residential Zone category, the height of an ancillary building or structure is measured from average grade (not established grade) to its highest point.
calculation_handling.gaps: Defines height_m for ancillary buildings/structures only; the measurement base is average grade, which differs from the established-grade base of principal-building height. Not a Chapter 800 row, so input_fidelity is not keyed.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum height 2.5 m for an ancillary building or structure in the Residential Zone category located less than 1.8 m from the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: distance_to_residential_m is a scenario value (where the ancillary building is placed); with no placement the arm cannot be selected.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum height 4.0 m for an ancillary building or structure in the Residential Zone category in all other cases (located 1.8 m or more from the residential building).
calculation_handling.gaps: 'In all other cases' is the complement of (2)(A); the 1.8 m threshold does not occur in this unit's text, so no condition is keyed and the lower 2.5 m max of (2)(A) governs where its condition holds.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building or structure in the Residential Zone category may not have more than one storey.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit is written as the word 'one'; keyed as the numeral 1 storeys.

calculation_handling.description: The top of an entrance into an ancillary building or structure in the Residential Zone category may be at most 2.5 m above the average elevation of the ground along the entrance.
calculation_handling.gaps: No DSL target fits: entrance_height_m is the elevation of a main pedestrian entrance / first floor above established grade, not the height of the top of an ancillary-building entrance (e.g. a garage door) above the ground along it. Keyed UNUSUAL; the 2.5 is the limit itself and no literal_not_expressed_reason fits exactly (threshold_used_in_application is the closest closed value).

units.disclosure: The top of a door or opening into a garage, shed or other accessory building can be no more than 2.5 m above the ground along that entrance. We do not check entrance heights.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck

calculation_handling.description: In the Residential Zone category, a platform (deck or similar structure, other than a green roof) may not be located on top of any ancillary building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Platform placement is a design fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A deck or similar platform (other than a green roof) cannot be built on top of a garage, shed or other accessory building. We do not check platform placement.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck

calculation_handling.description: In the Residential Zone category, a platform (other than a green roof) more than 1.2 m above the ground at any point below it may not be attached to an ancillary building or structure containing a parking space.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 1.2 m test is on the platform's height above the ground below it; no lot_condition threshold token reads platform height, so it is not keyed as condition.if. Design fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A deck or platform more than 1.2 m above the ground cannot be attached to a garage or other accessory building that holds a parking space. We do not check deck placement.

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: the gross floor area of ancillary buildings is not counted in a lot's total gross floor area or floor space index.
calculation_handling.gaps: Also affects gfa_m2 (total gross floor area); fsi is named as the defined variable.

evidence.frontage_band: a lot frontage of 12.0 metres or more

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with frontage of 12.0 m or more, the total floor area of all ancillary buildings or structures (excluding outdoor pools and other water-holding structures) is at most 60.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: The text says 'total floor area' (not 'interior floor area' or 'gross floor area'); interior_floor_area_m2 is the closest target. It is a total across all ancillary buildings on the lot, not per building. Outdoor swimming pools are excluded from the total.

calculation_handling.description: In all other cases (lot frontage under 12.0 m), the total floor area of all ancillary buildings or structures (excluding outdoor pools) is at most 40.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'in all other cases' is the complement of (2)(A); the condition's 12.0 m threshold is taken from (2)(A), as this clause states no number for it. interior_floor_area_m2 is the closest target for 'total floor area'.

units.disclosure: "In all other cases" means every lot not covered by (A) — a lot with a lot frontage of less than 12.0 metres: there the total floor area of all ancillary buildings or structures may not exceed 40.0 square metres. Not evaluated (no floor-area target).

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building or structure located less than 1.8 m from a residential building on the lot may have a floor area of at most 10.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: The distance to the residential building is a scenario value (distance_to_residential_m); the limit applies per ancillary building, not as a lot total. interior_floor_area_m2 is the closest target for 'floor area'.

calculation_handling.description: The eaves of a roof on an ancillary building may encroach up to 0.3 metres into the required minimum building setback in 10.5.60.20, if the eaves are no closer than 0.15 metres to a lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: The eaves of an ancillary building.

units.disclosure: Eaves on a shed or garage may project up to 0.3 m into the setback but must stay 0.15 m from the lot line; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Ancillary buildings and structures (other than the water surface of pools, fountains and ponds) are included in the overall lot coverage calculation.
calculation_handling.gaps: Inclusion rule for the lot coverage measurement; the area of proposed ancillary structures is a scenario value.

calculation_handling.description: The area covered by all ancillary buildings and structures may not exceed 10% of the lot area.

evidence.secondary_suite: a residential building with a secondary suite
evidence.semi_detached_houseplex: semi-detached houseplex or a residential building

calculation_handling.description: The 10% ancillary coverage limit in (1)(B) does not apply on a lot with a detached or semi-detached houseplex or a building with a secondary suite, if overall lot coverage of all buildings does not exceed 45% of the lot area.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 45 percent overall-coverage test is a condition on the disapplication; there is no lot-coverage band token, so it is recorded as threshold_used_in_application rather than a condition.if. The houseplex / secondary-suite arms are alternatives (or), so has_secondary_suite is in application only.

units.disclosure: If all buildings on the lot together cover no more than 45 % of it, the limit on ancillary building coverage does not apply to a lot with a houseplex or a secondary suite.

calculation_handling.description: The water surface area of an outdoor swimming pool, fountain or artificial pond is not included in the lot coverage calculation.
The water surface area of pools, fountains and ponds may not exceed 15% of the lot area.
calculation_handling.gaps: lot_coverage_pct here is the water surface area as a share of lot area (nearest vocab target); the text writes "15%".

units.disclosure: On a lot with an apartment or non-residential building, a wind device may be 3.0 metres above the permitted height if that height is under 24.0 metres or the lot abuts another Residential Zone category lot, and 5.0 metres above it otherwise. The tool does not compute this.
