Where the RM zone label carries an "f" value, that value is the required minimum lot frontage in metres.

numeric_expression: required_lot_frontage_m = by_type(detached_house: 12.0 m; detached_houseplex: 12.0 m; semi_detached_house: 15.0 m; non_residential_building: 24.0 m) @(1)(B)

calculation_handling.description: Where the RM zone label has no "f" value, the required minimum lot frontage is 12.0 m for a detached house or detached houseplex, 15.0 m for an entire semi-detached house, and 24.0 m for an apartment building on a lot not abutting a major street or for a non-residential building.
calculation_handling.gaps: The (iii)(a) apartment arm (24.0 m, only on a lot not abutting a major street) is a lot-condition branch by_type cannot carry (M-107): for an apartment building the frontage is not_evaluated, never 24.0 m on a major-street lot.

calculation_handling.description: For a semi-detached house or apartment building on two lots, and for a semi-detached houseplex, the required minimum lot frontage for each lot is 50% of the requirement in (A) or (B).
calculation_handling.gaps: M-181(3): binds the semi-detached houseplex at 50 % of the (A) / (B) requirement (label f, or the no-f 15.0 m); the link that sets (A) and (B) aside for it is derived from the clause text (Spec 68 §6, "percent of the requirements cited in"). A semi-detached house (RM: or apartment building) on two lots is a site fact, disclosed (M-174(1)).

units.disclosure: If the semi-detached house is divided onto two lots: each lot's minimum lot frontage is 50 % of the requirement.

evidence.no_individual_private_driveway: does not have an individual private driveway

calculation_handling.description: For a townhouse on a lot abutting a major street where every unit fronts directly on a street, the required minimum lot frontage is 6.0 m for each dwelling unit, reduced by 1.0 m for each unit without an individual private driveway leading to its front.
calculation_handling.gaps: Answered under no_individual_private_driveway (M-176(1), build more): 5.0 m per dwelling unit. The number of dwelling units in the block is a Layer 3 scenario value (M-160); with a driveway for each unit the frontage is 6.0 m per unit (disclosed).

units.disclosure: The frontage assumes no townhouse unit has its own driveway: 5.0 m per unit (20 m for 4 units). If each unit has its own driveway to the front, it needs 6.0 m per unit (24 m for 4 units).

evidence.unit_not_fronting_street: not fronting directly on a street

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street with a townhouse having one or more units not fronting directly on a street, the required minimum lot frontage is 30.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Whether any unit does not front a street is a design fact with no lot-condition token for the negative case; it needs user input.

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot has a value on the Lot Coverage Overlay Map, that value is the maximum lot coverage as a percentage of lot area.
Where the lot has no value on the Lot Coverage Overlay Map, no lot coverage limit applies (unregulated).
On a lot abutting a major street, the maximum lot coverage for a townhouse or apartment building is 50 percent of the lot area, replacing (A).
calculation_handling.gaps: Unlike the RS text, this clause says 'despite (A)' only, not (A) and (B).

evidence.secondary_suite: a residential building with a secondary suite

calculation_handling.description: Where the Lot Coverage Overlay value is below 45 percent and the lot has a detached houseplex, a semi-detached houseplex or a residential building with a secondary suite, the maximum lot coverage for all buildings and structures on the lot is 45 percent.
calculation_handling.gaps: The building-type / secondary-suite arm is a disjunction (houseplex OR any residential building with a secondary suite); it is carried in application, not as a conjunctive condition token. The limit covers all buildings and structures on the lot, not only the principal building.

calculation_handling.description: Scope: Article 10.80.40 applies to buildings and structures in the RM zone, except ancillary buildings or structures, which are governed by Article 10.5.60.

evidence.label_value: the letter "u"

calculation_handling.description: Where the zone label has a 'u' value, that value is the maximum number of dwelling units on the lot.
An apartment building on a lot abutting a major street may have the greater of 60 units or the label 'u' value.
calculation_handling.gaps: Apartment buildings are outside MaxBLD building types.

units.disclosure: An apartment building on a major street may have up to 60 units, or more if the zone label allows. We do not model apartment buildings, so this is not evaluated.

evidence.no_individual_private_driveway: does not have an individual private driveway

calculation_handling.description: Each townhouse dwelling unit must be at least 5.0 m wide where it has no individual private driveway leading directly to its front.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only under no_individual_private_driveway (design choice). By M-176(1) (build more) no individual private driveway is assumed, so this 5.0 m is answered; (B) 6.0 m is the disclosed trade-off (vocab design_choice_disclosure.default_overrides).

units.disclosure: Townhouse unit width is 5.0 m per unit without an individual private driveway, 6.0 m with one.

calculation_handling.description: Each townhouse dwelling unit must be at least 6.0 m wide in all other cases (i.e. where it has an individual private driveway to its front).
calculation_handling.gaps: Driveway layout is a design input.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets principal building requirements for a detached house, a detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot is subject to them.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the Chapter 900 exception content; 'only residential building on a lot' has no vocabulary token.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets principal building requirements for a semi-detached house, a semi-detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot is subject to them for the portion that is one dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the Chapter 900 exception content.

calculation_handling.description: Where a base regulation in 10.80.40.10 or 10.80.40.40 for a detached or semi-detached houseplex is more permissive than the exception-derived requirement under 10.80.40.1(4), the more permissive base regulation prevails.
calculation_handling.gaps: Ranking applies only to clauses 10.80.40.10 and 10.80.40.40 and the houseplex types.

calculation_handling.description: A two-unit houseplex may have at most four bedrooms per dwelling unit (8 in total).
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the proposed unit and bedroom counts.

calculation_handling.description: A houseplex with three or more units may have at most three bedrooms per dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the proposed unit and bedroom counts.

calculation_handling.description: Counting rule: a bachelor dwelling unit counts as one bedroom for (A) and (B).
Transition: a lawfully existing houseplex may exceed the bedroom maximum in (6), provided no bedrooms are added after June 26, 2025 that would increase the non-compliance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs as-built bedroom counts and lawful-existing status.

units.disclosure: An existing houseplex built lawfully may keep more bedrooms than the current limit, as long as none are added after June 26, 2025. We cannot verify existing buildings, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Transition: a houseplex built under a building permit issued after June 26, 2025 may exceed the bedroom maximum if it has no more bedrooms per unit than an approval (zoning certificate, rezoning, minor variance or site plan) applied for on or before June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs application and permit history we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Projects with planning approvals applied for on or before June 26, 2025 may keep their approved bedroom counts. We do not hold application history, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: For a building relying on the (B) transition, no bedrooms may be added after the permit if they would increase the non-compliance beyond what that permit established.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs permit history and as-built bedroom counts.

units.disclosure: A building that relies on the bedroom transition rule may not add bedrooms beyond its permit. We do not hold permit history, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: 'Lawful / lawfully existing' also covers buildings, structures or uses authorized or permitted on or before June 26, 2025 and for which a building permit was lawfully issued before that date. The text says 'For the purposes of regulation 10.80.40.1(8)' (a self-reference); read conservatively as supporting the transition rule in 10.80.40.1(7), matching the parallel 10.40.40.1(9).
calculation_handling.gaps: Apparent cross-reference defect in the source text (self-reference to (8)).

calculation_handling.description: Defines 'request for a zoning certificate' by reference to Municipal Code Chapter 363, Article I.
Defines 'complete application for a zoning by-law amendment' by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
Defines 'complete application for a minor variance' by reference to O. Reg. 200/96, Section 2.
Defines 'complete application for site plan approval' by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
The maximum height of a building or structure in the RM zone is the HT value on the Height Overlay Map.

numeric_expression: height_m = by_type(detached_house: 10.0 m; semi_detached_house: 10.0 m; other: 12.0 m) @(1)(B)

evidence.overlay_mapped: no numerical value following the letters

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot has no HT value on the Height Overlay Map, the maximum height is 10.0 m for a detached or semi-detached house and 12.0 m for any other building or structure.
calculation_handling.gaps: Building types list "any" alongside the named types because (1)(B)(ii) covers "any other building or structure" (the by_type other arm).

calculation_handling.description: For a detached or semi-detached houseplex, the maximum height is the greater of the HT value and 10.0 m.

numeric_expression: height_m = by_type(townhouse: max(13.0 m; overlay(HT)); apartment_building: max(19.0 m; overlay(HT))) @(1)(D)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street, the maximum height is the greater of 13.0 m or HT for a townhouse, and the greater of 19.0 m or HT for an apartment building.

For a detached or semi-detached house, the maximum height of the exterior portion of main walls is the higher of 7.0 m above established grade or 2.5 m less than the maximum height in 10.80.40.10(1), applied to all side main walls for at least 70 percent of each side wall's width (option A).
calculation_handling.gaps: Main-wall height is an envelope limit (M-176(2)): the storey above max(7.0 m; H − 2.5 m) is a roof storey in the Spec 78 §Phase-5 max-build pass. Which pair takes the limit (all side walls for 70 % of their width, or the front and rear walls for the frontage-tier share) is a design choice the maximum build makes (P5.12 main_wall_pair). The subject is per zone (M-190): RM names a detached or semi-detached house only, so an RM houseplex or townhouse has no main-wall cap; RT has no main-wall rule (M-186).

units.disclosure: Main walls may be no higher than the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m less than the permitted maximum height, on either all side main walls (for at least 70% of each side main wall's width) or all front and rear main walls (for at least the share of their total width the clause sets by lot frontage); the design chooses which pair.

numeric_expression: main_wall_front_rear_share_pct = band(lot_frontage_m; ≥ 12.0 m: 60 pct; > 7.5 m and < 12.0 m: 50 pct; ≤ 7.5 m: 40 pct) @(2)(B)

calculation_handling.description: Option (B): the same main wall height limit applied to all front and rear main walls for at least 60 / 50 / 40 percent of their total width, by lot frontage (12.0 m or more / over 7.5 m and under 12.0 m / 7.5 m or less).
calculation_handling.gaps: Main-wall height is an envelope limit (M-176(2)): the storey above max(7.0 m; H − 2.5 m) is a roof storey in the Spec 78 §Phase-5 max-build pass. Which pair takes the limit (all side walls for 70 % of their width, or the front and rear walls for the frontage-tier share) is a design choice the maximum build makes (P5.12 main_wall_pair). The subject is per zone (M-190): RM names a detached or semi-detached house only, so an RM houseplex or townhouse has no main-wall cap; RT has no main-wall rule (M-186).

units.disclosure: Main walls may be no higher than the higher of 7.0 m or 2.5 m less than the permitted maximum height, on either all side main walls (for at least 70% of each side main wall's width) or all front and rear main walls (for at least the share of their total width the clause sets by lot frontage); the design chooses which pair.

calculation_handling.description: The main wall height limits in (2)(A) and (2)(B) do not apply to townhouses or apartment buildings on a lot abutting a major street.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-190: on a lot abutting a major street the x.40.10(2) main-wall cap does not apply to the forms named; those forms are not modelled in the maximum build (M-214(1)) and the lot carries major_street_forms_not_modelled.

units.disclosure: On a major street an apartment building (up to 60 units) or a townhouse may be permitted with larger limits; not modelled here.

calculation_handling.description: The maximum number of storeys is the ST value on the Height Overlay Map.

evidence.overlay_mapped: no numerical value following the letters

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot has no ST value, the number of storeys is not limited by this regulation.
The ST storey limit in (3)(A) does not apply to a detached or semi-detached houseplex.

numeric_expression: height_storeys = by_type(townhouse: max(4 storeys; overlay(ST)); apartment_building: max(6 storeys; overlay(ST))) @(3)(D)

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street (excluding a mechanical penthouse), the maximum storeys are the greater of four or ST for a townhouse and the greater of six or ST for an apartment building.
calculation_handling.gaps: "four" and "six" are written as words; keyed as 4 storeys and 6 storeys.

calculation_handling.description: For a detached or semi-detached house, the lowest point of a main pedestrian entrance through the front wall or a side main wall may be no higher than 1.2 m above established grade.
calculation_handling.gaps: The entrance elevation is a design choice (M-172, restrictive): disclosed, never a bound on the build answer (M-174).

units.disclosure: The main front entrance may be no more than 1.2 m above the ground level the City measures from (established grade).

calculation_handling.description: On a detached or semi-detached house of two or more storeys, dormer walls are not main walls if the dormer face is in a roof directly above a part of a main wall that does not exceed the maximum main wall height (and (B) is met).
calculation_handling.gaps: Dormer geometry is a design input we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Dormer walls do not count as main walls if each dormer face sits in a roof directly above a part of a main wall within the main wall height limit; the design chooses the dormers.

calculation_handling.description: For dormer walls not to count as main walls, the total width of dormer faces may be no more than 40 percent of the width of the main wall parts within the main wall height limit, measured at the uppermost storey below the roof.
calculation_handling.gaps: M-185: the maximum build takes the dormers at this 40 % share of the main-wall width (the design chooses the dormers, M-176(3)); the share feeds the Spec 78 §Phase-5 roof-storey area (P5.12 dormers_at_max). Kept DEFINE: the clause decides whether dormer walls count as main walls.

units.disclosure: Dormer walls do not count as main walls if the dormer faces total no more than 40% of the width of the main walls below them that are within the main wall height limit; the design chooses the dormers.

evidence.flat_or_shallow_roof: slope of less than 1.0 vertical units for every 10.0 horizontal units
evidence.semi_detached_house: semi-detached house in the RM zone

calculation_handling.description: With a flat or shallow roof (slope under 1.0 vertical to 10.0 horizontal over more than 50 percent of the roof area), main walls may rise above the main-wall height limit if the front and rear main walls above it are set back at least 1.4 m from the front and rear main walls below. Only the storey above the limit is set back; the storeys below are unchanged.
calculation_handling.gaps: The roof form is the builder's choice (flat_or_shallow_roof, M-172(3)); Layer 3 computes both roof forms and headlines the larger (M-184).

units.disclosure: The top storey is set back 1.4 m from the front and rear walls.

calculation_handling.description: Maximum building length for a detached house or semi-detached house in the RM zone is 17.0 m.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of more than 12.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: Where the required minimum lot frontage exceeds 12.0 m, a detached or semi-detached house may extend up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length if the extended part is no higher than 5.0 m and one storey.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit applies only to the optional one-storey extension (up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length); no dsl_target names the extended part (M-102).

units.disclosure: On RM lots needing more than 12.0 m of frontage, a house may extend up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length if the extension is no higher than 5.0 m and one storey. We do not model this extension.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of more than 12.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: The one-storey extension may be no wider than 50% of the width of the dwelling unit at its widest point.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit applies only to the optional one-storey extension (up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length); no dsl_target names the extended part (M-102).

units.disclosure: On RM lots in the frontage band, the optional one-storey extension may be no wider than 50% of the building's width. We do not model this extension.

evidence.required_frontage_band: required minimum lot frontage of more than 12.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: The one-storey extension (up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length) must be at least 3.0 m from each side lot line (RM).
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed on extension_side_setback_m (bound min; Spec 69a M-255): it binds only the extended part, never the whole building. The 2.0 m extension itself and its height, storey and width conditions describe the proposed extension and are not modelled.

units.disclosure: On RM lots in the frontage band, a one-storey extension of up to 2.0 m beyond the maximum building length must be at least 3.0 m from each side lot line.

calculation_handling.description: On a lot abutting a major street, maximum building length for a townhouse is 19.0 m.
On a lot abutting a major street, maximum building length for an apartment building is 25.0 m.

In the RM zone, the rear main wall of a detached or semi-detached house may be no more than 19.0 m from the required minimum front yard setback (maximum building depth), not counting a one-storey extension that complies with 10.80.40.20(2).
calculation_handling.gaps: The one-storey rear extension allowance (10.80.40.20(2)) is keyed in that regulation, not here.

evidence.label_value: the letter "d" in the zone label

calculation_handling.description: Maximum FSI is the 'd' value in the zone label.

evidence.label_value: does not include a "d" value

calculation_handling.description: Where the zone label has no 'd' value, FSI is not limited by this regulation.

evidence.secondary_suite: a residential building with a secondary suite

calculation_handling.description: The FSI limits in (A) and (B) do not apply to a detached houseplex, semi-detached houseplex or a residential building with a secondary suite. Displaces 10.80.40.40(1)(A) and (1)(B) for those buildings.
The FSI regulations do not apply to a townhouse or an apartment building with 60 or fewer dwelling units on a lot abutting a major street. Displaces 10.80.40.40(1)(A)-(C).
calculation_handling.gaps: Requires a major-street abutment test; apartment buildings are outside MaxBLD building types.

calculation_handling.description: A detached house in the RM zone may have at most four platforms (decks or balconies) reached from the second storey or above, and at most one on each of the front, rear and each side.
calculation_handling.gaps: The total (four) is keyed on platform_count (bound max), a platform element target (Spec 69a M-254 / M-255); the one-per-side arm is listed. The platform design itself is a scenario detail.

units.disclosure: Upper-storey decks and balconies on a detached house are limited to four in total and one per side.

calculation_handling.description: Each platform with access from the second storey or above of a detached house may be at most 4.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: A semi-detached house may have at most three upper-storey platforms per dwelling unit, and at most one on each of the front, rear and exterior side of the unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: No vocab.dsl_target counts platforms, so this numeric count limit cannot be keyed as a LIMIT; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) and the counts are listed as unexpressed literals. Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: Each upper-storey platform of a semi-detached house may be at most 4.0 m2.
calculation_handling.gaps: Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: A rear upper-storey platform of a semi-detached house must be at least 1.8 m from the common wall dividing the dwelling units (or its projection to a lot line).
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed on separation_m as the nearest target (distance to the common wall between units); no target names a distance from a party wall. Platform design (count, area, position) is a scenario detail we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Rules for upper-storey decks and balconies are not checked; confirm them with your designer.

calculation_handling.description: Where front yard averaging in 10.5.40.70(1) does not apply, the minimum front yard setback in the RM zone is 6.0 m.
Minimum rear yard setback in the RM zone is at least 7.5 m (the greater of this and (B)).
Minimum rear yard setback in the RM zone is at least 25% of the lot depth (the greater of this and (A)).
Minimum side yard setback in the RM zone is 1.2 m for detached house or detached houseplex.
Minimum side yard setback in the RM zone is 1.5 m for semi-detached house or semi-detached houseplex.
Minimum side yard setback in the RM zone is 2.4 m for apartment building or non residential building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Non-residential buildings are outside the MaxBLD building types; the apartment building arm is modelled.

calculation_handling.description: Front yard on a major street: lot depth 36.0 m or less: the lesser of the 10.5.40.70(1) setback or 6.0 m where 10.5.40.70(1) applies, else 3.0 m; deeper than 36.0 m: 6.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The through-lot arm (i)(c) (6.0 m) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on a through lot the front setback is not_evaluated, never a guessed value.

calculation_handling.description: On a major street, a townhouse or apartment building needs a minimum rear yard setback of 7.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The unit text names no zone (the zone is implied only by its Section 10.80 placement), so application zones are left empty for want of an evidence phrase.

calculation_handling.description: On a major street, a townhouse needs a side yard setback of 0.9 m if all units front directly onto a street, or 7.5 m otherwise.
calculation_handling.gaps: The (ii) 7.5 m arm (units not all fronting a street; token unit_not_fronting_street) is a lot-condition branch the DSL cannot express (M-107): on such a lot the side setback is not_evaluated, never 0.9 m.

calculation_handling.description: On a major street, an apartment building needs a side yard setback of 2.4 m, 7.5 m for the wall beyond 25.0 m of building length, and 3.0 m from a street side lot line on a corner lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 2.4 m (i) is the side yard. The 5.5 m (ii) applies only to portions of the main wall that have primary windows: a design choice, taken as walls without primary windows (Spec 69a M-249, the M-197 form); if a portion of the main wall has primary windows, its side yard setback is 5.5 m. The 7.5 m (iii) is the deep-portion setback (deep_side_setback_m) for the wall beyond 25.0 m of building length, not a whole-building side yard (M-205(2) form). The unit text names no zone (the zone is implied only by its Section 10.80 placement), so application zones are left empty for want of an evidence phrase.

calculation_handling.description: Where facing main walls of the same apartment building or townhouse include one or more walls with no openings to dwelling units, they must be at least 5.5 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: The base arm: it applies to every design; the arms that need openings carry the design-choice tokens main_wall_openings (one wall) and main_wall_openings_each (each wall) (M-282), so the smallest separation is answered by default and the larger arms are disclosed. Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 5.5 m between them if one or more of them has no openings to dwelling units.

evidence.main_wall_openings_each: each main wall has an opening to a dwelling unit

calculation_handling.description: Where each facing main wall of the same apartment building or townhouse has an opening to a dwelling unit, they must be at least 11.0 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: The arm applies when the design has the openings to dwelling units the text names: the design-choice token main_wall_openings_each (M-282; user input main_wall_openings_each, taken as absent, so the smallest separation is answered and this arm is disclosed). Separation is measured between main walls of the same building where a perpendicular line from one intercepts the other.

units.disclosure: Facing main walls need 11.0 m between them if each has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Where two or more residential buildings are on the same lot and the main wall of one or more of them has no openings to dwelling units, the buildings must be at least 5.5 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only where two or more residential buildings on the same lot; no token tests that scope (M-149), and the maximum build has one residential building (M-177(3); M-158 new build), so the 5.5 m separation is disclosed, never bound. Suite-to-house separation is 150.7.60.30(1) / 150.8.60.30(1) (M-177(2), M-187 Q12).

units.disclosure: If the lot has two or more residential buildings: their main walls must be at least 5.5 m apart, or 11.0 m where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Where two or more residential buildings are on the same lot and each facing main wall has an opening to a dwelling unit, the buildings must be at least 11.0 m apart above ground.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only where two or more residential buildings on the same lot; no token tests that scope (M-149), and the maximum build has one residential building (M-177(3); M-158 new build), so the 11.0 m separation is disclosed, never bound. Suite-to-house separation is 150.7.60.30(1) / 150.8.60.30(1) (M-177(2), M-187 Q12).

units.disclosure: If the lot has two or more residential buildings: their main walls must be at least 5.5 m apart, or 11.0 m where each wall has an opening to a dwelling unit.

evidence.lawfully_existing: lawfully existing buildings on the same lot

calculation_handling.description: Where the lawful separation between main walls of lawfully existing buildings on the same lot (or of one lawfully existing building) is less than the By-law requires, that existing distance becomes the minimum for those walls. Keyed PERMIT (relief for existing conditions) rather than LIMIT because the value is the as-built distance and the clause names no date for an existing() expression.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs as-built separation distances and lawful-existing status.

units.disclosure: Lawfully existing buildings in the RM zone may keep their existing wall separations even if these are less than now required. We cannot measure existing buildings, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Any addition or extension to a lawfully existing building or structure covered by 10.80.40.81(1) must meet the required main-wall separation or be authorized by a Section 45 minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs as-built facts about the existing building.

units.disclosure: Additions to such existing buildings must meet current separation rules or get a minor variance. This is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: A parking space inside a building (not an ancillary building) on an RM lot may be converted to interior floor area for a use under 10.80.20.100(21) or (22), with no replacement parking, if it is in a residential building other than an apartment building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Building types: "any" because the clause names only an exclusion (other than an apartment building); the exclusion is not expressible as a token. Depends on an existing in-building parking space.

calculation_handling.description: Within a detached house, semi-detached house or townhouse, each dwelling unit may have at most one secondary suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: A maximum count of secondary suites per dwelling unit, but vocab.dsl_target has no suites-per-unit target, so it is keyed as a PERMIT of up to one suite and the 'one' is listed as an application threshold rather than a LIMIT expression. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: Each dwelling unit may have at most one secondary suite; the house-with-suite answer has exactly one.

calculation_handling.description: A secondary suite is permitted within a lawfully existing detached house, semi-detached house or townhouse in the RA, RAC, CL, CR, I, IH, IE, IS and IPW zones (where those building types are not otherwise permitted).
calculation_handling.gaps: The named zones (RA, RAC, CL, CR, I, IH, IE, IS, IPW) are not in vocab.zone, so zones is empty; the unit does not apply in the R, RD, RS, RT or RM zones. Depends on an existing building's lawful status.

calculation_handling.description: The interior floor area of a secondary suite, or of all secondary suites together, must be no more than 45 percent of the interior floor area of the dwelling unit in which it is located.
calculation_handling.gaps: The bound is 45 percent of the whole house interior floor area (suite included), M-199; the house interior is the principal's maximum build, a Layer 3 quantity (Spec 78 P5.10 suite_interior_sqm, owed to step commit ①), not a DSL input, so no expression is written and 45 percent stays a clause literal. No zone is named (Chapter 150 applies wherever a secondary suite is permitted).

units.disclosure: A secondary suite may take up to 45% of the interior floor area of the house it is in, the suite included; if the City reads 45% against the main unit only, the suite is smaller.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.10.40.40(1), a secondary suite in the basement of a one-storey detached house may occupy the whole basement.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the 45 percent cap of (1) for this case. 'One storey' is a fact about the house (current_stories) with no condition token; the basement location is a design input.

units.disclosure: In a one-storey detached house, a basement secondary suite may take the whole basement.
