calculation_handling.description: For Chapter 150.7 (garden suites), "lawful" and "lawfully" also include anything existing or authorized on or before February 3, 2022.
calculation_handling.gaps: The date February 3, 2022 is a date and not keyed as a literal. The defined term is not a DSL variable. garden_suite evidence is the chapter scope phrase; the chapter applies to garden suites per 150.7.1(1).

units.disclosure: For garden suites, a building or use that existed or was authorized on or before February 3, 2022 counts as lawfully existing.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(2), an ancillary building may be used for living accommodation in one garden suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Overrides the 10.5.60.1(2) prohibition on living accommodation in ancillary buildings, for one garden suite. No zone is named.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(3), an ancillary building may have both food preparation facilities and sanitary facilities in a garden suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Overrides the 'not both' limb of 10.5.60.1(3) for a garden suite. Interior fit-out is a design fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A garden suite may have both a kitchen and washroom facilities. We do not check interior fit-out.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(4), above-ground parts of an ancillary building containing a garden suite may be erected before the main walls and roof of the residential building on the same lot are erected and completed.
calculation_handling.gaps: Overrides the construction-timing prohibition of 10.5.60.1(4) for an ancillary building containing a garden suite; a sequencing rule, not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A garden suite building may be built before the main house on the lot is finished. This is a construction-timing rule we do not evaluate.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.5.60.1(1), a home occupation is permitted in a garden suite that is exclusively and separately occupied as a principal residence, applying Section 150.5 as if the garden suite were a dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Home occupation is not a vocab.uses token; the dwelling_unit token records the 'as if it is a dwelling unit' treatment. Occupancy (principal residence) is not a lot fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A home business may operate in a garden suite that is someone's principal residence, under the home occupation rules in Section 150.5. We do not evaluate home occupations.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.13.20.1(1), a short-term rental is permitted in an ancillary building if it is in a garden suite that is exclusively and separately occupied as a principal residence.
calculation_handling.gaps: Short-term rental is not a vocab.uses token. Occupancy (principal residence) is not a lot fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A short-term rental is allowed in a garden suite that is someone's principal residence. We do not evaluate short-term rental use.

calculation_handling.description: A maximum of one ancillary building containing either a garden suite or a laneway suite is permitted on a lot, and a lot may not contain both a garden suite and a laneway suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit is written 'a maximum of one'; keyed as the numeral 1 units. The second sentence (a lot may not contain both a garden suite and a laneway suite) is a prohibition carried by this same unit; it is described here rather than split into a separate unit.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of greater than 6.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.50.10(3), on a lot with a residential building and a garden suite, where the lot frontage is greater than 6.0 m, at least 50% of the area behind the residential building's rear main walls, across the full lot width, must be soft landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only when a garden suite is proposed or present (user input). The measured area is the area between the rear main walls and the rear lot line across the full lot width, which is close to but not identical to the rear yard targeted by rear_soft_landscaping_pct. Displaces 10.5.50.10(3) for garden-suite lots. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: With a garden suite, at least half of the backyard area behind the house must be soft landscaping (grass, plants) on lots wider than 6.0 m. We apply this only when you tell us a garden suite is planned.

evidence.frontage_band: lot frontage of 6.0 metres or less

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.50.10(3), on a lot with a residential building and a garden suite, where the lot frontage is 6.0 m or less, at least 25% of the area behind the residential building's rear main walls, across the full lot width, must be soft landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies only when a garden suite is proposed or present (user input). The measured area differs slightly from the rear yard targeted by rear_soft_landscaping_pct. Displaces 10.5.50.10(3) for garden-suite lots. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: With a garden suite on a lot 6.0 m wide or less, at least a quarter of the backyard area behind the house must be soft landscaping. We apply this only when you tell us a garden suite is planned.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 5.10.40.70(2), required minimum ancillary building setbacks apply to all parts of an ancillary building containing a garden suite above and below ground, excluding footings.
calculation_handling.gaps: Measurement inclusion rule; no DSL variable. No zone named.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(2) and (5) and 10.10.60.20(1), on a lot deeper than 45.0 m the minimum rear yard setback of a garden suite building is the greater of 1.5 m or half its height.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'half' written as 0.5 ratio; proposed_height_m is the garden suite building's height (a scenario value).

calculation_handling.description: In all other cases (lot depth 45.0 m or less) the minimum rear yard setback of a garden suite building is 1.5 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'In all other cases' is the residual of (A); its threshold literal is not in this clause, so condition is none (on deep lots (A) is never less than 1.5 m, so no conflict).

calculation_handling.description: If the rear lot line abuts a lot in the Residential Zone category and the garden suite building has openings such as windows in its rear main wall above 4.0 m above average grade, the (B) rear yard setback of 1.5 m is increased by 1.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Scope not tested (M-149): the rear lot line abutting a Residential-zone lot, and rear-wall openings above 4.0 m (a design choice, suite_wall_openings). Restrictive (raises the (B) 1.5 m by 1.5 m), so it is disclosed, never applied to the maximum (M-172(3), M-177(3)). The first 1.5 m is the (B) value being increased.

units.disclosure: If the garden suite has openings such as windows in its rear main wall more than 4.0 m above average grade and the rear lot line abuts a residential lot: the minimum rear yard setback is 3.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: On a through lot where a residential building on an adjacent lot fronts on the street abutting the rear lot line, the garden suite building's minimum rear yard setback equals the required minimum front yard setback for the residential building on the adjacent lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The adjacent-lot fact is taken as holding (M-176, larger setback); abutting_front_setback_m is the lot's own Layer 2 front_setback_m, supplied by the step (Spec 69a M-198(1); Spec 78 P5.13). With no input the answer is not_evaluated:missing_input.

units.disclosure: On a through lot, a garden suite must be set back from the rear street as far as the neighbour's required front setback; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: In all other cases of the through-lot rule, the garden suite building's minimum rear yard setback is 1.5 metres.
For a garden suite building with a parking space on a through lot with vehicle access from the rear street, one argument of the greater-of is the rear yard setback required by 150.7.60.20(3)(A).
calculation_handling.gaps: Cross-reference arm to (3)(A) (the adjacent lot's required front setback), which has no DSL variable. Vehicle access from the rear street is a design input.

units.disclosure: A garden suite with parking on a through lot, entered from the rear street, needs at least the neighbour's required front setback or 6.0 m; not evaluated.

evidence.garage_entrance_faces_street: vehicle access is from the street abutting the rear lot line

calculation_handling.description: For a garden suite building with a parking space on a through lot with vehicle access from the rear street, the minimum rear yard setback is the greater of the (3)(A) setback or 6.0 metres; this unit carries the 6.0 m argument.
calculation_handling.gaps: Vehicle access from the rear street and the parking space are design inputs; the other max() argument is unit (4)(A).

units.disclosure: If the garden suite contains a parking space entered from the street behind a through lot: its rear yard setback is at least 6.0 m.

numeric_expression: side_setback_m = max(1.5 m; min(10 pct × lot_frontage_m; 3.0 m)) @(5)(A)

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(3) and (6) and 10.10.60.20(1), where the side lot line does not abut a street and the side main wall has openings such as doors or windows, the garden suite's minimum side yard setback is the greater of 1.5 m or 10 percent of the lot frontage, to a maximum of 3.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Scope not tested (M-149): a side lot line not abutting a street, and openings in the side main wall (a design choice, suite_wall_openings). Restrictive (a 1.5 m floor instead of (B)'s 0.6 m), so it is disclosed, never applied to the maximum (M-172(3), M-177(3)); (B) answers. 'To a maximum of 3.0 metres' read as capping the 10 percent amount.

units.disclosure: If the garden suite has doors or windows in a side main wall facing a side lot line that does not abut a street: that side yard setback is at least the greater of 1.5 m or 10% of the lot frontage, to a maximum of 3.0 m.

numeric_expression: side_setback_m = max(0.6 m; min(10 pct × lot_frontage_m; 3.0 m)) @(5)(B)

calculation_handling.description: In all other cases, the garden suite's minimum side yard setback is the greater of 0.6 m or 10 percent of the lot frontage, to a maximum of 3.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Residual of (A) (no openings, or the side abuts a street); selection between (A) and (B) needs the wall-openings input.

evidence.adjacent_lot_fronts_flanking_street: adjacent lot fronts on the street

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(3)(C)(i), on a corner lot where a residential building on an adjacent lot fronts the flanking street, the garden suite's minimum side yard setback is the average of the adjacent building's front yard setback and the principal building's minimum required side yard setback, but never less than 1.5 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: The averaging arm ((abutting_front_setback_m + side_setback_m) / 2) needs a divisor literal that is not in the text, so only the 1.5 m floor is expressed; the true value may be higher. Keyed to side_setback_street_m because the side lot line abuts a street.

units.disclosure: On a corner lot next to a house facing your side street, a garden suite's street-side setback is an average of the neighbour's front setback and your house's side setback (at least 1.5 m); we only check the 1.5 m floor.

calculation_handling.description: On a corner lot, a garden suite building containing a parking space with vehicle access from the flanking street has a minimum side yard setback of the greater of 6.0 m or the (A) setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: Only the 6.0 m argument is expressed; the (A) argument is carried by unit (6)(A). Parking space and flanking-street access are design inputs.

units.disclosure: If the garden suite on a corner lot contains a parking space entered from the side street: its side yard setback on that street is at least 6.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: In all other corner-lot cases, the garden suite's minimum side yard setback is the greater of the required minimum side yard setback for the residential building on the lot or 1.5 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: The other max() argument is the residential building's side_setback_m, the same target name as this unit's, so it cannot be written without circularity; only 1.5 m is expressed. Condition corner_lot read from the stem heading 'Garden Suite on Corner Lot' and the (A)/(B) context.

calculation_handling.description: Where a lawfully existing ancillary building is closer to the lot line than 150.7.60.20 requires, a garden suite in it may keep that building's existing rear yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: Could be read as LIMIT rear_setback_m = existing(rear_setback_m; …), but the clause gives no date or enactment for the existing value, so it is keyed as a PERMIT of the existing setback. Depends on the as-built setback of the existing ancillary building.

units.disclosure: If you convert an existing garage or shed that is closer to the lot line than the garden suite rules allow, the suite may keep the existing rear setback; we cannot check this without the as-built setbacks.

calculation_handling.description: Likewise, a garden suite in a lawfully existing ancillary building may keep that building's existing side yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: Could be read as LIMIT side_setback_m = existing(side_setback_m; …), but no date is given; keyed as PERMIT. Depends on the as-built side setback.

units.disclosure: If you convert an existing garage or shed that is closer to the side lot line than the garden suite rules allow, the suite may keep the existing side setback; we cannot check this without the as-built setbacks.

calculation_handling.description: A lawfully existing garden suite may keep side or rear setbacks smaller than 150.7.60.20(2) and (6) require, if no additions after July 24, 2025 increase the non-compliance.
calculation_handling.gaps: The date July 24, 2025 is a date, not a literal.

units.disclosure: An existing garden suite built before the July 24, 2025 setback change may keep its smaller setbacks; we cannot check this without the building history.

calculation_handling.description: A garden suite built under a permit issued after July 24, 2025 may have reduced setbacks only where they were already identified in a zoning certificate, rezoning, minor variance or site plan application filed on or before July 24, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Transition rule keyed on application filing dates; "Section 45 of the Planning Act" is a statute reference, not a literal. The lot's application history is not held.

units.disclosure: Garden suites with applications filed on or before July 24, 2025 may keep reduced setbacks approved through those applications; we cannot check application history.

calculation_handling.description: For a garden suite built under (2)(B), later additions may not increase the setback non-compliance beyond that established by the building permit.

units.disclosure: A garden suite that relies on the transition setbacks cannot later be extended in a way that makes the setbacks worse; we do not evaluate this.

calculation_handling.description: For 150.7.60.21(2), lawful / lawfully / lawfully existing also include anything authorized on or before July 24, 2025 or with a building permit lawfully issued before that date.
calculation_handling.gaps: garden_suite evidence is the scope phrase (150.7.60.21(2) governs garden suites). Dates are not literals.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "request for a zoning certificate" by reference to Municipal Code Chapter 363, Article I.
calculation_handling.gaps: "Chapter 363" and "Article I" are code references, not literals.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "complete application for a zoning by-law amendment" by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
calculation_handling.gaps: "5.5.2" is a policy number, not a literal.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "complete application for a minor variance" by reference to Section 2 of O. Reg. 200/96 under the Planning Act.
calculation_handling.gaps: "Section 2" and "200/96" are statute references, not literals.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "complete application for site plan approval" by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
calculation_handling.gaps: "5.5.2" is a policy number, not a literal.

calculation_handling.description: The main wall of an ancillary building containing a garden suite must be at least 4.0 m from the main wall of the residential building on the same lot if the ancillary building's height is no greater than 4.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: proposed_height_m is the height of the ancillary building containing the garden suite (a scenario value); for ancillary buildings 10.5.60.40(1) measures height from average grade rather than established grade, so the input approximates. Overrides 10.5.60.30(1) (general ancillary separation) for garden suites.

units.disclosure: A garden suite no taller than 4.0 m must be at least 4.0 m from the house; a 6.3 m suite needs 7.5 m, taken where the lot depth fits.

calculation_handling.description: The main wall of an ancillary building containing a garden suite must be at least 7.5 m from the main wall of the residential building on the same lot if the ancillary building's height is greater than 4.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: proposed_height_m is the height of the ancillary building containing the garden suite (a scenario value); for ancillary buildings 10.5.60.40(1) measures height from average grade rather than established grade, so the input approximates. Overrides 10.5.60.30(1) (general ancillary separation) for garden suites. Displaced by (1)(C) inside the area described there.

units.disclosure: A garden suite taller than 4.0 m must be at least 7.5 m from the house; at 4.0 m from the house the suite is limited to 4.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.7.60.30(1)(B), an ancillary building containing a garden suite with a height greater than 4.0 m, on a lot in the area bounded by Coxwell Avenue, Coxwell Boulevard and Massey Creek (west), the Don River and Sunrise Avenue (north), Victoria Park Avenue and Nursewood Park (east) and Lake Ontario (south), must be at least 5.0 m from a residential building on the same lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 150.7.60.30(1)(B) (7.5 m) within the described area. The area is described by streets and natural features; we hold no geometry for it, so whether a lot is inside cannot be determined. The measurement here is to 'a residential building', not main wall to main wall as in (A)/(B). proposed_height_m is the height of the ancillary building containing the garden suite (a scenario value); for ancillary buildings 10.5.60.40(1) measures height from average grade rather than established grade, so the input approximates. Overrides 10.5.60.30(1) (general ancillary separation) for garden suites.

units.disclosure: Inside the area bounded by Coxwell Ave/Coxwell Blvd/Massey Creek, the Don River/Sunrise Ave, Victoria Park Ave/Nursewood Park and Lake Ontario, a garden suite building taller than 4.0 m needs only 5.0 m (not 7.5 m) from the house. We cannot yet tell whether your lot is inside this area, so we apply the 7.5 m rule and flag this.

calculation_handling.description: If the existing separation between a lawfully existing ancillary building and a lawfully existing residential building on the same lot is less than the garden-suite separation required by 150.7.60.30(1), the existing separation becomes the required minimum.
calculation_handling.gaps: Sets the minimum to an as-built value; the DSL existing(...) form needs a date or enactment the text does not give, so no expression is written and the unit is keyed as a DEFINE of separation_m rather than a LIMIT. Needs as-built separation data we do not hold. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: If an existing garage or shed is closer to the house than the garden-suite rules require, converting it to a garden suite can keep the existing distance. We do not hold as-built building separations.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.40(2)(B), an ancillary building containing a garden suite located less than 7.5 m from the residential building on the lot has a maximum height of 4.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Distance to the residential building is a scenario value.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.40(2)(B), an ancillary building containing a garden suite located 7.5 m or more from the residential building on the lot has a maximum height of 6.3 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Distance to the residential building is a scenario value.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.40(3), an ancillary building containing a garden suite may have a maximum of two storeys, subject to the height limits in (1).
Antennae on the roof of a garden suite building may exceed its permitted maximum height by 1.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Height projection allowance for a rooftop element; there is no DSL target for element projection above the height limit, so 1.0 m is listed as not expressed.

units.disclosure: Antennae may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Flagpoles on the roof of a garden suite building may exceed its permitted maximum height by 1.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection; no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Flagpoles may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Parapets for a green roof on a garden suite building may exceed its permitted maximum height by 1.0 metres if they are no closer than 1.0 metre to the main walls.
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection with a set-in condition from the main walls; no DSL target or condition variable.

units.disclosure: Green-roof parapets set back 1.0 m from the walls may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Satellite dishes on the roof of a garden suite building may exceed its permitted maximum height by 1.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection; no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Satellite dishes may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Weather vanes on the roof of a garden suite building may exceed its permitted maximum height by 1.0 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection; no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Weather vanes may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Skylights on the roof of a garden suite building may exceed its permitted maximum height by 0.3 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection; no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Skylights may rise up to 0.3 m above a garden suite's height limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Equipment for the functional operation of a garden suite building (electrical, utility, mechanical, ventilation) on its roof may exceed its permitted maximum height by 1.0 metre, subject to (6).
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection; no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Rooftop mechanical equipment may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit, within the (6) limits; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Functional structures or parts of a garden suite building (enclosed stairwells, roof access, maintenance storage, chimneys, vents, water supply) may exceed its permitted maximum height by 1.0 metre, subject to (6).
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection; no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Rooftop stair enclosures, chimneys and vents may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit, within the (6) limits; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Structures that enclose, screen or cover the (A) and (B) elements may exceed the garden suite building's permitted maximum height by 1.0 metre, subject to (6).
calculation_handling.gaps: Rooftop element projection; no DSL target.

units.disclosure: Screens around rooftop equipment may rise up to 1.0 m above a garden suite's height limit; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Rooftop functional equipment and structures permitted by (5) must not cover more than 30 percent of the roof area, measured horizontally.
calculation_handling.gaps: A numeric limit on rooftop equipment coverage with no DSL target (lot_coverage_pct is lot coverage, not roof coverage), so keyed UNUSUAL. The unit text says 'an ancillary building' (the garden suite building by reference to (5)).

units.disclosure: Rooftop equipment on a garden suite may cover at most 30% of the roof; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Rooftop functional equipment and structures permitted by (5) must not be closer than 1.0 metre to the main walls of the ancillary building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Set-in from the main walls has no DSL target (encroachment_clearance_m is measured from a lot line), so keyed UNUSUAL.

units.disclosure: Rooftop equipment on a garden suite must be set in at least 1.0 m from the walls; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Regulation 10.5.60.40(4) (ancillary building entrance height) does not apply to an ancillary building containing a garden suite.
The GFA of an ancillary building containing a garden suite is excluded from the lot's total GFA and FSI.
calculation_handling.gaps: Exclusion rule for the FSI / GFA measurement of the lot; names fsi as the variable it shapes.

calculation_handling.description: The GFA of the garden suite building must be less than the GFA of the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: A relative maximum (garden suite GFA < main building GFA): gfa_m2 is the suite building's own target and there is no DSL input for the main residential building's GFA, so no numeric_expression can be written.

units.disclosure: A garden suite must be smaller in gross floor area than the house on the lot; the maximum suite is sized below the house.

calculation_handling.description: The general maximum floor area for ancillary buildings in 10.5.60.50(2) does not apply to an ancillary building containing a garden suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.5.60.50(2) for garden suite buildings; displaces[] is not a keyed field here.

calculation_handling.description: The maximum GFA of an ancillary building containing a garden suite is 120 m2.
Despite (4)(A), a one-storey garden suite building may have at most 60 m2 GFA.
calculation_handling.gaps: "one storey" is the design-choice token suite_one_storey (M-284; user input, taken as false: two storeys, the 120 m2 arm answered; the one-storey 60 m2 arm is disclosed).

calculation_handling.description: The GFA of a garden suite building may be reduced by the areas listed in 10.5.40.40(1), (2) and (3)(A) and (B) (GFA exclusions).
calculation_handling.gaps: Measurement rule incorporating the exclusion list in 10.5.40.40; could also be read as INCLUDE. The excluded areas depend on the suite design.

calculation_handling.description: Transition: a garden suite may have gross floor area exceeding 150.7.60.50(2), (4) and (5) if it is a lawfully existing garden suite and no additions increasing the noncompliance are added after July 24, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Relief from the garden suite GFA limits for lawfully existing garden suites (lawfully existing as extended by 150.7.60.51(2)(A)). Depends on as-built and permit history we do not hold. Not keyed PREVAILING: it is a transition exemption, not an alternate compliance path under a former by-law, section or schedule.

units.disclosure: An existing legal garden suite may keep floor area above the current garden suite limits, as long as nothing is added after July 24, 2025 that makes it less compliant. We do not hold building or permit history, so we apply the current limits.

calculation_handling.description: Transition: a garden suite may have gross floor area exceeding 150.7.60.50(2), (4) and (5) if built under a building permit issued after July 24, 2025 whose only excess gross floor area is that identified in a zoning certificate, zoning by-law amendment, minor variance or site plan approval applied for on or before July 24, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on permit and application history (zoning certificate, rezoning, minor variance, site plan approval filed on or before July 24, 2025) we do not hold. The sub-items (i)-(iv) are alternatives within this unit. Not keyed PREVAILING (no former by-law, section or schedule).

units.disclosure: A garden suite built under a permit issued after July 24, 2025 may exceed the current floor area limits if the extra area was already shown in an application filed on or before that date. We do not hold application history, so we apply the current limits.

calculation_handling.description: For a garden suite built under (1)(B), no additions with excess gross floor area that would increase the noncompliance beyond that established by the founding building permit may be added after that permit is issued.
calculation_handling.gaps: Limits the (1)(B) transition relief; depends on permit history we do not hold.

units.disclosure: A garden suite that relied on the transition rule cannot later be enlarged beyond what its building permit allowed. We do not hold permit history.

calculation_handling.description: For 150.7.60.51(1), lawful, lawfully and lawfully existing include, in addition to the Chapter 800 definitions, buildings, structures or uses authorized or permitted on or before July 24, 2025 and for which a building permit was lawfully issued before July 24, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Extends the lawfully existing term for the garden suite transition only; not a Chapter 800 measurement row, so input_fidelity is not keyed.

units.disclosure: For the garden-suite transition rules, a building or suite authorized on or before July 24, 2025, or with a building permit lawfully issued before that date, counts as existing.

calculation_handling.description: For 150.7.60.51(1), a request for a zoning certificate means one that satisfies Article I, Building Permits, of Municipal Code Chapter 363.

units.disclosure: A zoning certificate request counts for the garden-suite transition only if it meets the City's building-permit rules (Municipal Code Chapter 363, Article I).

calculation_handling.description: For 150.7.60.51(1), a complete application for a zoning by-law amendment means one that satisfies Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
For 150.7.60.51(1), a complete application for a minor variance means one that satisfies Section 2 of Ontario Regulation 200/96 under the Planning Act.
For 150.7.60.51(1), a complete application for site plan approval means one that satisfies Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.

evidence.deck_or_platform: a platform, such as a deck

calculation_handling.description: Interpretation rule: the exterior sides of a platform (deck, porch, balcony or similar) attached to or within 0.3 m of a garden-suite building are not main walls if at least 50% of the sides above the floor are open.
calculation_handling.gaps: Both numbers are thresholds deciding whether the platform sides count as main walls; no DSL variable exists for platform openness or distance to the suite building. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: A deck or balcony on a garden suite whose sides are at least half open is not treated as part of the suite's walls. We do not model garden-suite platform design.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(11), a platform without main walls on a garden suite is permitted if its area (excluding a green roof) is less than 10% of the garden suite's interior floor area.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 10% is a strict 'less than' share of the suite's interior floor area; it could be read as a platform_area_m2 limit, but the percentage-of-area form has no clean DSL binding (pct literal against an m2 target), so it is keyed conservatively as a condition of the PERMIT with the literal listed. Displaces 10.5.60.20(11) for these platforms. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: A deck on a garden suite must be smaller than 10% of the suite's floor area. We do not model garden-suite decks.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the platform permission: the platform must comply with the minimum setbacks and separation distances required for the garden-suite building.
calculation_handling.gaps: A non-numeric condition referring to the garden-suite setbacks (150.7.60.20) and separation (150.7.60.30); no requirement token fits. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: A garden-suite deck must meet the same setbacks and separation distances as the garden suite itself. We do not model garden-suite decks.

calculation_handling.description: Condition of the platform permission: platform sides next to a side yard must be screened from the abutting lot by an opaque barrier at least 1.5 m high.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 1.5 m is a minimum barrier height; no DSL target exists for screening height, so the literal is listed. The unit text names no building type (the garden suite is named in (2)(A) and (2)(B), not in this arm), so building_types is 'any'. No zone is named in the text.

units.disclosure: The side of a garden-suite deck facing a side yard needs an opaque screen at least 1.5 m tall. We do not model garden-suite decks.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.40(5)(B), the floor of a garden-suite platform permitted by (2) (other than a green roof) may be no higher than 0.2 m above the floor of the storey it is accessed from.
calculation_handling.gaps: The height is measured above the floor of the access storey, so it is keyed on platform_above_access_floor_m (a platform element target, M-280), not on platform_height_m (above established grade). The unit text names no building type (the garden suite is named only in (3)(B)), so building_types is 'any'. Displaces 10.5.60.40(5)(B). No zone is named.

units.disclosure: A garden-suite deck floor can be at most 0.2 m above the suite floor it opens from.

calculation_handling.description: The floor of a garden-suite platform must be located on the first floor of the garden-suite building.
calculation_handling.gaps: A non-numeric location obligation with no requirement token; keyed as a limitation of the platform permission. 'first floor' is an ordinal, not a numeric limit. Displaces 10.5.60.40(5)(B). No zone is named.

units.disclosure: A garden-suite deck is only allowed at the suite's first floor (no upper-level decks). We do not model garden-suite decks.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.7.60.60(2)(B), a platform without main walls (with its stairs or ramps) may encroach up to 1.5 m from the front main wall of the ancillary building into the separation required by 150.7.60.30(1), if the platform is no higher than 0.3 m above the average ground elevation along that wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.3 m platform-height threshold has no lot_condition token (building_height_band reads building height, not platform height), so the condition is left 'none' and the literal is listed. The encroachment is into the garden-suite separation distance only. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: A low garden-suite deck (no more than 0.3 m above ground) and its steps may extend up to 1.5 m into the required space between the suite and the house. We do not model garden-suite decks.

calculation_handling.description: A canopy, awning, similar structure or roof over a platform that encroaches into a required separation or setback may be at most 4.0 m above the average ground elevation along the abutting main wall of the ancillary building.
calculation_handling.gaps: A height cap on an encroaching canopy, awning or roof over a platform; height_m is the height of the building the unit applies to and no element-height target exists, so it is keyed UNUSUAL and disclosed (CHAT-13; the laneway twin 150.8.60.60(5)(A)). The 4.0 is the cap itself; threshold_used_in_application is the closest closed reason.

units.disclosure: A canopy, awning or roof over a garden-suite deck that projects into a setback can be at most 4.0 m high. We do not model garden-suite canopies.

calculation_handling.description: A canopy, awning or similar structure may encroach up to 1.5 m from the front main wall of the ancillary building into the separation required by 150.7.60.30(1).
calculation_handling.gaps: The encroachment is into the garden-suite separation distance only. Canopies have no vocab.uses token. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: A canopy or awning on the front of a garden suite may extend up to 1.5 m into the required space between the suite and the house. We do not model garden-suite canopies.

calculation_handling.description: Between a rear or side lot line and the garden-suite building, on a main wall facing a street, a canopy, awning or similar structure may encroach into the setbacks of 150.7.60.20 by the lesser of 50% of the required setback or 1.5 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'the lesser of 50 percent of the required building setback or 1.5 metres' is written as min(50 pct × lot_line_setback_m; 1.5 m); the 50 pct literal multiplies the required ancillary setback (lot_line_setback_m), so its unit is a share rather than the target's m. Applies only to a street-facing main wall, which has no lot_condition token, so condition is 'none'. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: On a garden-suite wall facing a street, a canopy or awning may project into the setback by up to half the required setback or 1.5 m, whichever is less. We do not model garden-suite canopies.

calculation_handling.description: On a garden-suite building, a pilaster, decorative column, cornice, sill, belt course or similar feature no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line may encroach up to 0.6 m into a setback of 150.7.60.20 or the separation of 150.7.60.30(1).
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.3 m lot-line clearance is a precondition (a second target, encroachment_clearance_m, would be needed to express it), listed as a threshold. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Decorative features on a garden suite (cornices, sills, columns) may project up to 0.6 m into setbacks if they stay at least 0.3 m from the lot line. We do not model these details.

calculation_handling.description: On a garden-suite building, a chimney breast no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line and no wider than 2.0 m may encroach up to 0.6 m into a setback of 150.7.60.20 or the separation of 150.7.60.30(1).
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.3 m clearance and 2.0 m width are preconditions of the encroachment; listed as thresholds. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: A chimney breast on a garden suite (up to 2.0 m wide) may project up to 0.6 m into setbacks if it stays at least 0.3 m from the lot line. We do not model these details.

calculation_handling.description: Wall-mounted equipment (vents, pipes, utility equipment, satellite dishes, antennae, air conditioners) on a main wall of a garden-suite building, no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line, may encroach up to 0.6 m into the setbacks of 150.7.60.20.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.6 m maximum is stated in the stem (7), so the statement cites (7). The 0.3 m clearance is a precondition, listed as a threshold. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Wall-mounted equipment such as vents or air conditioners on a garden suite may project up to 0.6 m into setbacks if it stays at least 0.3 m from the lot line. We do not model these details.

calculation_handling.description: Wall-mounted equipment on the front main wall of a garden-suite building, no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line, may encroach up to 0.6 m into the separation required by 150.7.60.30(1).
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.6 m maximum is stated in the stem (7), so the statement cites (7). The 0.3 m clearance is a precondition, listed as a threshold. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Wall-mounted equipment on the front of a garden suite may project up to 0.6 m into the required space between the suite and the house. We do not model these details.

numeric_expression: lot_coverage_pct = if(mapped(LC); max(45 pct @(1)(A); overlay(LC) @(1)(B)(i)); unregulated) @(1)

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.70(1), 10.10.60.70(1) and the zone lot coverage regulations, on a lot with a residential building (not an apartment building) and a garden suite building, option (A): the area covered by all buildings and structures must not exceed 45 percent.
calculation_handling.gaps: The alternative arms (A) and (B) are one statement (M-179(1), Spec 68 §7.4): where the Lot Coverage Overlay is mapped, the larger of (A) 45 % for all buildings and (B)(i) the overlay value for the residential building; where it is not, (B)(ii) sets no coverage for the residential building, which is the larger (unregulated is terminal, M-54). x.30.40(1)(D) 45 % still applies under both (M-191). The (B) all-ancillary 20 % is on ancillary_coverage_pct (150.7.60.70(1)(B)).

units.disclosure: With a garden suite the larger of the two coverage options is used: (A) 45 % for all buildings, or (B) the suite left out of coverage with all ancillary buildings together at most 20 %; the other option is shown.

calculation_handling.description: Option (B): the garden suite building is excluded from the overall lot coverage; all ancillary buildings combined, including the garden suite, may not exceed 20 percent of the lot area; and the residential building's maximum lot coverage is the Lot Coverage Overlay Map value if mapped, otherwise no lot coverage applies to it.
calculation_handling.gaps: All ancillary buildings combined, including the garden suite, are capped at 20 % of the lot on ancillary_coverage_pct (M-179(1)); the residential building's arm (overlay or none) is the (B) argument of 150.7.60.70(1)(A)'s max (M-191). Other ancillary buildings are taken as absent (M-177(3)).

units.disclosure: Under option (B), your house follows the Lot Coverage Overlay Map (or no limit if unmapped) and all accessory buildings together, including the garden suite, may cover at most 20% of the lot.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.75.1(4), a solar energy device on a garden suite building must comply with the minimum building setbacks for a garden suite building.
calculation_handling.gaps: Incorporates the garden suite building setbacks (150.7.60.20) for the device; read as INCLUDE rather than REQUIRE because no vocab.requirement token fits. Solar devices are not part of the envelope calculation.

calculation_handling.description: Allowance of 1.2 m for a solar energy device above the permitted maximum height of an ancillary building containing a garden suite; a device height offset relative to another unit's limit, not a building height target.
calculation_handling.gaps: No DSL target or input for device height above another regulation's permitted maximum.

units.disclosure: Rooftop solar devices on a garden suite may rise up to 1.2 metres above the maximum height allowed for that garden suite building. This allowance is not included in the height calculation.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 200.5.10.1(1) and 200.5.10.11(1)(C): if a lot has an ancillary building containing a garden suite, no parking spaces are required for any dwelling units and secondary suites in a detached house, semi-detached house, townhouse, detached houseplex or semi-detached houseplex on the same lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the parking space requirements of 200.5.10.1(1) and 200.5.10.11(1)(C) for the listed house types on a lot with a garden suite. There is no lot_condition token for 'has a garden suite' (it is user input has_garden_suite), so the trigger is carried by user_inputs and application, not condition.

units.disclosure: No parking is required with the suite; it must provide two bicycle parking spaces.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 200.5.10.1(1) and 200.5.10.11(1)(C), no parking space is required for a garden suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the parking space requirements of 200.5.10.1(1) and 200.5.10.11(1)(C) for the garden suite itself.

units.disclosure: No parking is required with the suite; it must provide two bicycle parking spaces.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building containing a garden suite must provide at least two bicycle parking spaces, within the garden suite or within any required separation distance or required building setbacks for the ancillary building.
calculation_handling.gaps: The minimum is written as the word 'two'; keyed as the numeral 2 units. The location rule (within the suite or the required separation/setbacks) is a design fact and is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: No parking is required with the suite; it must provide two bicycle parking spaces.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.80.40(3), if a lot has an ancillary building containing a garden suite, vehicle access to a parking space must be provided from a lawfully existing vehicle access.
calculation_handling.gaps: A non-numeric obligation (REQUIRE in substance), but no vocab.requirement value fits 'access from a lawfully existing vehicle access' (access_from_lane is a different obligation), so it is keyed UNUSUAL and disclosed. The lawfully_existing token refers to the vehicle access, not the building. Overrides 10.5.80.40(3).

units.disclosure: On a lot with a garden suite, any parking must be reached from an existing legal driveway or vehicle access; a new vehicle access cannot be added. We do not hold driveway history, so we do not check this.

calculation_handling.description: Scope statement: the regulations of Section 150.8 apply to laneway suites.
calculation_handling.gaps: A scope/applicability statement with no numeric content; no zone is named.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(2), an ancillary building may be used for living accommodation in one laneway suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Use permission; the one-building limit is carried by 150.8.20.1(2).

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(3), an ancillary building may have both food preparation and sanitary facilities in a laneway suite.
Despite 150.5.60.1(1), a home occupation is permitted in a laneway suite exclusively and separately occupied as a principal residence, applying Section 150.5 as if it is a dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Home occupation is a use outside MaxBLD scope with no vocab use token.

units.disclosure: A home business is allowed in a laneway suite that is someone's principal residence; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.13.20.1(1), a short-term rental is permitted in an ancillary building if it is in a laneway suite exclusively and separately occupied as a principal residence.
calculation_handling.gaps: Short-term rental is a use outside MaxBLD scope with no vocab use token.

units.disclosure: A short-term rental is allowed in a laneway suite that is someone's principal residence; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(4), above-ground parts of an ancillary building containing a laneway suite may be erected before the main walls and roof of the residential building on the same lot are complete.
calculation_handling.gaps: Construction sequencing permission; no envelope effect.

calculation_handling.description: A maximum of one ancillary building containing either a laneway suite or a garden suite is permitted on a lot, and a lot may not contain both a laneway suite and a garden suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: The count is of suite buildings (laneway or garden) on the lot, not principal buildings. The second sentence (not both) is a prohibition carried in the same unit; it follows from the one-building limit when each suite is in its own building.

calculation_handling.description: A laneway suite is allowed only on a lot whose rear or side lot line abuts a lane for at least 3.5 m, or with a cumulative 3.5 m along a side and rear lot line.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 3.5 m length of lot line abutting the lane has no DSL input (lane-abutting length is not held); recorded as threshold_used_in_application. Keyed as a conditional PERMIT of the laneway suite building type; could also be read as UNUSUAL (an eligibility test).

units.disclosure: A laneway suite needs at least 3.5 m of lane along the rear lot line, along a side lot line, or along the side and rear lot lines combined; the lane length along each lot line is measured from the lane centreline and is an estimate.

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with a residential building and a laneway suite, with a lot frontage of 6.0 m or less, at least 60 percent of the area between the house's rear main walls and the laneway suite's front main wall must be soft landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: rear_soft_landscaping_pct is the closest target: the regulated area (between all rear main walls of the residential building and the front main wall of the laneway suite building) lies in the rear yard but is not the whole rear yard, so the share applies to that area only. Overrides 10.5.50.10(3) on a lot with a laneway suite.

units.disclosure: On a lot with a frontage of 6.0 m or less, 60 % of the area between the house's rear walls and the laneway suite's front wall must be soft landscaping; this is shown, and it does not shrink the suite.

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with a residential building and a laneway suite, with a lot frontage greater than 6.0 m, at least 85 percent of the area between the house's rear main walls and the laneway suite's front main wall must be soft landscaping, excluding a pedestrian walkway up to 1.5 m wide.
calculation_handling.gaps: rear_soft_landscaping_pct is the closest target: the regulated area (between all rear main walls of the residential building and the front main wall of the laneway suite building) lies in the rear yard but is not the whole rear yard, so the share applies to that area only. Overrides 10.5.50.10(3) on a lot with a laneway suite. The 1.5 m is the maximum width of the excluded pedestrian walkway (it bounds the exclusion, not the soft landscaping share); no target exists for walkway width.

units.disclosure: On a lot with a frontage over 6.0 m, 85 % of the area between the house's rear walls and the laneway suite's front wall must be soft landscaping (a walkway up to 1.5 m wide excluded); this is shown, and it does not shrink the suite.

calculation_handling.description: On a lot with a laneway suite, the area between the laneway suite building and the lot line abutting the lane, excluding a permitted driveway and a pedestrian walkway up to 1.5 m wide, must be landscaping, of which at least 75 percent must be soft landscaping.
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed REQUIRE landscaping_type (the area must be landscaping). The 75 percent soft-landscaping share applies to the lane-side strip; no DSL target covers that area (rear_soft_landscaping_pct is the rear yard between house and suite), so it is not expressed. The 1.5 m bounds the excluded walkway width.

units.disclosure: The strip between a laneway suite and the lane (apart from a permitted driveway and a walkway up to 1.5 m wide) must be landscaped, at least 75% of it with soft landscaping such as grass or planting. We do not check this strip.

calculation_handling.description: Measurement rule: the required minimum ancillary building setbacks apply to all above-ground and below-ground parts of a laneway-suite building, excluding footings.
calculation_handling.gaps: A rule on which parts of the building the setbacks are measured to; it defines no single DSL variable, so target is 'none'. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Laneway suite setbacks are measured to every part of the building above and below ground (except footings). We do not model below-grade parts.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(2) and (5) and 10.10.60.20(1), the minimum rear yard setback of a laneway-suite building is 0.0 m if the rear lot line does not abut a street or lane and the rear main wall has no openings (vehicle access, doors or windows).
calculation_handling.gaps: The conditions are negations (rear lot line does NOT abut a street or lane; NO openings in the rear wall); the condition grammar has no negated token, so condition is 'none' and the arm depends on the lot's rear abutment and on the user's wall openings (suite_wall_openings). Displaces 10.5.60.20(2), 10.5.60.20(5) and 10.10.60.20(1) for laneway suites. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Whether the rear lot line abuts a street or lane is not known for this lot; the larger setback (1.0 m) is used.

calculation_handling.description: In all other cases (rear lot line abuts a street or lane, or the rear wall has openings), the minimum rear yard setback of a laneway-suite building is 1.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'in all other cases' is the complement of (2)(A), which has no expressible condition; condition is 'none'. Displaces 10.5.60.20(2), 10.5.60.20(5) and 10.10.60.20(1) for laneway suites. No zone is named.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(3) and (6) and 10.10.60.20(1), the minimum side yard setback of a laneway-suite building is 0.0 m if the side lot line does not abut a street or lane and the side main wall has no openings.
calculation_handling.gaps: The conditions are negations with no negated token in the grammar; condition is 'none'. Depends on side-lot-line abutment and the user's wall openings. Displaces 10.5.60.20(3), 10.5.60.20(6) and 10.10.60.20(1) for laneway suites. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Whether the side lot line abuts a street or lane is not known for this lot; the larger setback (1.0 m) is used.

calculation_handling.description: If the side lot line abuts a street, the minimum side yard setback of the laneway-suite building is the required minimum side yard setback for the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Incorporates the residential building's required side yard setback by reference; no literal of its own, so keyed as INCLUDE (the template has no include_ref field; the referenced value is the zone's side setback for the residential building on a street side). The street-abutting side lot line has no plain lot_condition token, so condition is 'none'. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: On a corner lot, the laneway suite is set back from the side lot line that abuts the street by the side yard setback required for the house.

evidence.abuts_lane: rear lot line abuts a lane
evidence.building_height_band: beginning from a height of 4.0 metres

calculation_handling.description: If the side lot line abuts a lot in the R, RD, RS, RT or RM zone and the rear lot line abuts a lane, the part of the laneway-suite building above a height of 4.0 m must be set back 1.5 m from a side lot line that abuts the rear lot line of another lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Layer 2 answers the 1.5 m upper side setback of the part above 4.0 m (upper_side_setback_m); Layer 3 draws the step-back over the 1.0 m side setback below (Spec 78 P5.5). Which side line abuts another lot's rear lot line, and that lot's zone, have no tokens (lot-line classification, Spec 78 P5.14 ML-1): the step-back is applied on the lane lot as the larger setback (M-198, M-197).

units.disclosure: Above 4.0 m the laneway suite steps back 1.5 m from the side lot line that abuts another lot's rear lot line; below 4.0 m its side setback is 1.0 m.

calculation_handling.description: In all other cases, the minimum side yard setback of a laneway-suite building is 1.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'in all other cases' is the complement of (3)(A)-(C), which have no fully expressible conditions; condition is 'none'. Displaces 10.5.60.20(3), 10.5.60.20(6) and 10.10.60.20(1) for laneway suites. No zone is named.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing ancillary building's lawful setback is less than the 150.8.60.20 minimum for a laneway suite building, the minimum rear yard setback for a laneway suite in that building is the existing building's rear yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: The value is the as-built rear setback of the existing ancillary building; existing() needs a date or enactment the text does not give, and we hold no as-built input, so no expression is written. M-158(1): by default the lot is a new build (lawfully_existing resolves false), so the 150.8.60.20 minimum is answered; the existing building's smaller setback is the disclosed caveat (M-211(4), existing_ancillary_setbacks).

units.disclosure: If the existing ancillary building is lawfully existing, a laneway suite in it may keep its setbacks.

calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing ancillary building's lawful setback is less than the 150.8.60.20 minimum for a laneway suite building, the minimum side yard setback for a laneway suite in that building is the existing building's side yard setback.
calculation_handling.gaps: As-built side setback; no as-built input and no date for existing(), so no expression. M-158(1): by default the lot is a new build (lawfully_existing resolves false), so the 150.8.60.20 minimum is answered; the existing building's smaller setback is the disclosed caveat (M-211(4), existing_ancillary_setbacks).

units.disclosure: If the existing ancillary building is lawfully existing, a laneway suite in it may keep its setbacks.

evidence.building_height_band: if the height of the ancillary building

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.30(1), a laneway suite building no taller than 4.0 m must be at least 4.0 m from the main wall of the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: proposed_height_m is the height of the laneway suite building (a scenario value).

units.disclosure: A laneway suite no taller than 4.0 m must be at least 4.0 m from the house; a 6.3 m suite needs 7.5 m, taken where the lot depth fits. If the laneway suite sits with an existing house, the separation and height rows are indicative only: the existing house's dimensions are not held, so its distance to the suite is not confirmed.

evidence.building_height_band: if the height of the ancillary building

calculation_handling.description: A laneway suite building taller than 4.0 m must be at least 7.5 m from the main wall of the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: proposed_height_m is the height of the laneway suite building (a scenario value).

units.disclosure: A laneway suite taller than 4.0 m must be at least 7.5 m from the house; at 4.0 m from the house the suite is limited to 4.0 m. If the laneway suite sits with an existing house, the separation and height rows are indicative only: the existing house's dimensions are not held, so its distance to the suite is not confirmed.

calculation_handling.description: The maximum building length of a laneway suite building is 10.0 m.
The maximum building width of a laneway suite building is 8.0 m.

If the separation between a lawfully existing ancillary building and a lawfully existing residential building on the same lot is less than the laneway suite separation required by 150.8.60.30, the required minimum separation is the existing separation.
calculation_handling.gaps: existing() needs a date; the clause names none ('lawfully existing'), so the enactment of By-law 569-2013 is used as the reference (the conservative reading of 'lawfully existing' under this By-law); flag for adjudication. The relief applies only where the existing separation is less than the 150.8.60.30 requirement, and then replaces that requirement for the existing pair of buildings. We hold no as-built separation, so it is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: If an existing accessory building is already closer to the house than the laneway suite rules require, the existing distance is accepted. We do not know existing building positions, so we apply the standard separation.

calculation_handling.description: If the lawful building length of a lawfully existing ancillary building exceeds the maximum laneway suite building length in 150.8.60.30(5), the permitted maximum building length for an ancillary building containing a laneway suite is the existing lawful length.
calculation_handling.gaps: existing() needs a date; the clause names none ('lawfully existing'), so the enactment of By-law 569-2013 is used as the reference (the conservative reading of 'lawfully existing' under this By-law); flag for adjudication. Applies only where the existing lawful length exceeds the 150.8.60.30(5) maximum, and then replaces it. We hold no as-built length, so it is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: If an existing accessory building is longer than the laneway suite length limit, a laneway suite in it may keep that existing length. We do not know existing building sizes, so we apply the standard limit.

calculation_handling.description: If the lawful building width of a lawfully existing ancillary building exceeds the maximum laneway suite building width in 150.8.60.30(6), the permitted maximum building width for an ancillary building containing a laneway suite is the existing lawful width.
calculation_handling.gaps: existing() needs a date; the clause names none ('lawfully existing'), so the enactment of By-law 569-2013 is used as the reference (the conservative reading of 'lawfully existing' under this By-law); flag for adjudication. Applies only where the existing lawful width exceeds the 150.8.60.30(6) maximum, and then replaces it. We hold no as-built width, so it is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: If the laneway suite sits with an existing house, the separation and height rows are indicative only: the existing house's dimensions are not held, so its distance to the suite is not confirmed.

calculation_handling.gaps: The distance to the residential building is a scenario value. Displaces 10.5.60.40(2)(B) for laneway suites. No zone is named.
