calculation_handling.gaps: A permitted height allowance for a rooftop element; no DSL target exists for rooftop element height, so the 1.5 metres allowance (added to the cross-referenced maximum height) is listed as not expressed. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Small rooftop elements on a laneway suite may rise a little above the height limit. We do not model rooftop elements.

calculation_handling.description: Structures or parts of the building used for its functional operation (enclosed stairwells, roof access, storage, chimneys, vents, water supply), subject to (6), on the roof of a laneway-suite building may exceed the building's permitted maximum height by 1.5 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: A permitted height allowance for a rooftop element; no DSL target exists for rooftop element height, so the 1.5 metres allowance (added to the cross-referenced maximum height) is listed as not expressed. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Small rooftop elements on a laneway suite may rise a little above the height limit. We do not model rooftop elements.

calculation_handling.description: Structures enclosing, screening or covering the elements in (5)(A) and (B), subject to (6), on the roof of a laneway-suite building may exceed the building's permitted maximum height by 1.5 metres.
calculation_handling.gaps: A permitted height allowance for a rooftop element; no DSL target exists for rooftop element height, so the 1.5 metres allowance (added to the cross-referenced maximum height) is listed as not expressed. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Small rooftop elements on a laneway suite may rise a little above the height limit. We do not model rooftop elements.

calculation_handling.description: Rooftop functional equipment and structures permitted by (5) must not cover more than 30% of the roof area, measured horizontally.
calculation_handling.gaps: A cap on roof area taken by rooftop elements; no DSL target exists for roof share, so the 30% is listed as not expressed. The unit text names no building type (it refers to elements permitted in (5), which concern laneway-suite buildings), so building_types is 'any'. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Rooftop equipment on a laneway suite that exceeds the height limit may cover at most 30% of the roof. We do not model rooftop elements.

calculation_handling.description: Rooftop functional equipment and structures permitted by (5) must not be closer than 1.5 m to the main walls of the ancillary building.
calculation_handling.gaps: A minimum inset of rooftop elements from the main walls; no DSL target exists for it, so the 1.5 m is listed as not expressed. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Rooftop equipment on a laneway suite that exceeds the height limit must be set back at least 1.5 m from the walls. We do not model rooftop elements.

calculation_handling.description: Regulation 10.5.60.40(4) (entrance height) does not apply to an ancillary building containing a laneway suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces 10.5.60.40(4) for laneway suites (no displaces field in the template). No zone is named.

calculation_handling.description: The gross floor area of an ancillary building containing a laneway suite is excluded from the lot's total gross floor area and floor space index.
calculation_handling.gaps: Exclusion rule for gfa_m2 / fsi; the text omits 'of' ('gross floor area an ancillary building').

calculation_handling.description: The gross floor area of an ancillary building containing a laneway suite must be less than the gross floor area of the residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: The bound is the residential building's gross floor area, which shares the gfa_m2 target name; no separate DSL input exists, so no expression. The bound is strict ('less than').

units.disclosure: A laneway suite must be smaller in gross floor area than the house on the lot; the maximum suite is sized below the house.

calculation_handling.description: Regulation 10.5.60.50(2) (maximum floor area of an ancillary building) does not apply to an ancillary building containing a laneway suite.
The gross floor area of a laneway suite building may be reduced by the areas listed in 10.5.40.40(1), (2) and (3)(A) and (B).
calculation_handling.gaps: Applies the principal-building GFA exclusions to the laneway suite building; needs the suite's floor plan.

units.disclosure: The laneway suite building's counted floor area may exclude the areas listed in 10.5.40.40(1), (2) and (3)(A) and (B).

calculation_handling.description: A lawfully existing laneway suite may exceed the GFA requirements of 150.8.60.50(2) and (4), if no additions after July 24, 2025 increase the non-compliance.
calculation_handling.gaps: The date July 24, 2025 is a date, not a literal.

units.disclosure: An existing laneway suite built before the July 24, 2025 floor area change may keep its larger floor area; we cannot check this without the building history.

calculation_handling.description: A laneway suite built under a permit issued after July 24, 2025 may exceed the GFA requirements only where the excess was identified in a zoning certificate, rezoning, minor variance or site plan application filed on or before July 24, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Transition rule keyed on application filing dates; "Section 45 of the Planning Act" is a statute reference, not a literal. The lot's application history is not held.

units.disclosure: Laneway suites with applications filed on or before July 24, 2025 may keep extra floor area approved through those applications; we cannot check application history.

calculation_handling.description: For a laneway suite built under (1)(B), later additions may not increase the GFA non-compliance beyond that established by the building permit.

units.disclosure: A laneway suite that relies on the transition floor area cannot later be extended in a way that adds more excess floor area; we do not evaluate this.

calculation_handling.description: For 150.8.60.51(1), lawful / lawfully / lawfully existing also include anything authorized on or before July 24, 2025 or with a building permit lawfully issued before that date.
calculation_handling.gaps: laneway_suite evidence is the scope phrase (150.8.60.51(1) governs laneway suites). Dates are not literals.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "request for a zoning certificate" by reference to Municipal Code Chapter 363, Article I.
calculation_handling.gaps: "Chapter 363" and "Article I" are code references, not literals.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "complete application for a zoning by-law amendment" by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
calculation_handling.gaps: "5.5.2" is a policy number, not a literal.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "complete application for a minor variance" by reference to Section 2 of O. Reg. 200/96 under the Planning Act.
calculation_handling.gaps: "Section 2" and "200/96" are statute references, not literals.

calculation_handling.description: Defines a "complete application for site plan approval" by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
calculation_handling.gaps: "5.5.2" is a policy number, not a literal.

calculation_handling.description: Exclusion rule: the exterior sides of a platform (deck, porch, balcony or similar) attached to or within 0.3 m of an ancillary building containing a laneway suite are not main walls if at least 50 percent of the exterior sides above the floor are open to the outside.
calculation_handling.gaps: 0.3 m (proximity) and 50 percent (openness) are the tests for the exclusion; no lot_condition token reads them. Design facts; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(11), a platform without main walls (per (1)) is permitted on a laneway suite building if its area, other than a green roof, is less than 10 percent of the laneway suite's interior floor area.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 10 percent test compares platform area with the suite's interior floor area (a ratio of two design values); no condition token reads it, and it is not keyed as a platform_area_m2 LIMIT because the clause frames it as a condition of the permission. Overrides 10.5.60.20(11).

units.disclosure: A deck on a laneway suite is allowed if it is smaller than 10% of the suite's interior floor area. We do not check deck sizes.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.20(11), a platform without main walls is permitted on a laneway suite building if it complies with the required minimum building setbacks and separation distances for the ancillary building containing a laneway suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: The condition is compliance with the laneway suite setbacks and separation; the platform's placement is a design fact.

units.disclosure: A deck on a laneway suite must respect the same setbacks and separation distances as the laneway suite building. We do not check deck placement.

calculation_handling.description: The exterior sides of a laneway suite platform adjacent to a side yard must be visually screened from the abutting lot by an opaque barrier at least 1.5 m high.
calculation_handling.gaps: A screening obligation with a minimum barrier height; no vocab.requirement value or DSL target covers screening, so it is keyed UNUSUAL. The 1.5 m is the barrier minimum itself; threshold_used_in_application is the closest closed reason.

units.disclosure: A laneway suite deck facing a side yard must be screened from the neighbour by a solid barrier at least 1.5 m high. We do not check screening.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.40(5)(B), the floor of a permitted laneway suite platform (other than a green roof) must be no higher than 0.2 m above the floor of the storey from which it gains access.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit is measured from the floor of the access storey, so it is keyed on platform_above_access_floor_m (a platform element target, M-280), not on platform_height_m. Overrides 10.5.60.40(5)(B). The unit text names no building type; the platform is the one permitted under (2) on a laneway suite.

units.disclosure: A laneway suite deck floor can be at most 0.2 m above the floor of the room it opens from.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.40(5)(B), the floor of a permitted laneway suite platform (other than a green roof) must be no higher than 4.0 m above average grade, unless it is attached to or within 0.3 m of a main wall facing a lane.
calculation_handling.gaps: Measured above average grade (platform_height_m is defined above established grade; the input approximates). The 'unless attached to or within 0.3 m of a main wall facing a lane' exception has no condition token and is not keyed; where it holds this limit does not apply. The unit text names no ancillary building or laneway suite directly; the platform is the one permitted under (2). Design value; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite (2)(B), a platform without main walls, with stairs or ramps to it, may encroach up to 1.5 m from the front main wall of the ancillary building into the separation required by 150.8.60.30(1), if the platform is no higher than 0.3 m above the average ground elevation along that front main wall.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.3 m height test has no condition token; not keyed. Displaces (2)(B) for the 150.8.60.30(1) separation only. Design element; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: A canopy, awning or similar structure, or a roof over a platform complying with (4), may encroach into a required separation or setback subject to a maximum height of 4.0 m above the average ground elevation along the abutting main wall of the ancillary building.
calculation_handling.gaps: A height cap on an encroaching canopy/awning; height_m is the height of the building the unit applies to and no element-height target exists, so it is keyed UNUSUAL. The 4.0 is the cap itself; threshold_used_in_application is the closest closed reason.

units.disclosure: A canopy, awning or roof over a deck that projects into a laneway suite's setback or separation area can be at most 4.0 m above the ground. We do not check canopies.

calculation_handling.description: A canopy, awning or similar structure may encroach up to 1.5 m from the front main wall of the ancillary building into the separation required by 150.8.60.30(1).
Between a lane and the laneway suite building, a canopy, awning or similar structure may encroach up to 0.75 m from the main wall facing the lane into the setbacks required by 150.8.60.20.

A pilaster, decorative column, cornice, sill, belt course or similar architectural feature on a laneway suite building may encroach up to 0.6 m into a setback required by 150.8.60.20 or the separation required by 150.8.60.30(1).
A chimney breast on a laneway suite building may encroach up to 0.6 m into a setback required by 150.8.60.20 or the separation required by 150.8.60.30(1), if it is no wider than 2.0 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 2.0 m width is a condition of the encroachment (no condition token reads chimney width), not a separate limit. Design element; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Wall-mounted equipment (vents, pipes, utility equipment, satellite dishes, antennae, air conditioners) on a laneway suite building's main wall facing a lane may encroach up to 0.6 m into the lane-side setbacks required by 150.8.60.20.
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.6 m value is in the stem (7); cited @(7). Design element; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Wall-mounted equipment on the front main wall of a laneway suite building may encroach up to 0.6 m into the separation required by 150.8.60.30(1).
calculation_handling.gaps: The 0.6 m value is in the stem (7); cited @(7). Design element; not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.70(1) and 10.10.60.70(1), if a lot has a laneway-suite building, that building is not included in the overall lot coverage calculation.
calculation_handling.gaps: An exclusion rule for the lot coverage calculation; applies only when a laneway suite is present or proposed (user input). Displaces 10.5.60.70(1) and 10.10.60.70(1) for such lots. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: A laneway suite does not count toward the lot coverage limit for the house; all ancillary buildings together, the suite included, may cover at most 30% of the lot.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.70(1) and 10.10.60.70(1), on a lot with a laneway suite, the area covered by all ancillary buildings combined (including the laneway suite) may not exceed 30% of the lot area.
calculation_handling.gaps: The coverage is of all ancillary buildings combined, not of the principal building; lot_coverage_pct is used with building_types limited to ancillary buildings. Applies only when a laneway suite is present or proposed (user input; no lot_condition token). Displaces 10.5.60.70(1) and 10.10.60.70(1). No zone is named.

units.disclosure: All ancillary buildings together, the laneway suite included, may cover at most 30% of the lot. If the lot has other ancillary buildings, they count toward the 30% ancillary coverage.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 200.5.10.1(1) and 200.5.10.11(1)(C), if a lot has an ancillary building containing a laneway suite, no parking spaces are required for any dwelling units and secondary suites in a detached house, semi-detached house, townhouse, duplex, triplex or fourplex on the same lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the Chapter 200 parking requirements for the main building's units when a laneway suite exists (user input has_laneway_suite; no lot_condition token).

units.disclosure: No parking is required with the suite; it must provide two bicycle parking spaces.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 200.5.10.1(1) and 200.5.10.11(1)(C), no parking space is required for a laneway suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Displaces the Chapter 200 parking requirement for the laneway suite itself.

units.disclosure: No parking is required with the suite; it must provide two bicycle parking spaces.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building containing a laneway suite must have at least two bicycle parking spaces, located within the suite, any required separation distance, or the required setbacks for the laneway suite building.
calculation_handling.gaps: 'two' written as 2. The location options are not checked.

units.disclosure: No parking is required with the suite; it must provide two bicycle parking spaces.

calculation_handling.description: Indoor amenity space of at least 2.0 m2 per dwelling unit; there is no amenity-space target in the model.

units.disclosure: In the RA zone a lot with 20 or more dwelling units needs at least 2.0 square metres of indoor amenity space per dwelling unit at or above established grade. Amenity space is not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: At least 40.0 m2 of outdoor amenity space adjoining or accessible to the indoor amenity space; there is no amenity-space target in the model.

units.disclosure: In the RA zone a lot with 20 or more dwelling units needs at least 40.0 square metres of outdoor amenity space adjoining or directly accessible to the indoor amenity space. Amenity space is not modelled.

calculation_handling.description: No more than 25 percent of the outdoor amenity component may be a green roof; there is no amenity-space target in the model.

units.disclosure: In the RA zone, for a lot with 20 or more dwelling units, no more than 25 percent of the outdoor amenity component may be a green roof. Amenity space is not modelled.

Defines Prevailing Sections as the sections, as amended, of the Former General Zoning By-laws listed and identified as such in Sections 900.2 to 900.50.
Where a Chapter 900 exception exists, all regulations of the By-law, including the exception, apply together.
Site Specific Provisions in Chapter 900 govern over any inconsistent regulations in Chapters 5 to 800.
Regulations of Chapters 5 to 800 that are inconsistent with a Prevailing By-law or Prevailing Section do not apply to prevent a building or use that complies with it.
All applicable regulations of the By-law apply to new buildings, additions and enlargements, and to any use of land not permitted by the Prevailing By-law or Prevailing Section.

Where this By-law applies under 1.5.7(1), the Former General Zoning By-laws continue to apply only to the extent needed to interpret and support Prevailing By-laws or Sections, and do not have priority over this By-law.

calculation_handling.description: Enacting instruction that adds regulation 10.5.80.1(4); no regulation of its own.

As replaced by By-law 1075-2026: wall-mounted equipment on a garden-suite building (vents, pipes, utility equipment, satellite dishes or antennae), no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line, may encroach up to 0.6 m.
calculation_handling.gaps: Source defect (lead_in_without_items): the replacement text ends 'as follows' but lists no items, so the setbacks or separation into which the equipment may encroach are not stated; the encroachment target is kept generic. Air conditioners are no longer listed. The 0.3 m lot-line clearance is a precondition, listed as a threshold. No zone is named.

units.disclosure: Wall-mounted equipment on a garden suite may project up to 0.6 m if it stays at least 0.3 m from the lot line. The amended text does not say which setbacks this applies to, and we do not model these details.

calculation_handling.description: Amending instruction of By-law 1075-2026: regulation 150.7.60.60(7) of Zoning By-law 569-2013 is replaced by the text that follows.
calculation_handling.gaps: An amendment instruction with no regulatory content of its own; the section number '31.' and by-law numbers are not literals.

calculation_handling.description: A heating, ventilation and air conditioning device associated with a garden suite, whether on the garden suite building or ground mounted, may encroach up to 0.9 m into a required building setback or required separation distance if no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line; on the building it may sit on the roof and exceed the height limit by 2.0 m or on a platform; ground mounted it must be within 2.0 m of a main wall or a platform.
calculation_handling.gaps: Only the setback encroachment arms ((A)(i), (B)(i)) are expressed. The separation-distance encroachment arms ((A)(ii), (B)(ii)) have no DSL target (encroachment_m is into a setback), the 2.0 m rooftop height projection has no target, and the 2.0 m placement from a main wall or platform has no variable, so those literals are listed as not expressed. Mixed targets (encroachment_m max, encroachment_clearance_m min) in one unit. The subject is an HVAC device, which has no vocab building type or use; keyed to garden_suite as its host.

units.disclosure: Garden suite heat pumps and air conditioners may project up to 0.9 m into setbacks and separation distances (staying 0.3 m from lot lines), up to 2.0 m above the roof, and must be within 2.0 m of a wall or platform if on the ground; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: Wall-mounted equipment on a laneway suite may extend up to 0.6 m if it stays at least 0.3 m from the lot line.

calculation_handling.description: Amending By-law 1075-2026, item 33, replaces regulation 150.8.60.60(7) with the text keyed in the (7) unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Amendment instruction (replacement); the operative text is the (7) unit. "33" is the item number of the amending by-law, recorded as count_or_ordinal_not_a_limit in case it is not treated as a regulation number.

calculation_handling.description: A heating, ventilation and air conditioning device associated with a laneway suite: (A) on the laneway suite building it may encroach up to 0.9 m into a required building setback or front yard setback if no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line, may sit on the roof and exceed the building's maximum height by 2.0 m, and may be on a platform; (B) if ground mounted it may encroach up to 0.9 m into a required building setback or separation distance if no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line, and must be within 2.0 m of a main wall or platform.
calculation_handling.gaps: The unit holds several limbs; keyed as a LIMIT on encroachment_m (the 0.9 m maximum, one statement per limb that sets it). The 0.3 m lot-line distance in (A)(i), (A)(ii), (B)(i), (B)(ii) is the condition of each encroachment (it could also be read as an encroachment_clearance_m minimum; a LIMIT names one target, so it is listed as not expressed). The 2.0 m in (A)(iii) is a permitted height exceedance for rooftop devices (no DSL target for an exceedance over the height limit) and the 2.0 m in (B)(iii) is a location requirement (within 2.0 m of a main wall or platform); neither has a fitting target, threshold_used_in_application is the closest closed reason. (A)(iv) (may be located on a platform) is a permission with no literal. HVAC device placement is a design fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: Heating, ventilation and air conditioning equipment for a laneway suite may project up to 0.9 m into setbacks (staying at least 0.3 m from lot lines), may sit on the roof up to 2.0 m above the height limit, and ground-mounted units must be within 2.0 m of a wall or platform. We do not check equipment placement.

calculation_handling.description: Amending instruction (By-law 1075-2026, item 34): adds new article 150.8.75, clause 150.8.75.1 and regulation 150.8.75.1(1) to Zoning By-law 569-2013.

calculation_handling.description: The required number of parking spaces may be reduced for electric vehicle supply equipment and for support structures attached to a solar parking canopy, subject to conditions including a 0.3 metre clearance from the side of a parking space.
calculation_handling.gaps: The reduction depends on equipment layout facts we do not hold, and the 0.3 metre clearance has no matching target in our vocabulary.

units.disclosure: Required parking can be reduced where electric vehicle supply equipment or solar canopy support structures take up space, subject to conditions such as a 0.3 metre clearance from the side of a parking space. We do not model this reduction, so the parking requirement shown is not reduced.
